uses: Antiemetic, gastrokinetic for gastric emptying, dyspepsia, GERD.
side_effects: Galactorrhoea, gynaecomastia, decreased libido, skin rashes.
dosage: Acute nausea/vomiting (Adult): 10-20 mg 6-8 hours; Child: 0.25-0.5 mg/kg. Functional dyspepsia: 10-20 mg 3 times daily before food.
precautions: Avoid grapefruit juice during therapy.
contraindications: GIT obstruction, urinary outflow obstruction, paralytic ileus, comatose condition, hepatic/cardiovascular disease, glaucoma.

name: METOCLOPRAMIDE
uses: Nausea and vomiting in GI disorders or radiotherapy, GERD, gastroparesis, premedication.
side_effects: Extrapyramidal symptoms, tardive dyskinesia, hyperprolactinemia, neuroleptic malignant syndrome.
dosage: Adult: 10 mg 3 times daily; Children: 2-5 mg/kg. Aid to GI procedure: 10-20 mg as single dose.
precautions: Assess for extra-pyramidal side effects (rigidity, tremor), signs of depression.
contraindications: GI obstruction, perforation, pheochromocytoma, epilepsy, Parkinson’s, pregnancy, breast feeding.

name: ONDANSETRON
uses: Chemotherapy induced nausea and vomiting (CINV), post operative (PONV), radiation induced nausea, uremic pruritus.
side_effects: Headache, constipation, hiccups, flushing, arrhythmia, hypotension.
dosage: CINV (moderate): 8 mg 30 min prior; IV: 0.15 mg/kg. PONV: 4 mg IV/IM before anaesthesia.
precautions: Safety not established in children below 4 years.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, co-administration with apomorphine, pregnancy, breastfeeding, severe liver impairment.

name: PROCHLORPERAZINE
uses: Postoperative nausea and vomiting, chemotherapy induced nausea, vertigo, psychosis.
side_effects: Muscle dystonia, other extrapyramidal side effects, dry mouth, drowsiness.
dosage: Acute vomiting: 20 mg initially then 10 mg after 2 hours. Prevention: 5-10 mg 2-3 times daily (0.25 mg/kg).
precautions: Should be protected from light.

name: PROMETHAZINE
uses: Nausea, vomiting, motion sickness, sedation.
side_effects: Sedation, blurred vision, confusion, hallucination, extrapyramidal symptoms.
dosage: Nausea/vomiting: 12.5-25 mg 4-6 hours. Motion sickness: 25 mg 30-60 min before travel.
precautions: May cause photosensitivity; avoid prolonged exposure to sunlight.

name: DIPHENOXYLATE
uses: Acute diarrhoea, chronic mild ulcerative colitis.
side_effects: Blurred vision, sedation, nausea, abdominal discomfort, dryness of mouth.
dosage: Adult: Initial 4 tablets, then 2 tablets every 6 hours until controlled.
precautions: Monitor for pseudomembranous colitis.
contraindications: Children < 4 years, hypersensitivity, pregnancy, breast feeding, hepatic disease, ulcerative colitis.

name: LOPERAMIDE
uses: Acute nonspecific diarrhoea, chronic diarrhoea, faecal incontinence, intestinal colic pain.
side_effects: Dizziness, drowsiness, fatigue, flatulence, nausea.
dosage: Acute: 4 mg initially, then 2 mg (max 16 mg/day). Chronic: 4-8 mg daily in divided doses.
precautions: Avoid use as primary therapy in acute dysentery. Discontinue if no improvement in 48 hours.
contraindications: Active ulcerative colitis, pseudomembranous colitis, age < 2 years, bloody diarrhoea.

name: ORAL REHYDRATION SALTS
uses: Dehydration from acute diarrhoea.
side_effects: Vomiting (too rapid administration), hypernatremia, hyperkalaemia.
dosage: Adult: 200-400 ml after every loose motion. Child: 200 ml after every loose motion.
precautions: Renal impairment; protect from moisture.

name: RIFAXIMIN
uses: Traveller’s diarrhoea, hepatic encephalopathy, irritable bowel syndrome.
side_effects: Flatulence, rectal tenesmus, abdominal pain, defecation urgency, nausea.
dosage: Traveller’s: 200 mg TDS for 3 days. HE: 550 mg BD. IBS: 550 mg TDS for 14 days.
precautions: Discontinue if symptoms persist > 24-48 hours. Hepatic impairment.

name: ZINC SULFATE
uses: Adjunct to ORS in acute diarrhoea.
side_effects: Abdominal pain, dyspepsia, nausea, vomiting, gastric irritation.
dosage: Infants < 6 months: 10 mg daily for 10-14 days. Child 6 months-5 years: 20 mg daily.
precautions: Inform doctor if tarry stools or severe nausea occurs.

name: ISPAGHULA HUSK
uses: Constipation.
side_effects: Abdominal distension, flatulence.
dosage: 0.5-2 gm/day at bed time; Children: half of adult dose.
precautions: Increase fluid intake; bulk forming foods in diet.

name: DOCUSATE SODIUM
uses: Constipation, adjunct to radiological procedure.
side_effects: Rashes, transient abdominal cramping pain.
dosage: 50-300 mg per oral single or divided dose (max 500 mg).
precautions: N/A
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, intestinal obstruction, prolonged use, children.

name: LIQUID PARAFFIN
uses: Constipation.
side_effects: Lipoid pneumonia, interference with fat soluble vitamin absorption, granulomatous lesions.
dosage: 10-30 ml at night.
precautions: Avoid aspiration.

name: BISACODYL
uses: Constipation, bowel preparation for radiology/surgery.
side_effects: Abdominal cramp, local irritation.
dosage: Adult: 5-10 mg at night. Paediatric (>6 yr): 5 mg at night.
precautions: Swallow whole; do not take with antacid within 1 hour.

name: SENNA
uses: Constipation, bowel preparation.
side_effects: Abdominal cramps.
dosage: Adult: 2-4 tablets at night. Child (>6 years): half of adult dose.
precautions: Avoid except when straining.

name: LACTULOSE
uses: Constipation, hepatic encephalopathy.
side_effects: Dehydration, hypernatremia, abdominal distension, flatulence.
dosage: Adult: 15 ml twice daily. HE (Adult): 30-45 ml per oral.
precautions: Pregnancy; ensure adequate water intake.

name: MACROGOL 3350
uses: Constipation, fecal impaction.
side_effects: Diarrhoea, dehydration, indigestion, pain abdomen.
dosage: Constipation: 1 sachet in 125 ml water daily. Impaction: 8 sachets within 6 hours.
precautions: Take plenty of fluids.
contraindications: Gut obstruction/perforation, severe IBD, cardiovascular diseases.

name: MAGNESIUM HYDROXIDE (MILK OF MAGNESIA)
uses: Constipation, acid peptic disease.
side_effects: Abdominal cramp, electrolyte imbalance, hypotension.
dosage: Constipation: 30-60 ml at bed time. Acid peptic: 5-15 ml in 4 divided doses.
precautions: Shake before use; take on empty stomach.
contraindications: Renal failure, acute abdomen, undiagnosed abdominal pain.

name: MAGNESIUM SULPHATE
uses: Constipation, hypomagnesemia, eclampsia, torsades de pointes.
side_effects: Flaccid paralysis, circulatory collapse, electrolyte disturbance.
dosage: Constipation: 5-10 g dissolved in 24 ml water.
precautions: Not for long term use; do not give at bedtime.
contraindications: Renal impairment, heart block, acute surgical abdomen.

name: POLYETHYLENE GLYCOL 3350
uses: Constipation.
side_effects: Nausea, abdominal bloating, cramping, excessive stool frequency.
dosage: 17 g reconstituted in a glass of water.
precautions: Report unusual cramps or bloating.

name: ADALIMUMAB
uses: Crohn’s disease, ulcerative colitis, rheumatic and psoriatic arthritis.
side_effects: Hypersensitivity, increased serum ALT, infection.
dosage: Crohn's/UC: Initial 160 mg, then 80 mg (day 15), maintenance 40 mg every other week.
precautions: N/A

name: BUDESONIDE
uses: Mild to moderate active Crohn’s disease.
side_effects: Increased infection risk, abdominal pain, flatulence, corticosteroid effects.
dosage: Active disease: 9 mg orally daily for 8 weeks; Maintenance: 6 mg daily.
precautions: N/A

name: HYDROCORTISONE ACETATE
uses: Ulcerative colitis, proctitis, proctosigmoiditis.
side_effects: Local pain/burning, rectal bleeding.
dosage: Suppository: 25 mg twice daily for 2 weeks.
precautions: Proctoscopic examination required before treatment.

name: INFLIXIMAB
uses: Crohn’s disease, ulcerative colitis.
side_effects: Hypersensitivity, abdominal pain, infusion related reaction.
dosage: Adult: IV 5 mg/kg at 0, 2, 6 weeks, then every 8 weeks.
precautions: Risk of lymphoma in children; consider antihistamine premedication.

name: MESALAZINE
uses: Ulcerative colitis acute attack and maintenance, Crohn’s ileo-colitis.
side_effects: Dizziness, oligospermia, abdominal pain, headache.
dosage: Maintenance (Adult): 1.2-2.4 g daily. Acute (Adult): 2.4 g daily.
precautions: Empty stomach prior to rectal administration.
contraindications: Salicylate hypersensitivity, breastfeeding, active peptic ulcer, severe renal failure.

name: SULFASALAZINE
uses: Ulcerative colitis, active Crohn’s disease, rheumatoid arthritis.
side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, exacerbation of colitis, blood disorders, lung complications.
dosage: Adult (Acute): 1-2 g QID. Child (>2 yrs): 40-60 mg/kg.
precautions: G6PD deficiency, renal/hepatic impairment; ensure hydration.
contraindications: Salicylate/sulfonamide hypersensitivity, child < 2 yrs, intestinal obstruction.

name: OCTREOTIDE
uses: Esophageal variceal bleeding, acromegaly, carcinoid tumor.
side_effects: N/A
dosage: Variceal bleeding: 50 mcg IV bolus, then 25-50 mcg/hr for 1-5 days.
precautions: N/A

name: TERLIPRESSIN
uses: Bleeding from esophageal varices.
side_effects: Abdominal cramps, headache, cardiac arrhythmias.
dosage: Initially 2 mg every 4-6 hours until controlled, then 1 mg up to 48 hours.
precautions: Use in pregnancy only if clearly needed.
contraindications: Seizure, migraine, asthma, heart failure, renal disease.

name: URSODEOXYCHOLIC ACID
uses: Dissolution of gallstones, primary biliary cirrhosis.
side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, pruritus.
dosage: Gallstones: 8-12 mg/kg daily. Cirrhosis: 10-15 mg/kg daily.
precautions: Avoid aluminium antacids; pregnant and lactating mothers.

name: PROBIOTICS
uses: Infective diarrhoea, antibiotic associated diarrhoea, traveller’s diarrhoea risk.
side_effects: Infection, acidosis (rare).
dosage: Typical dosage: 1-10 billion cells divided into 3 or 4 doses.
precautions: N/A

name: GLYCERYL TRINATRE (NITROGLYCERINE)
uses: Prophylaxis and acute attack of angina pectoris, Hypertensive emergencies, acute decompensated heart failure
side_effects: Throbbing headache (most frequent in early therapy), flushing, dizziness, postural hypotension, Tachycardia, syncope, paradoxical bradycardia
dosage: Angina (acute attack): Intravenous infusion, adult: initially 5–10 mcg/min. The rate may be increased by 10 mcg/min every 3–5 min until symptoms relieved, systolic arterial pressure falls to <100 mm Hg, or dose reaches 200 mcg/min. Hypertensive emergencies: Intravenous infusion, adult: 5-10 mcg/min initial dose up to 200 mcg/min. Acute decompensated heart failure: Intravenous infusion, adult: 10–20 mcg/min, increase up to 200 mcg/min; Children: Initially 0.25- 0.5 mcg/kg/min to titrate to 0.5-1.0 mcg/kg/min. Maximum dose 20 mcg/kg/min.
precautions: Use caution in severe hepatic impairment, hypothyroidism, malnutrition, hypothermia, recent history of myocardial infarction. Renal impairment (10-50 ml/min): never administer. Uninterrupted infusion > 24 hours produces tolerance.
contraindications: Avoid in hypersensitivity to nitrates, hypotension, hypovolemia, hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy, aortic stenosis, cardiac tamponade, constrictive pericarditis, mitral stenosis, marked anemia, head trauma, cerebral hemorrhage, angle-closure glaucoma.

name: ISOSORBIDE DINITRATE
uses: Prophylaxis and treatment of angina, left ventricular failure.
side_effects: See under glyceryl trinitrate, tolerance (in long term, uninterrupted use)
dosage: Angina (acute attack): Sublingual, adult: 5–10 mg repeated as required. Angina (prophylaxis): Oral, adult: 30-120 mg daily in divided doses. Intravenous infusion: 2-10 mg daily, maximum dose 20 mg/hour. Left ventricular failure: Oral, adult 40-160 mg daily in divided doses, maximum dose 240 mg daily; Intravenous infusion: 2-10 mg daily, maximum dose 20 mg/hour.
precautions: See under glyceryl trinitrate. Patients may develop tolerance; avoid by giving the second of 2 daily doses of longer-acting oral preparations after an 8-hour rather than a 12-hour interval.

name: ISOSOBIDE MONONITRATES
uses: Prophylaxis of angina pectoris, adjunct in congestive heart failure.
side_effects: See under glyceryl trinitrate
dosage: Prophylaxis for angina: Oral (immediate release), adult: initially 20 mg 2-3 times daily or 40 mg twice daily or 10 mg twice daily (in those who have not previously received nitrates) maximum dose 120 mg in 2-3 divided doses daily.
precautions: See under glyceryl trinitrate

name: ATENOLOL
uses: Chronic stable angina, secondary prevention after myocardial infarction, supra ventricular arrhythmia, mild CHF, hypertension, migraine prophylaxis.
side_effects: Bradycardia, gastrointestinal disturbances including nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, abdominal cramp, fatigue, cold hands and feet, hypertriglyceridemia.
dosage: Hypertension: Oral, adult: 25 – 50 mg daily. Oral, child: 0.5-1.0 mg/kg/dose in 1-2 divided doses daily. Maximum dose- 2mg/kg/day or 100 mg/day. Angina: Oral, adult: 100 mg, maximum dose 200 mg daily 1 or 2 doses. Arrhythmias: Oral, adult: 50-100 mg daily. Intravenous, adult: 2.5 mg at rate of 1 mg/min repeated at 5 min interval to a maximum of 10 mg/dose. Early intervention Myocardial infarction: slow intravenous infusion, adult: 5 mg by then oral 50 mg after 15 minutes then oral 50 mg after 12 hours then 100 mg daily. Migraine prophylaxis: Oral, adult: 50–200 mg daily in divided doses.
precautions: Use caution in patients with first –degree atrioventricular block, portal hypertension, renal impairment (reduce dose), diabetes mellitus. Pregnancy- avoid (IUGR, neonatal hypoglycemia and bradycardia). Breast feeding: avoid. Monitor lung function. Symptoms of hypoglycemia and thyrotoxicosis may get masked.
contraindications: Avoid in history of asthma or bronchospasm, uncontrolled heart failure, prinzemetal angina, bradycardia (heart rate <50 bpm), hypotension, sick sinus syndrome, second and third degree atrioventricular block, cardiogenic shock, metabolic acidosis, severe peripheral arterial disease, pheochromocytoma (unless used with an alpha blocker).

name: BISOPROLOL
uses: Hypertension, angina, adjunct in heart failure
side_effects: See under atenolol
dosage: Hypertension and angina: Oral, adult: 5-10 mg once daily, 20 mg daily (maximum). Adjunct in heart failure: Oral, adult: initially 1.25 mg once daily (in the morning) for 1 week then, if well tolerated, increased to 2.5 mg once daily for 1 week, then 3.75 mg once daily for 1 week, then 5 mg once daily for 4 weeks, then 7.5 mg once daily for 4 weeks, then 10 mg once daily, maximum 10 mg daily.
precautions: See under atenolol

name: CARVEDILOL
uses: Angina, hypertension, adjunct to diuretics/digoxin/ACE inhibitors in heart failure
side_effects: Allergic skin reactions, angina, AV block, changes in liver enzymes, depressed mood, disturbances of micturition, influenza-like symptoms, leucopenia, nasal stuffiness, postural hypotension, thrombocytopenia, wheezing, headache, dizziness, bradycardia and impotence
dosage: Hypertension: Oral, adult: Initially 12.5 mg once daily for 2 days, then increased to 25 mg once daily; increased if necessary up to 50 mg daily. Angina: Oral, adult: initially 12.5 mg once daily, increased after 2 days to 25 mg twice daily. Adjunct in heart failure: Oral, adult: initially 3.125 mg twice daily to 6.25 mg twice daily, then to 12.5 mg twice daily then to 25 mg twice daily. Dose increased at intervals of at least 2 weeks
precautions: See under atenolol. Check for edema in feet, legs daily. Rise slowly from sitting or lying position to minimize orthostatic hypotension
contraindications: See under atenolol. Avoid in acute decompensated heart failure requiring intravenous inotropes.

name: METOPROLOL
uses: Angina, hypertension, arrhythmias, migraine prophylaxis, hyperthyroidism adjunct, early intervention in myocardial infarction.
side_effects: See under atenolol
dosage: Angina: Oral, adult: 50- 100 mg, 2-3 times daily. Hypertension: Oral, adult: initially 100 mg daily, maximum dose 400 mg daily. Arrhythmias: Oral, adult: 50-100 mg, 2-3 times daily; Intravenous, adult: up to 5 mg at rate 1-2 mg/minute repeated after 5 minutes if necessary, total dose 10-15 mg. Early intervention in myocardial infarction: Intravenous, adult: 5 mg every 2 minutes to a maximum dose of 15 mg, followed after 15 minutes by oral 50 mg every 6 hours for 48 hours; maintenance oral 200 mg daily. Hyperthyroidism (adjunct): Oral, adult: 50 mg 4 times a day. Oral, child: 1-2 mg/kg/day in 2 divided doses daily. Maximum dose 6 mg/kg/day up to 200 mg/day.
precautions: See under atenolol. Abrupt withdrawal may cause MI, ventricular arrhythmias, myocardial ischemia; taper dose over 7-14 days.

name: PROPRANOLOL
uses: Chronic stable angina, hypertension, secondary prevention after acute myocardial infraction, anxiety, thyrotoxicosis, migraine prophylaxis, pheochromocytoma (only with alpha blocker), prophylaxis of variceal bleeding, mitral valve prolapse, essential tremor, child with cyanotic spells.
side_effects: See under atenolol. Hallucination, nightmare, sexual dysfunction.
dosage: Hypertension: Oral, adult: initially 80 mg twice daily; maintenance dose 160-320 mg daily. Oral, child: 1-4 mg/kg/day in 3-4 divided doses. Prophylaxis of variceal bleeding: Oral, adult: initially 40 mg twice daily increased to 80 mg twice daily. Angina: Oral, adult: initially 40 mg 2-3 time daily; maintenance 120-240 mg daily. Arrhythmias: Oral, adult: 10-40 mg in 3-4 divided doses daily. Anxiety: Oral, adult: 40 mg once daily; may increase to 40 mg 3 times daily. Essential tremor: Oral, adult: initially 40 mg 2-3 times daily; maintenance 80-160 mg daily. Cyanotic spells: Child, intravenous: 0.15-0.25 mg/kg/day in 4 divided dose; Oral, child: 2-4 mg/kg/day in 4 divided doses. Infantile hemangioma: Oral, child: 1-2 mg/kg/day in 3 divided doses.
precautions: See under atenolol. Reduce oral dose in renal and hepatic impairment. Monitor blood glucose. Do not discontinue abruptly.

name: DILTIAZEM
uses: Angina pectoris
side_effects: Asthenia, AV block, bradycardia, dizziness, gastro-intestinal disturbances, headache, hot flushes, hypotension, malaise, edema, palpitation, Sino-atrial block
dosage: Angina: Oral, adult: Initially 60 mg 3 times a day, adjusted according to response; maximum 360 mg/day. Elderly: Initially 60 mg twice daily. Oral, child: 1.5-2 mg/kg/day in 3-4 divided doses (maximum dose: < 6mg/kg/day up to 360 mg/day).
precautions: Avoid if bradycardia is severe. Hepatic impairment: reduce dose. Renal impairment: start with smaller dose.
contraindications: Avoid in acute porphyria, left ventricular failure with pulmonary congestion, second- or third-degree AV block (unless pacemaker fitted), severe bradycardia, sick sinus syndrome.

name: VERAPAMIL
uses: Angina pectoris, supra ventricular arrhythmias, hypertension, migraine prophylaxis, supraventricular tachycardia in children
side_effects: Constipation; nausea, vomiting, flushing, headache, dizziness, fatigue, ankle edema; rarely allergic reactions; myalgia, arthralgia; increased prolactin; gynecomastia and gingival hyperplasia; hypotension, heart failure, bradycardia, heart block, and asystole.
dosage: Angina, supraventricular arrhythmia: Oral, adult: 40-120 mg 3 times daily. Hypertension: Oral, adult: 240-480 mg daily in 2- 3 divided doses. Hypertensive emergency: Slow intravenous injection over 2 minutes, 5 - 10 mg. Paroxysmal tachyarrhythmia: slow intravenous injection, adult: initially 5-10 mg further 5 mg after 5-10 minutes if required. Supraventricular tachycardia: Child, intravenous: 0.1-0.3 mg/kg/dose may be repeated in 30 min. Maximum first dose 5 mg, second dose 10 mg.
precautions: Hepatic impairment; children (specialist advice only). Not to discontinue abruptly. Avoid use in neonate and young infants.
contraindications: Hypotension, bradycardia, second- and third-degree heart block, sick sinus syndrome; cardiogenic shock, history of heart failure, atrial flutter or fibrillation complicating Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome, acute porphyria. Avoid if ventricular failure present.

name: ADENOSINE
uses: Paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia (including Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome)
side_effects: Chest pain, transient facial flush, bronchospasm, nausea and severe bradycardia, difficult or labored breathing, chest tightness
dosage: Rapid intravenous injection: 3 mg over 2 seconds; if necessary followed by 6 mg after 1-2 minutes and then by 12 mg after a further 1-2 minutes. Neonate, intravenous: 0.05 mg/kg over 1-2 sec; maximum dose 0.25 mg/kg. Child, intravenous: 0.1-0.2 mg/kg (initial max 6 mg) over 1-2 sec; maximum of 0.25 mg/kg.
precautions: Use cautiously in arterial fibrillation or flutter and heart transplant. Assess cardiopulmonary and respiratory status.
contraindications: Pre-existing second or third degree AV block, asthma and sick sinus syndrome.

name: AMIODARONE
uses: Paroxysmal supraventricular, nodal and ventricular tachycardia, atrial fibrillation or flutter, ventricular arrhythmia, ventricular fibrillation.
side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, raised serum transaminases, bradycardia, ventricular arrhythmia, neurologic dysfunction (dizziness, tremor), thyroid dysfunction, pulmonary toxicity on long term use.
dosage: Arrhythmias: Oral, adult: 200 mg 3 times daily for 1 week reduced to 200 mg twice daily. Ventricular fibrillation: intravenous infusion, adult: 300 mg over at least 3 minutes. Drug resistant refractory cardiac arrhythmia: Oral, child: < 1 year: 600-800 mg/1.73m2/day in 1-2 divided dose for 1-14 days. > 1 years: 10-15 mg/kg/day in 1-2 divided doses for 14 days. Child, intravenous: 5 mg/kg over 30 min followed by continuous infusion at rate of 5 mcg/kg/min (Max: 15-20 mcg/kg/min).
precautions: Pregnancy: risk of neonatal goiter. Breast feeding: avoid. Clinical monitoring of serum potassium, chest X-ray, pulmonary function tests, liver and thyroid function tests recommended.
contraindications: Avoid in sinus bradycardia, SA heart block, Iodine sensitivity, cardiogenic shock, second or third degree AV block, thyroid dysfunctions, severe hepatic, pneumonitis, pulmonary fibrosis, hypokalemia, CHF (with inadequate compensation).

name: DIGOXIN
uses: Supraventricular arrhythmias, particularly atrial fibrillation; heart failure
side_effects: GI disturbances (anorexia, nausea, vomiting), visual disturbances, headache, fatigue, drowsiness, confusion, dizziness, all arrhythmias except Mobitz type II block; rarely rash; gynecomastia; thrombocytopenia.
dosage: Atrial fibrillation: Oral, adult: initially 1–1.5 mg in divided doses over 24 hours followed by 62.5–500 mcg daily. Emergency control: intravenous infusion over at least 2 hours, adult: 0.75–1 mg. Pediatric (mcg/kg/day): Premature neonate 20 (Total daily PO), 15 (IV/IM); Full Term 30 (PO), 20 (IV/IM); 1 month-2 years 40-50 (PO), 30-40 (IV/IM); 2-10 years 30-40 (PO), 20-30 (IV/IM); >10 years 10-15 (PO), 8-12 (IV/IM). Initially, half the total daily dose, then other half every 8 hours in 2 divided doses.
precautions: Use caution in recent MI, sick sinus syndrome, renal impairment. Monitor apical pulse; withhold if rate is <60 bpm (adult), <70 bpm (child), <90 bpm (infant). Therapeutic drug monitoring advised.
contraindications: Avoid in hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy; Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome; ventricular tachycardia or fibrillation; intermittent complete heart block; second-degree AV block.

name: DISOPYRAMIDE
uses: Atrial and ventricular arrhythmias including those resistant to lignocaine.
side_effects: Angle-closure glaucoma, antimuscarinic effects, AV block, blurred vision, cholestatic jaundice, dry mouth, hypoglycemia, hypotension, myocardial depression, psychosis, urinary retention, ventricular tachycardia, torsade de pointes.
dosage: Oral (immediate release), adult: 300-800 mg daily in divided doses. Slow intravenous injection, adult: 2 mg/kg over at least 5 minutes to a maximum of 150 mg with ECG monitoring.
precautions: Use caution in the elderly and children. Do not drive or operate machinery. Do not stop the drug suddenly.
contraindications: Avoid in preexisting second or third degree AV block, cardiogenic shock, heart failure (can produce severe hypotension). Renal or hepatic insufficiency, third trimester of pregnancy, glaucoma, myasthenia gravis or urinary retention.

name: ISOPRENALINE
uses: Torsade de pointes, bradycardia in patients with heart block, control attacks of Stokes Adam syndrome.
side_effects: Tachycardia, hypotension, arrhythmia, tremor, sweating
dosage: Intravenous injection, adult: 0.5-10 mcg/minute. Oral, adult: initially 30 mg every 6 hours, range, 90-840 mg daily (rarely used).
precautions: N/A

name: LIDOCAINE/ LIGNOCAINE
uses: Ventricular arrhythmias (especially after myocardial infarction), local anesthesia
side_effects: Flushing, dizziness, paresthesia, drowsiness, confusion, apnea, respiratory depression, coma, seizure, hypotension, arrhythmia, heart block, bradycardia (may lead to cardiac arrest), nystagmus.
dosage: Ventricular arrhythmias: intravenous injection, adult: loading dose of 50-100 mg at rate 25-50 mg/minute, followed immediately by infusion 1-4 mg/minute. Intravenous, child: 1 mg/kg/dose slow IV, may repeat 10-15 min. Max total dose: 3-5 mg/kg within first hour.
precautions: Lower dosage in CHF, cardiac surgery, bradycardia, hepatic impairment. Pregnancy and breastfeeding. Monitor for ECG.
contraindications: Avoid in Sino atrial nodal disorder, any grade of atrioventricular block, severe myocardial depression, acute porphyria, hypovolemia, Wolff-Parkinson-White, Stokes Adams syndrome.

name: PROCAINAMIDE
uses: Severe ventricular arrhythmias; atrial tachycardia, atrial fibrillation; maintenance of sinus rhythm after cardioversion.
side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, rash, pruritus, fever, myocardial depression, heart failure, angioedema, dizziness, psychosis; leukopenia, hemolytic anemia, agranulocytosis, SLE like syndrome.
dosage: Oral, adult: up to 50 mg/kg daily in divided doses every 3-6 hours. Slow intravenous injection, adult: rate not exceeding 50 mg/minute, 100 mg repeated at 5 minute intervals until controlled; maximum 1g. Intravenous infusion, adult: 500-600 mg over 25-30 minutes, maintenance 2-6 mg/minute.
precautions: Discontinue if leukocyte/platelet count drops. Perform CBC twice a week for 3 months. Monitor continuously by ECG during IV use.
contraindications: Avoid in Torsade’s de pointes, SLE, 2nd and 3rd degree heart block, heart failure, hypotension, elderly, renal/hepatic impairment, asthma, myasthenia gravis, pregnancy, breastfeeding, electrolyte imbalance.

name: CAPTOPRIL
uses: Mild to moderate essential hypertension, adjunctive treatment in congestive heart failure, severe hypertension resistant to other treatment, following myocardial infraction, diabetic nephropathy.
side_effects: alopecia, rash, profound hypotension, dehydration, taste impairment, leucopenia, proteinuria, persistent dry cough, sleep disorder, dyspnea, neutropenia, Raynaud’s syndrome.
dosage: Hypertension: Oral, adult: initially 5 mg once daily; usual maintenance 20 mg once daily; maximum 40 mg once daily. Take 1-2 hours after meals.
precautions: Use caution in severe aortic stenosis. Monitor renal function. Rise slowly to minimize orthostatic hypotension. Not to discontinue product abruptly.
contraindications: Avoid in bilateral renal artery stenosis, pregnancy, hyperkalemia, pre-existing cough.

name: ENALAPRIL
uses: Hypertension, heart failure
side_effects: Dizziness, headache, nausea, diarrhea, dry cough, fatigue, asthenia, angioedema, urticaria, rashes, hyperkalemia, impaired perspiration
dosage: Hypertension: Oral, adult: 5 mg once daily (2.5 mg daily initially if on diuretic or renal impairment); maintenance 20 mg once daily: maximum 40 mg once daily. Oral, child: 0.1- 0.6 mg/kg/day in 1-2 divided doses. Maximum dose 40 mg/day.
precautions: Use cautious in impaired liver function and neonates. Monitor renal function.
contraindications: See under captopril. Avoid in renal impairment when GFR < 30 ml/1.73m2/min.

name: LISINOPRIL
uses: Essential and renovascular hypertension, adjunctive treatment in congestive heart failure, following myocardial infarction, diabetic nephropathy.
side_effects: Profound hypotension, hyperkalemia, rash, tachycardia, myocardial infarction, sweating, impotence, dizziness, upper respiratory tract infection, fatigue, diarrhea.
dosage: Hypertension: initially 10 mg daily (2.5-5 mg if renal impairment); usual maintenance 20 mg once daily (max 80 mg). Heart failure (adjunct): Oral, adult: initially 2.5 mg daily; usual maintenance 5-20 mg daily. Diabetic nephropathy: Oral, adult: initially 2.5 mg daily; usual range 10-20 mg daily. Prophylaxis after MI: Oral, adult: 5 mg within 24 hours, followed by 5 mg 24 hours later, then 10 mg after a further 24 hours, and continuing with 10 mg once daily for 6 weeks.
precautions: Drink plenty of water. Avoid potassium rich diet.
contraindications: Avoid in pregnancy, hereditary angioedema, breast-feeding. See under captopril.

name: RAMIPRIL
uses: Hypertension, congestive heart failure, prophylaxis after myocardial infarction, prophylaxis of cardiovascular events or stroke.
side_effects: See under Enalapril
dosage: Hypertension: Oral, adult: initially 1.25 mg once daily; usual range 2.5-5 mg once daily; maximum 10 mg once daily. CHF (adjunct): Oral, adult: initially 1.25 mg once daily; maximum 10 mg daily. Prophylaxis after MI: Oral, adult: initially 2.5 mg twice daily, increased to 5 mg twice daily; maintenance 2.5-5 mg twice daily. Prophylaxis of stroke: initially 2.5 mg once daily, increased up to 10 mg once daily.
precautions: N/A

name: IRBESARTAN
uses: Hypertension, hypertension in patients receiving hemodialysis, renal disease in hypertensive with type 2 diabetes mellitus
side_effects: Fatigue, musculoskeletal pain, nausea, vomiting
dosage: Hypertension: Oral, adult (18–74 years): Initially 150 mg once daily, increased to 300 mg once daily. Oral, adult (>75 years): Initially 75–150 mg once daily, increased to 300 mg. Hemodialysis: Oral, adult: Initially 75–150 mg once daily. Type 2 diabetes renal disease: Oral, adult (18–74 years): Initially 150 mg once daily, increased to 300 mg once daily.
precautions: N/A
contraindications: Avoid in renal artery stenosis, moderate to severe renal impairment or liver impairment, aortic or mitral valve stenosis.

name: LOSARTAN
uses: Hypertension, congestive heart failure, diabetic nephropathy in type 2 diabetes mellitus
side_effects: Hypotension, dizziness, diarrhea, pruritus, rash, taste disturbance, thrombocytopenia, photosensitivity
dosage: Hypertension: Oral, adult: 50 mg (elderly >75 years: 25 mg) once daily; increase up to 150 mg. Oral, Child: 0.75 mg/kg/dose once daily (Max 50 mg/day). Maximum dose: 1.4 mg/kg/day or 100 mg/day. Diabetic nephropathy: Oral, adult: initially 50 mg (elderly >75 years: 25 mg) once daily, increase up to 100 mg. CHF: Oral, adult: Initially 12.5 mg once daily, increase to 150 mg once daily.
precautions: Use caution in moderate to severe renal/liver impairment, aortic or mitral valve stenosis. Rise slowly to minimize orthostatic hypotension.
contraindications: Avoid in pregnancy and breast feeding, children of 6 years or younger, CHF, renal impairment (GFR < 30 ml/min/1.73m2), renal artery stenosis.

name: TELMISARTAN
uses: Hypertension, prevention of cardiovascular events in patients with established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease or type 2 diabetes mellitus with target-organ damage.
side_effects: Arthralgia, back pain, chest pain, eczema, gastro-intestinal disturbances, influenza like symptoms, leg cramps, myalgia, pharyngitis, sinusitis, urinary-tract infection, abnormal vision, anxiety, dry mouth, sweating, tendonitis, vertigo
dosage: Hypertension: Oral, adult: Initially 20–40 mg once daily, increased if necessary up to 80 mg once daily. Prevention of CV events: Oral, adult: 80 mg once daily. Severe renal impairment: Oral, adult: Initial dose of 20 mg once daily.
precautions: N/A
contraindications: Avoid in bilateral renal artery stenosis, pregnancy and breast feeding, in severe impairment or biliary obstruction.

name: VALSARTAN
uses: Hypertension, myocardial infarction with left ventricular failure or left ventricular systolic dysfunction.
side_effects: See under losartan.
dosage: Hypertension: Oral, adult: 80 mg once daily (initially 40 mg if intravascular volume depletion); increased up to 160 mg daily. Myocardial infarction: Oral, adult: initially 20 mg twice daily increased up to 160 mg twice daily. Mild to moderate hepatic impairment: maximum dose of 80 mg daily.
precautions: Use caution in mild to moderate renal and hepatic impairment. Take medicine before meal.
contraindications: See under Losartan. Avoid in biliary cirrhosis, cholestasis, severe hepatic impairment, renal impairment when eGFR <10 ml/min/ 1.73m2.

name: LABETALOL
uses: Hypertension, Hypertensive emergencies, hypertension following myocardial infarction, hypertension of pregnancy
side_effects: Difficulty in micturition, epigastric pain, liver damage, nausea, postural hypotension, vomiting, weakness, severe hepatocellular injury
dosage: Hypertension: Oral, adult: Initially 100 mg (50 mg for elderly) twice daily; usual dose 200 mg twice daily; maximum 2.4 g per day. Hypertensive emergencies: Intravenous injection: adult: 50 mg over 1 minute; maximum 200 mg. Intravenous infusion: adult: Initially 2 mg/minute; usual dose 50–200 mg. Pregnancy Hypertension: Intravenous infusion: Initially 20 mg/hour, increased to 160 mg/hour. Oral, child: 4 mg/kg/day in 2 divided doses. Max 40 mg/kg/day. Hypertensive emergency: Child, IV: 0.2-1.0 mg/kg/dose every 10 min. Max 20 mg/dose.
precautions: Pregnancy: possibly harmful in first trimester. Monitor infants for signs of alpha-blockade. Stop if laboratory evidence of liver damage or jaundice occurs. Take medicine after food.
contraindications: See under contraindication in Atenolol. Avoid in severe liver damage. Hepatic impairment: avoid as reported. Renal impairment: Dose reduction may be required.

name: NEBIVOLOL
uses: Essential hypertension, hypertension in patient with renal impairment, adjunct in stable mild to moderate heart failure
side_effects: See under adverse effect Atenolol. Depression, edema.
dosage: Essential hypertension: Oral, adult: 5 mg daily; elderly: Initially 2.5 mg daily. Hypertension with renal impairment: Oral, adult: Initially 2.5 mg once daily. Adjunct in heart failure: Oral, elderly (≥ 70 years): Initially 1.25 mg once daily for 1–2 weeks, then increased up to 10 mg once daily.
precautions: Breast feeding: avoid.
contraindications: See under contraindication Atenolol. Avoid in acute or decompensated heart failure requiring intravenous inotropes, severe hepatic impairment. Renal impairment: avoid in heart failure if serum creatinine > 250 micromole/liter.

name: AMLODIPINE
uses: Hypertension, angina pectoris
side_effects: Abdominal pain, nausea, flushing, edema (ankle edema), headache, dizziness, sleep disturbances, fatigue, alopecia, arthralgia, asthenia, back pain, dry mouth, dyspnea, impotence, gynecomastia, myalgia, muscle cramp, skin discoloration.
dosage: Hypertension or angina: Oral, adult: initially 5 mg once daily; maximum dose 10 mg once daily. Oral, child: 0.1-0.6 mg/kg/day in 1-2 divided doses. Maximum dose: 20 mg/day.
precautions: In hepatic impairment: dose reduction. Try to avoid large amount of alcohol.
contraindications: Cardiogenic shock, unstable angina, significant aortic stenosis. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: avoid.

name: FELODIPINE
uses: Angina, hypertension
side_effects: flushing, headache, peripheral edema.
dosage: Angina: Oral, adult: 5 mg/day, maximum dose 10 mg/day. Oral, elderly: 2.5 mg/day. Hypertension: initially 5 mg (elderly 2.5 mg) daily in the morning; usual maintenance 5-10 mg once daily.
precautions: Withdraw if cardiogenic shock develops. In hepatic impairment, reduce dose.
contraindications: Avoid in Cardiac outflow obstruction, aortic stenosis uncontrolled heart failure, unstable angina, within 1 month of myocardial infarction. Pregnancy- avoid.

name: NIFEDIPINE
uses: prophylaxis of angina, hypertension, Raynaud’s phenomenon, pulmonary hypertension.
side_effects: dizziness, giddiness, flushing, light headedness, peripheral edema and palpitation.
dosage: Hypertension and angina prophylaxis: Oral, adult: 20 mg twice daily. Usual maintenance 10-40 mg twice daily. Raynaud’s: Oral, adult: initially 5 mg 3 times daily. Pulmonary hypertension: Oral, adult: 120 to 240 mg once daily. Hypertension: Child, sublingual: 0.25-0.5 mg/kg/dose. Maximum 10 mg/dose.
precautions: In patients with angina, the drug may cause increased angina. To be taken with or after food.
contraindications: Avoid in congestive heart failure or aortic stenosis, especially in those receiving concomitant beta blocking agents.

name: CLONIDINE
uses: Hypertension, prevention of recurrent migraine, prevention of vascular headache, treatment for acute withdrawal in opioid dependent patients.
side_effects: Constipation, depression, dizziness, drowsiness, dry mouth, headache, malaise, nausea, postural hypotension, salivary gland pain, sexual dysfunction, sleep disturbances, vomiting. Bradycardia, delusion, hallucination.
dosage: Hypertension: Oral, adult: Initially 50–100 mcg 3 times a day, usual maximum 1.2 mg daily. Migraine/Vascular headache: Oral, adult: Initially 50 mcg twice daily for 2 weeks, then 75 mcg twice daily. Opioid withdrawal: Oral, adult: 0.1-0.3 mg every 4-6 hours; maximum 2.4 mg/day.
precautions: Withdraw gradually to avoid rebound hypertension. Pregnancy: use caution. Breast feeding: avoid. Renal impairment: reduce initial dose. Drowsiness may affect driving.
contraindications: Avoid in severe bradyarrhythmia secondary to second- or third-degree AV block or sick sinus syndrome.

name: HYDRALAZINE HYDROCHLORIDE
uses: Moderate and severe hypertension (adjunct), hypertensive emergencies in pregnant (not a first line agent), hypertension with renal complication and children
side_effects: Tachycardia, palpitation, hypotension, nausea, vomiting, SLE-like syndrome, weight gain and headache, muscle weakness, cramps, dizziness.
dosage: Mild or moderate hypertension: Oral, adult: 25 mg twice daily, increased to maximum 50 mg twice daily. Hypertensive emergencies: intravenous infusion, adult: initially 200-300 mcg/minute, maintenance 50-150 mcg/minute. Slow intravenous injection, adult: 5-10 mg diluted. Hypertension: Oral, child: 0.75-1.0 mg/kg/day in 2-4 divided doses. Maximum dose: 25 mg/dose. Hypertensive crisis: Child, IV/IM: 0.1-0.2 mg/kg/dose every 4-6 hours. Max 20 mg/dose.
precautions: Use caution in hepatic/renal impairment, coronary artery disease, pregnancy, elderly. Perform CBC and LE cell preparation during therapy. Monitor blood glucose in diabetics.
contraindications: Avoid in severe tachycardia, high output heart failure, myocardial insufficiency due to mechanical obstruction, corpulmonale, dissecting aortic aneurysm, porphyria, SLE.

name: METHYLDOPA
uses: Hypertension, hypertension in pregnancy
side_effects: Sedation, dryness of mouth, decreased libido, parkinsonian signs, hyperprolactinemia, gynecomastia, hepatitis, hepatotoxicity, hemolytic anemia, leucopenia, lupus like syndrome, myocarditis, pancreatitis, malabsorbtion, diarrhea, Bell’s palsy, bone marrow depression.
dosage: Hypertension: Oral, adult: 250 mg, 2-3 times a day. Maximum 3 g daily. Oral, elderly: initially 125 mg twice daily, max 2 g daily.
precautions: Use cautiously in history of liver disease and renal impairment. Screening for hepatotoxicity at 3 weeks then 3 months. Protect medication from light.
contraindications: Avoid in acute porphyria, depression, pheochromocytoma.

name: PRAZOSIN
uses: Hypertension, benign prostatic hyperplasia.
side_effects: Postural hypotension, dizziness, headache, palpitation, nervousness, drowsiness, priapism, blurred vision, depression, dry mouth, dyspnea, gastrointestinal disturbances, edema, syncope, urinary frequency, vertigo, weakness.
dosage: Hypertension: Oral, adult: 500 mcg 2-3 times daily for 3-7 days, then increased up to maximum 20 mg daily. Benign prostatic hyperplasia: Oral, adult: Initially 500 mcg twice daily, maintenance 2 mg twice daily.
precautions: Use caution in cataract surgery, elderly, renal or hepatic impairment. Breast feeding: use caution. Take first dose at bedtime; do not drive for 4 hr. after first dose.
contraindications: Avoid in history of micturition syncope and postural hypotension, congestive heart failure due to mechanical obstruction.

name: SODIUM NITROPRUSSIDE
uses: Hypertensive crisis, controlled hypotension in anesthesia, acute or chronic heart failure.
side_effects: severe hypotension; headache, dizziness; retrosternal discomfort, nausea, retching, abdominal pain; perspiration; palpitations, anxiety, reduced platelet count, acute transient phlebitis.
dosage: Hypertensive crisis: Intravenous infusion, adult: initially 0.5–1.5 mcg/kg/minute, increased to 0.5–6 mcg/kg/minute; maximum, 8 mcg/kg/minute. Heart failure: 10- 15 mcg /minute, usual range 10-200 mcg/minute.
precautions: Elderly, hyponatremia, hypothermia, hypothyroidism, renal impairment, ischemic heart disease. Monitor blood pressure and blood cyanide/thiocyanate concentration. Avoid sudden withdrawal.
contraindications: Severe hepatic impairment, compensatory hypertension, severe vitamin B12 deficiency, Leber optic atrophy.

name: TAMSULOSIN
uses: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
side_effects: Postural hypotension, dizziness, headache, palpitation, drowsiness, priapism, pruritus, angioedema, asthenia, blurred vision, rash, rhinitis, tachycardia, depression, intraoperative floppy iris syndrome.
dosage: Oral, adult: 400 mcg daily as once daily.
precautions: Use caution if eGFR <10 ml/min/1.73m2. Do not drive or use machinery until sure of alertness. Not to crush, break, or chew.
contraindications: Avoid in micturition syncope, postural hypotension, severe liver impairment.

name: TERAZOSIN
uses: Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), mild to moderate hypertension
side_effects: Postural hypotension and syncope, dizziness, drowsiness, dry mouth, chest pain, pedal edema, palpitation, headache, priapism, thrombocytopenia, decreased libido, erectile disorders, weight gain, dyspnea, Angioedema, pain in extremities, blurred vision
dosage: Hypertension: Oral, adult: Initially 1 mg once daily at bedtime, usual maintenance dose 2-10 mg. BPH: Oral, adult: Initially 1 mg orally once daily. Maintenance 5–10 mg daily; maximum 10 mg per day.
precautions: See under Prazosin

name: PHENYLEPHRINE
uses: Acute hypotension, Priapism
side_effects: Arrhythmias, hypertension, palpitation, tachycardia, angle-closure glaucoma, anorexia, anxiety, bradycardia, confusion, dyspnea, headache, hypoxia, insomnia, nausea, peripheral ischemia, psychosis, tremor, urinary retention, vomiting, weakness
dosage: Acute hypotension: subcutaneous/intramuscular injection, adult: Initially 2–5 mg, followed by 1–10 mg. Slow intravenous injection: 100–500 mcg. Intravenous infusion: Initially up to 180 mcg/minute, reduced to 30–60 mcg/min. Priapism: Intracavernosal injection, adult: 100–200 mcg every 5–10 minutes; maximum 1 mg per course.
precautions: N/A
contraindications: Avoid in hypertension, severe hyperthyroidism. Pregnancy: avoid

name: DOBUTAMINE
uses: Inotropic support in infarction, cardiac surgery, septic shock, cardiogenic shock and during positive end expiratory pressure ventilation.
side_effects: Tachycardia, increase in systolic blood pressure, phlebitis. Extravasation causes tissue necrosis
dosage: Intravenous infusion, adult: 2.5-10 mcg/kg/minute, alternatively 0.5-40 mcg/kg/min
precautions: Use caution in severe hypotension, complicating cardiogenic shock, heart failure. Extravasation causes tissue necrosis. Do not mix with sodium bicarbonate or furosemide.

name: DOPAMINE
uses: Cardiogenic shock including in myocardial infarction and cardiac surgery.
side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, peripheral vasoconstriction; hypotension, tachycardia, ectopic beats, palpitations, anginal pain; headache, dyspnea; hypertension in over dosage. Extravasation causes tissue necrosis.
dosage: Cardiogenic shock: intravenous infusion, adult: initially 2–5 mcg/kg/minute into a large vein, gradually increased by 5-10 mcg/kg/minute; up to 20–50 mcg/kg/minute in seriously ill patients.
precautions: Correct hypovolemia, hypoxia, hypercapnia, and metabolic acidosis before starting treatment. Pregnancy: use only if potential benefit outweighs risk. Protect from light.
contraindications: Avoid in tachyarrhythmia, ventricular fibrillation, ischemic heart disease; pheochromocytoma, hyperthyroidism.

name: EPINEPHRINE /ADRENALINE
uses: Cardiac arrest, adjunct with local anesthetics, acute anaphylaxis
side_effects: Tachycardia, hypertension, tremor, chest pain, irregular heartbeats, headache, nausea, vomiting, nervousness, restlessness, weakness.
dosage: Acute anaphylaxis: intramuscular injection, adult: 0.5-1 ml, repeat every 10 minutes. Child (2-5 years): 0.2-0.4 ml; (6-12 years): 0.5 ml. Acute hypotension: continuous intravenous infusion, neonate and child: 100 nanogram/kg/min adjusted up to 1.5 mcg/kg/min. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation: Intravenous injection, adult: 1 mg every 3-5 min.
precautions: While using monitor blood pressure, heart rate. Avoid in patients on tricyclic antidepressants.
contraindications: Shock (other than anaphylactic shock), second stage labor. Do not use if color is cloudy or brownish.

name: MILRINONE
uses: Short-term treatment of severe congestive heart failure unresponsive to conventional therapy, acute heart failure following surgery.
side_effects: Ectopic beats, headache, hypotension, supraventricular arrhythmias, ventricular tachycardia. Chest pain, hypokalemia, thrombocytopenia, tremor, ventricular fibrillation.
dosage: Intravenous injection, adult: Initially 50 mcg/kg over 10 minutes, followed by infusion 375–750 nanogram/kg/minute; maximum dose: 1.13 mg/kg per day.
precautions: Use caution in hypokalemia, renal impairment, heart failure with HCM or valvular disease. Pregnancy: use with caution. Renal impairment: Reduce dose if eGFR < 50 mL/min/1.73 m2.

name: NOREPINEPHRINE/NORADRENALINE
uses: Acute hypotension
side_effects: Angle-closure glaucoma, anorexia, anxiety, arrhythmias, bradycardia, confusion, dyspnea, headache, hypertension, hypoxia, insomnia, nausea, palpitation, peripheral ischemia, psychosis, tachycardia, tremor, urinary retention, vomiting, weakness.
dosage: Acute hypotension: intravenous, adult: Initially 0.16–0.33 mL/minute, solution containing 40 mcg (base)/ml, adjusted according to response into large vein. Dilute 2 mg base with 48 mL infusion fluid for syringe pump. Dilute 20 mg base with 480 mL for drip counter.
precautions: Use caution in coronary thrombosis, diabetes, elderly, post-MI, hyperthyroidism, hypoxia. Avoid extravasation. Incompatible with alkalis.
contraindications: Hypertension. Uncorrected hypovolemia. Pregnancy: Avoid, may reduce placental perfusion.

name: BOSENTAN
uses: Pulmonary arterial hypertension, systemic sclerosis with ongoing digital ulcer disease.
side_effects: Anemia, diarrhea, flushing, gastro-esophageal reflux, headache, hypotension, edema, palpitation, syncope, liver cirrhosis, liver failure, leucopenia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia.
dosage: Pulmonary arterial hypertension: Oral, adult: Initially 62.5 mg twice daily for 4 weeks, then increased up to maximum 500 mg per day in 2 divided doses. Digital ulcer disease: Oral, adult: Initially 62.5 mg twice daily for 4 weeks, then increased to 125 mg twice daily.
precautions: Breast feeding: avoid. Effective hormonal contraception not considered effective. Monthly pregnancy tests advised. Monitor Hemoglobin and Liver function.
contraindications: Avoid in acute porphyria, systemic systolic blood pressure <85 mmHg. Pregnancy (X). Hepatic impairment: avoid in moderate to severe impairment.

name: SILDENAFIL
uses: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), erectile dysfunction
side_effects: headache, flushing, epistaxis, dyspepsia, insomnia, erythema, diarrhea, migraine, myalgia, nasal congestion, visual disturbance, back pain.
dosage: Erectile dysfunction: Oral, adult: 50 mg 1 hr. before sexual activity, maximum dose 100 mg, 1 dose per day. PAH: Oral, adult: 25 mg three times daily.
precautions: Avoid use with nitrates. Use caution in anatomic deformation of penis, retinitis pigmentosa, ischemic heart disease. With alcohol may cause dizziness.
contraindications: Avoid in hypotension, myocardial infarction, unstable angina, not for use in children with PAH.

name: ATORVASTATIN
uses: Primary hypercholesterolemia, homozygous or heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia or mixed hyperlipidemia.
side_effects: reversible myositis, headache, angina, chest pain, arthralgia, anorexia, weight gain, epistaxis, back pain, nasopharyngitis, hyperglycemia.
dosage: Primary hyperlipidemia: Oral, adult: 10 mg once daily; increase up to 80 mg. Oral, child (10-13 years): 10 mg once daily. Familial hypercholesterolemia: Oral, adult: initially 10 mg, increased to max 80 mg once daily. Oral, child (10-13 years): up to 20 mg once daily.
precautions: Liver function tests before and periodically during treatment. Non serious and reversible cognitive side effects may occur.
contraindications: Avoid in pregnancy, breastfeeding, active liver disease. Use caution in liver disease, elderly or high alcohol intake.

name: CHOLESTYRAMINE RESINS
uses: Adjunct to dietary therapy to decrease serum cholesterol and LDL concentrations, cholestasis induced pruritus.
side_effects: Bloating, dyspepsia, constipation, abdominal pain, anorexia, biliary colic, and skin rash.
dosage: Lipid reduction: Oral, adult: 12-24 g daily in water, up to 36 g if necessary. Cholestasis pruritus: Oral, adult: 4-8 g daily in water.
precautions: May impair absorption of fat-soluble vitamins, thyroid hormones, warfarin. Suspension should be prepared several hours before ingestion to reduce adverse effects.

name: EZETIMIBE
uses: Adjunct to dietary measures and statin treatment in primary hypercholesterolemia, homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia, or homozygous sitosterolemia.
side_effects: Fatigue, gastro-intestinal disturbances, headache, myalgia. Rare: anaphylaxis, angioedema, hepatitis, pancreatitis, rhabdomyolysis.
dosage: Oral, adult: 10 mg daily
precautions: N/A
contraindications: Avoid in moderate to severe hepatic impairment, myopathy, elevated hepatic transaminases, renal impairment (CrCl ≤ 30 ml/min/1.73 m2). Pregnancy (C) Breast feeding: avoid.

name: FENOFIBRATE
uses: Severe hypertriglyceridemia.
side_effects: Gastrointestinal disturbances, rash, urticaria, fatigue, headache, impotence.
dosage: Initially 160 mg once daily dose.
precautions: Use caution in mild to moderate renal and hepatic impairment. Monitor liver transaminases every 3 month for a year. Restrict fat diet.
contraindications: Avoid in gall bladder disease, hypoalbuminemia, nephrotic syndrome, pregnancy, breast feeding, severe hepatic impairment.

name: GEMFIBROZIL
uses: Adjunct to dietary therapy in hyperlipidemias of types II a, II b, III, IV and V.
side_effects: abdominal and epigastric pain, diarrhea, nausea, anorexia, headache, sexual dysfunction, myopathy, myositis, urticaria and pruritus.
dosage: Oral, adult: 1.2 g daily usually in 2 divided doses; range 0.9-1.2 g daily.
precautions: Risk for myopathy increases with renal impairment. Assess liver function, CBC, electrolytes every 3-6 months. Safety not established in children < 18 years. Pregnancy (C).
contraindications: Avoid in preexisting gallbladder disease, hepatic dysfunction, history of hypersensitivity. Breast feeding: Avoid.

name: NICOTINIC ACID (NIACIN)
uses: Adjunct to statin in hypertriglyceridemia and or used alone if statin not tolerated.
side_effects: diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, flushing, palpitations, dizziness, pruritus and rash.
dosage: Oral, adult: Initially 100-200 mg 3 times daily, gradually increased to l-2 g 3 times daily.
precautions: Use caution in liver disease, gout, diabetes, gallbladder disease, renal impairment. Pregnancy (A, C- for doses exceeding RDA). Breast feeding: use caution.
contraindications: Avoid in arterial hemorrhage, active peptic ulcer, and breast feeding.

name: SIMVASTATIN
uses: Primary and secondary prevention of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, in high risk individuals (e.g. with diabetes mellitus, post Myocardial infarction)
side_effects: Upper respiratory tract infection, myalgia, myopathy, rhabdomyolysis, abdominal pain, dyspepsia, hepatitis, jaundice, peripheral neuropathy, rashes, angioedema, cognitive side effects.
dosage: Prevention of cardiovascular events: Oral, adult: initially 20-40 mg once daily at night (maximum 80 mg).
precautions: Use caution in elderly (>65 years), hepatic or renal dysfunction. Suspend use if myopathy suspected. Reduce dose if used with certain antibiotics or antifungals.
contraindications: Avoid in pregnancy(X), breast-feeding, active liver disease. Use caution in uncontrolled hypothyroidism, perioperative periods.

name: ROSUVASTATIN
uses: Primary hypercholesterolemia (type IIa), mixed dyslipidemia (type IIb), or homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia, Prevention of cardiovascular events in patients at high risk.
side_effects: Flulike symptoms, constipation, urinary tract infection, proteinuria. Gynecomastia, hematuria, peripheral neuropathy, arthralgia.
dosage: Primary/Prevention of CV events: Oral, adult: Initially 5 mg once daily, increased up to 20 mg once daily. Severe primary hypercholesterolemia: Oral, adult: Initially 5–10 mg, increased up to 40 mg once daily. Renal impairment (eGFR 30–60 ml/min/1.73 m2): Initially 5 mg once daily (max 20 mg daily).
precautions: Use caution in mild to moderate renal impairment, patients with high CV risk.
contraindications: Avoid in pregnancy, breast feeding, severe renal impairment (eGFR < 30 ml/min), hepatic impairment.

name: FERROUS FUMARATE
uses: Iron-deficiency anemia.
side_effects: Diarrhea, constipation, nausea, epigastric pain, heart burn, discoloration of teeth.
dosage: Prophylactic: Oral, > 12 years: 210 mg elemental iron 1–2 times a day. Therapeutic: Oral, 12 years: 210 mg 2–3 times a day.
precautions: Best absorbed on an empty stomach but may be taken after food to reduce GI effects; may discolour stools.
contraindications: Hemochromatosis, hemosiderosis, hemolytic anemia (unless iron deficiency state is also present), any form of anaemia not caused by iron deficiency; patients receiving repeated blood transfusions; parenteral iron therapy.
interactions: Antacids and tetracyclines inhibit absorption. Citric acid and ascorbic acid increase absorption.

name: FERROUS FUMARATE WITH FOLIC ACID
uses: Iron deficiency anemia.
side_effects: See FERROUS FUMARATE and FOLIC ACID.
dosage: Oral, adult: 1 tablet/capsule daily, to be taken before food.
precautions: See FERROUS FUMARATE and FOLIC ACID.
contraindications: See FERROUS FUMARATE and FOLIC ACID.
interactions: See FERROUS FUMARATE and FOLIC ACID.

name: FERROUS GLUCONATE
uses: Prophylaxis and treatment of iron deficiency anemia.
side_effects: See FERROUS FUMARATE.
dosage: Prophylaxis: Child (6–11 years): 300–900 mg daily; Child (12–17 years) and Adult: 600 mg daily. Treatment: Child (6–11 years): 300–900 mg daily; Child (12–17 years) and Adult: 1.2–1.8 g daily in divided doses. All doses before food.
precautions: See FERROUS FUMARATE.

name: FERROUS SULPHATE
uses: Iron deficiency anemia.
side_effects: Diarrhea, constipation, nausea, epigastric pain (dose related).
dosage: Prophylaxis: 200 mg dried ferrous sulfate daily after food. Treatment: 400-600 mg daily in divided doses after food.
precautions: Tablet (300 mg) contains 60 mg elemental iron; Tablet (200 mg) contains 40 mg elemental iron.

name: FERROUS SULFATE WITH ASCORBIC ACID
uses: Iron deficiency anemia.
side_effects: N/A
dosage: Oral, adult: 1 tablet daily, dose to be taken before food.
precautions: Tablet contains Ferrous sulphate 325 mg and Sodium ascorbate 500 mg.

name: FERROUS SULPHATE WITH FOLIC ACID
uses: Prevention of iron and folic acid deficiencies in pregnancy; Severe anaemia.
side_effects: See FERROUS SULFATE.
dosage: Severe anaemia: Child <2 years: elemental iron 25 mg + folic acid 100–400 mcg daily for 3 months; Child 2–12 years: elemental iron 60 mg + folic acid 400 mcg daily for 3 months; Adult: elemental iron 120 mg + folic acid 400 mcg daily for 3 months. Pregnancy prophylaxis: Oral, adult: elemental iron 100 mg + folic acid 350–400 mcg daily throughout pregnancy.
precautions: Risk of precipitating subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord.
contraindications: Should never be given without vitamin B12 in undiagnosed megaloblastic anaemia; folate-dependent malignant disease. See FERROUS FUMARATE.

name: IRON DEXTRAN
uses: Iron deficiency anemia, only when oral administration has been found unsatisfactory or impossible.
side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, arthralgia, fever, urticaria, anaphylactic reactions, headache, hypotension.
dosage: 25-100 mg IV or deep IM every day when necessary, not to exceed 100 mg (2 ml/day).
precautions: Caution in pregnancy and hepatic/renal impairment. Contact physician if fever, chills, malaise, or joint aches occur.
contraindications: Allergic disorders including asthma, infection, active rheumatoid arthritis.

name: FOLIC ACID
uses: Folate deficiency megaloblastic anemia; prevention of neural tube defect in pregnancy.
side_effects: Bronchospasm, erythema, malaise, pruritis, rash, slight flushing.
dosage: Megaloblastic anemia: Oral, adult: 5 mg daily for 4 months. Prevention of neural tube defect (first occurrence): 400-500 mcg daily before conception and during first 12 weeks of pregnancy. Prevention of recurrence: 5 mg daily (reduced to 4 mg) from 4 weeks before conception to 12th week of pregnancy.
precautions: Monitor plasma folic acid levels, hemoglobin, and reticulocyte count.
contraindications: Should never be given without vitamin B12 in undiagnosed megaloblastic anaemia; folate dependent malignant disease.
interactions: Pyrimethamine, methotrexate, trimethoprim prevent activation. Absorption decreased by antacids and cholestyramine. Requirements increased by estrogens, phenytoin, carbamazepine.

name: EPOETIN ALFA
uses: Anemia associated with erythropoietin deficiency in chronic renal failure, autologous blood yield increase, symptomatic anaemia in cytotoxic chemotherapy or myelodysplastic syndrome.
side_effects: Hypertension, increased coagulability (thromboembolic events), pure red cell aplasia, seizures, flu-like symptoms, anaphylactic reactions.
dosage: Chronic renal failure: Initially 20 units/kg SC 3 times a week or 40 units/kg IV 3 times a week. Non-myeloid malignancies: Initially 450 units/kg SC once weekly, increase to 900 units/kg if response inadequate.
precautions: Monitor hemoglobin weekly. Do not shake or vigorously agitate vial. Refrigerate at 2–8°C.
contraindications: Uncontrolled hypertension; pure red cell aplasia (PRCA); Subcutaneous route contraindicated in chronic renal failure (per certain sections); Myocardial infarction, stroke, thromboembolism.
interactions: Androgens increase sensitivity of erythroid progenitors. Probenecid: Possible pharmacokinetic interaction. Desmopressin: Potential decrease in bleeding time.

name: HEPARIN (UNFRACTIONATED)
uses: Deep venous thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolism (PE), unstable angina, acute myocardial infarction, coronary angioplasty/stent placement.
side_effects: Hemorrhage, HIT, alopecia, bleeding, osteoporosis, hyperkalemia.
dosage: Prophylaxis of DVT/PE: Adult, SC: 5000 units 2 hours before surgery, then every 8-12 hours for 7 days. Treatment of DVT/PE: Adult, IV: loading 5000 units (75 units/kg) then infusion 18 units/kg/hour.
precautions: Laboratory monitoring essential (preferably daily). Check for heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT). Reverse with Protamine sulfate (1 mg per 1000 U heparin remaining). Pregnancy: use only if benefit justifies risk.
contraindications: Active bleeding, hemophilia, purpura, thrombocytopenia, hypersensitivity to pork products.
interactions: Action increased by oral anticoagulants, salicylates, dextran, NSAIDs. Action decreased by digoxin, tetracycline, nicotine.

name: LOW MOLECULAR WEIGHT HEPARINS
uses: Prophylaxis of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism.
side_effects: See HEPARIN.
dosage: Administered by SC injection in fixed or weight-adjusted dose regimen once or twice daily (e.g., Dalteparin, Enoxaparin).
precautions: See individual drug entries (Dalteparin, Enoxaparin). Routine monitoring not usually done.
contraindications: Reports of congenital anomalies in infants; causal relationship not established.

name: DALTEPARIN
uses: Prophylaxis of DVT in surgical and medical patients; treatment of DVT and PE.
side_effects: See HEPARIN.
dosage: Surgical prophylaxis: 2500 units SC 1-2 hours before surgery. Medical prophylaxis: 5000 units SC every 24 hours. PE Treatment: SC single daily dose based on weight (<46 kg: 7500 units; 46-56 kg: 10,000 units; 57-68 kg: 12,500 units).
precautions: See HEPARIN.

name: ENOXAPARIN
uses: Prophylaxis of DVT in surgical and medical patients.
side_effects: See HEPARIN.
dosage: Surgical prophylaxis: Moderate risk, 20 mg SC 2 hours before surgery then daily for 7-10 days; High risk, 40 mg SC 12 hours before surgery then daily. Medical prophylaxis: 4000 units SC every 24 hours for at least 6 days.
precautions: See HEPARIN.

name: WARFARIN
uses: Prevention of progression and recurrence of DVT or PE; thromboembolism prevention in heart valves, acute MI, or atrial fibrillation.
side_effects: Hemorrhage.
dosage: Initial dose 10 mg for 2 days, subsequent doses 3-9 mg daily in accordance with prothrombin activity of blood.
precautions: Monitor prothrombin activity (INR). Contraindicated in women who are or may become pregnant.
contraindications: GI ulcers, severe hypertension, bacterial endocarditis, pregnancy, recent surgery.
interactions: Vitamin K rich food/supplements decrease effect. Metabolism decreased by allopurinol, cimetidine, amiodarone, metronidazole (enhances hemorrhage risk).

name: ACENOCOUMAROL
uses: See WARFARIN.
side_effects: See WARFARIN.
dosage: 4-12 mg on first day, 4-8 mg on second day, maintenance 1-8 mg daily.
precautions: See WARFARIN.

name: APIXABAN
uses: Stroke prophylaxis with atrial fibrillation, postoperative DVT/PE prophylaxis, DVT or PE treatment.
side_effects: Anaemia, bruising, haemorrhage, nausea.
dosage: Stroke prophylaxis: 5 mg PO twice a day. Post-op DVT/PE: 2.5 mg PO twice a day for 35 days. DVT/PE treatment: 10 mg twice a day for 7 days, then 5 mg twice a day.
precautions: Risk of paralysis with indwelling epidural catheter.
contraindications: Active bleeding, malignant neoplasms, oesophageal varices, recent brain/spine surgery, vascular aneurysm.

name: BIVALIRUDIN
uses: Unstable angina/non-ST-segment elevation MI planned for urgent intervention or proceeding to PCI.
side_effects: Bleeding, ecchymosis, allergic reactions, anaemia, headache, hypotension.
dosage: Early intervention: IV injection 100 mcg/kg, then infusion 250 mcg/kg/hour. PCI without bypass: IV injection 100 mcg/kg for 1 dose, then 500 mcg/kg for 1 dose, then infusion 1.75 mg/kg/hour.
precautions: INR monitoring should be done. Discontinue if unexplained fall in blood pressure or hematocrit occurs.
contraindications: Active bleeding, bleeding disorders, severe hypertension, subacute bacterial endocarditis.
interactions: Increase risk of haemorrhage with other analgesics and anticoagulants.

name: DABIGATRAN
uses: Stroke prophylaxis with atrial fibrillation, DVT/PE treatment or prophylaxis.
side_effects: Dyspepsia, gastritis, intracranial hemorrhage, hypersensitivity (urticaria, rash).
dosage: Stroke prophylaxis: CrCl >30 ml/min: 150 mg twice a day. DVT/PE treatment: 150 mg twice a day. DVT/PE prophylaxis (post-surgery): 110 mg 1-4 hr after surgery then 220 mg once a day.
precautions: Monitor Ecarin clotting time (ECT); if unavailable monitor aPPT, PT, or TT.
contraindications: Severe renal impairment (CrCl <15 mL/min), active pathologic bleeding.

name: FONDAPARINUX
uses: DVT, heparin induced thrombocytopenia, unstable angina, ST-segment elevation and non-ST-segment elevation MI, PE.
side_effects: Anaemia, bleeding, purpura, chest pain, dyspnoea, hepatic impairment, oedema.
dosage: DVT/PE: <50 kg: 5 mg SC once a day; 50-100 kg: 7.5 mg SC once daily; >100 kg: 10 mg SC once daily. HIT: 2.5 mg SC once daily.
precautions: Monitor for sign and symptoms of neurologic impairment in epidural/spinal anesthesia.
contraindications: Active bleeding, bacterial endocarditis, active GI ulcer disease, brain surgery.

name: RIVAROXABAN
uses: Prophylaxis of venous thromboembolism (orthopaedic surgery), DVT, PE, nonvalvular atrial fibrillation.
side_effects: Abdominal pain, dizziness, dyspepsia, haemorrhage, renal impairment.
dosage: Orthopaedic prophylaxis: 10 mg PO once a day for 12 days. DVT/PE treatment: 15 mg twice a day for 21 days, then 20 mg once a day for 6 months.
precautions: Risk of bleeding in patients with haemodynamic instability or severe hypertension.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, active bleeding, malignant neoplasms, GI ulcer, vascular retinopathy.
interactions: Increases concentration with antibacterials/antivirals. Antiepileptics decrease plasma concentration.

name: ASPIRIN
uses: Prophylaxis of cerebro vascular diseases, MI, thromboembolic disorder, ischemic stroke and angina.
side_effects: Bronchospasm, GI bleeding, thrombocytopenia, seizures, Reye’s syndrome.
dosage: Thromboembolic disorders: Oral 325-650 mg/day. Transient ischemic attack: 50-325 mg/day. Evolving MI: 160-325 mg chewed/swallowed immediately.
precautions: Do not give to children/adolescents due to Reye’s syndrome. Take after food with plenty of water.
contraindications: Haemorrhagic stroke, hypersensitivity to acetylsalicylic, active peptic ulceration, haemophilia, asthma.
interactions: Increase effects of oral hypoglycemics. Increased chance of bleeding with anticoagulants.

name: CLOPIDOGREL
uses: Prevention of atherothrombotic events in TIA, stroke, or ACS (with or without ST-elevation).
side_effects: Abdominal pain, bleeding disorders (GI and intracranial), diarrhea, dyspepsia.
dosage: TIA/Stroke: 75 mg once daily. ACS without ST-elevation: Initially 300 mg, then 75 mg daily. ACS with ST-elevation: 18–75 years: Initially 300 mg, then 75 mg daily.
precautions: Avoid in pregnancy; caution in renal and hepatic impairment.
interactions: Action increased by anticoagulants, aspirin, NSAIDs. Effect decreased by PPIs.

name: PRASUGREL
uses: Prevention of atherothrombotic events in ACS undergoing PCI; alternative to clopidogrel.
side_effects: Anemia, GI hemorrhage, hematoma, hematuria, intracranial hemorrhage, rash.
dosage: Combination with aspirin for PCI: Adult <60 kg: Initially 60 mg then 5 mg once daily; Adult ≥60 kg: Initially 60 mg then 10 mg once daily.
precautions: Discontinue at least 7 days before elective surgery.
contraindications: Active bleeding, history of stroke or TIA. Body weight < 60 kg (requires caution/dose reduction).
interactions: Increased risk of hypersensitivity when given with other thienopyridines.

name: TICLOPIDINE
uses: Coronary artery stent thrombosis prevention, stroke.
side_effects: Diarrhea, elevated alkaline phosphatase/AST/ALT, nausea, rash, neutropenia, purpura.
dosage: Stent thrombosis: 250 mg twice a day with aspirin for 30 days. Stroke: 250 mg twice daily with food.
precautions: Monitor CBC and Liver function test every 2 weeks for the first 3 months. Risk of aplastic anemia.
contraindications: Neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, active bleeding, severe hepatic impairment.
interactions: Concurrent use of other anticoagulants increases bleeding incidence.

name: ALTEPLASE
uses: Acute myocardial infarction, pulmonary embolism, acute stroke.
side_effects: Risk of cerebral bleeding, reperfusion arrhythmias, pulmonary edema, hypotension.
dosage: MI (Accelerated): 15 mg IV bolus, then 0.75 mg/kg infusion over 30 min, then 0.5 mg/kg over 60 min (max 100 mg). Acute Stroke: 900 mcg/kg (max 90 mg) IV infusion, 10% bolus then remainder over 60 min.
precautions: Monitor for intracranial hemorrhage and blood pressure (systolic <180, diastolic <105 recommended).
contraindications: Current intracranial hemorrhage, subarachnoid hemorrhage, recent stroke, active internal bleeding, recent intracranial/intraspinal surgery.
interactions: Bleeding incidence increased with concurrent anticoagulants.

name: STREPTOKINASE
uses: Pulmonary embolism, deep venous thrombosis, acute myocardial infarction.
side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, bleeding, arrhythmias, allergic reactions (rash, flushing, anaphylaxis).
dosage: Acute MI: 1,500,000 units IV infusion over 60 minutes. DVT/PE: 250,000 units IV over 30 minutes, then 100,000 units every 1 hour for 12–72 hours.
precautions: Strongly antigenic; repeated administration elicits antibodies.
contraindications: Surgery within 10 days, severe trauma, GI bleeding within 3 months, history of hypertension (diastolic >110 mmHg).
interactions: Risk of hemorrhage increased with heparin, oral anticoagulants, or antiplatelets (aspirin).

name: TENECTEPLASE
uses: Acute myocardial infarction.
side_effects: See ALTEPLASE.
dosage: 30–50 mg IV bolus over 10 seconds. Dose varies by weight (e.g., <60 kg: 30 mg; >90 kg: 50 mg).
precautions: Initiate within 6 hours of symptom onset.

name: UROKINASE
uses: See STREPTOKINASE.
side_effects: Non-antigenic, but mild allergic reactions (bronchospasm, rash) reported.
dosage: Pulmonary embolism: Initial 4400 IU/kg IV over 10 minutes; Maintenance: 4400 IU/kg/hr for 12 hours.
precautions: If heparin was given, ensure aPTT is less than twice the normal control value before starting.
contraindications: Must not be given SC or IM. Fibrinogen should not be <100 mg/dl.
interactions: Increased hemorrhage risk with anticoagulants or substances affecting platelet function.

name: ETHAMSYLATE
uses: Blood loss in menorrhagia, post-partum bleeding, post abortion bleeding.
side_effects: Headache, rashes, hypotension.
dosage: Oral, adult: 500 mg 4 times daily during menstruation.
precautions: Caution if patient develops fever or has fibroids in uterus.

name: TRANEXAMIC ACID
uses: Menorrhagia, epistaxis, thrombolytic overdose, hereditary angioedema.
side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, disturbances in colour vision.
dosage: Menorrhagia: 1 g PO 3 times daily for 4 days. Epistaxis: 1 g PO 3 times a day for 7 days. Hereditary angioedema: 1–1.5 g PO 2–3 times a day.
precautions: Do not use with hormonal contraceptives. Do not take for more than 5 days in a row.
contraindications: Severe renal impairment (CrCl < 1.5 mg/dl), thromboembolic disease.

name: PROTAMINE SULPHATE
uses: Heparin overdose.
side_effects: Hypotension, bradycardia, flushing, urticaria, angioedema.
dosage: Adult, slow IV: 1 mg neutralises 100 units heparin if given within 15 minutes. Maximum 50 mg.
precautions: Caution in fish hypersensitivity or post-vasectomy patients. Monitor with coagulation studies.
contraindications: Bleeding that occurs without prior exposure to heparin.

name: PHYTOMENADIONE (VITAMIN K1)
uses: Antagonists to warfarin, prophylaxis against hemorrhagic disease of newborn.
side_effects: Facial flushing, bronchospasm, dyspnea, hypotension.
dosage: Warfarin-induced hypoprothrombinemia: Adult, 5-10 mg slow IV. Newborn prophylaxis: IM 0.5-1 mg as single dose.
precautions: Rapid IV administration may cause fatal anaphylaxis. Protect from light.
contraindications: Avoid IM route if bleeding or in 3rd trimester of pregnancy.
interactions: Decreases effects of warfarin by pharmacodynamic antagonism.

name: HUMAN ALBUMIN
uses: Hypovolemia, hypoalbuminemia, ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome, ARDS, hemolytic disease of the newborn.
side_effects: Anaphylactic shock, circulatory failure, cardiac failure, pulmonary edema.
dosage: Hypovolemia (Adult): IV 25 g. Newborns: 1 g/kg. Max daily dose: 2 g/kg of body weight.
precautions: Measures of circulating volume adequacy (not plasma levels) should guide dosing.
contraindications: Severe anemia, hypertension, esophageal varices, pulmonary edema, renal/post-renal anuria.

name: FACTOR IX COMPLEX
uses: Replacement therapy for factor IX deficiency in haemophilia B; bleeding due to deficiencies of factors II, VII, or X.
side_effects: Allergic reactions (chills, fever), flushing, thrombosis.
dosage: Treatment: IV 1 unit/kg increases plasma level by 1%. Units needed = weight (kg) x desired % increase x 1 unit/kg.
precautions: Do not exceed infusion rate of 10 mL/minute. Risk of thrombosis. Store at 2-8°C.
interactions: Aminocaproic Acid: May increase risk of thrombosis.

name: DESMOPRESSIN
uses: Bleeding control, diabetes insipidus, primary nocturnal enuresis.
side_effects: Fluid retention, headache, nausea, vomiting, epistaxis.
dosage: Diabetes insipidus: Adult/Child PO/IV 1-4 mcg daily. Hemophilia A: Intranasal 150 mcg in each nostril (if >50 kg).
precautions: Rhinitis can decrease intranasal effectiveness. Caution in hypertension.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, pseudo Von Willebrand’s disease, cardiac insufficiency, renal impairment.
interactions: Enhanced by carbamazepine/clofibrate. Diminished by alcohol/lithium.

name: POLYGELINE
uses: Low blood volume.
side_effects: Anaphylactic reaction, transient increase in bleeding time.
dosage: Adult, IV: initially 500-1000 ml of 3.5% solution.
precautions: Avoid hematocrit falling below 25–30%. Monitor urine output.
contraindications: Pregnancy at end of term; severe impairment.

name: CALCIUM
uses: Hypocalcemia in tetany, osteoporosis
side_effects: Constipation, bradycardia, cardiac arrhythmia, hypotension and irritation after parenteral administration
dosage: Supplement: 1-2 g between meals; daily requirement is greater in childhood, pregnancy, lactation and old age. Acute hypocalcaemia: 1-2 g by slow intravenous injection.
precautions: 1.25 g calcium carbonate is equivalent to 500 mg elemental calcium.
contraindications: Hypercalcemic states, do not use if allergic to any ingredients of calcium preparations
interactions: Reduce absorption of ciprofloxacin, tetracycline, iron, bisphosphonates

name: IODINE
uses: Prevention and treatment of iodine deficiency
side_effects: See section 12.5 under drugs used in endocrine system
dosage: Daily recommended intake: 150 μg (200 μg in pregnant and breast-feeding mothers); under 1 year: 50 μg; 2-6 years: 90 μg; 7-12 years: 120 μg.
precautions: Also see section 12.5 under drugs used in endocrine system.

name: IRON
uses: See section 4 under drugs used in blood
side_effects: N/A
dosage: N/A
precautions: See section 4 under drugs used in blood

name: PHOSPHATES
uses: Treatment of hypophosphatemia
side_effects: Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, fluid retention, and hypocalcaemia
dosage: N/A
precautions: Available as Potassium phosphate or Sodium phosphate salts.

name: SODIUM FLUORIDE
uses: Prevention of dental caries
side_effects: White flakes on teeth with recommended doses; Yellowish brown discoloration of teeth with more than recommended doses
dosage: Water content <0.3 ppm: child up to 6 months none; 6 months-3 years 250 μg daily; 3-6 years 500 μg daily; over 6 years 1 mg daily. Water content 0.3-0.7 ppm: child up to 3 years none; 3-6 years 250 μg daily, over 6 years 500 μg daily. Prevention: as oral rinse, child over 6 years 10 ml 0.05% solution daily or 10 ml 0.2% solution weekly.
precautions: Advisable to institute artificial fluoridation in areas with drinking water containing less than 700 μg/l (0.7 ppm).

name: ZINC
uses: Zinc deficiency, diarrhoea in children (rota virus infection), adjunct to vitamin A therapy
side_effects: Dyspepsia, abdominal pain, headache, nausea, vomiting, gastritis
dosage: Adjunct to oral rehydration solution in acute diarrhoea: Under 6 months: 10 mg (elemental zinc) daily for 10 days; 6 months – 5 years: 20 mg daily for 10 days.
precautions: Must be taken for 2-3 months to be effective. Used with caution in acute renal failure.
interactions: Decreases absorption of floroquinolones; absorption of zinc is reduced when taken with dietary products, caffeine

name: VITAMIN A (RETINOL)
uses: Deficiency states, prophylaxis in high risk subjects, steatorrhea, severe biliary obstruction, cirrhosis of liver or following total gastrectomy, severe ocular damage
side_effects: Hypervitaminosis, fatigue, irritability, mental change, anorexia, nausea, vomiting, GI upset
dosage: Treatment of xerophthalmia: infants (6-11 months) 100,000 U (3 drops) on diagnosis; child over one year and adult 200,000 units on diagnosis (repeat next day and after one month). Prevention of deficiency: child 6 months to 5 years, 200,000 U every 6 months. Measles: 200,000 U. Newly delivered mothers: 200,000 U within 6 weeks.
precautions: Avoid high doses in pregnancy due to risk of hypervitaminosis.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to vitamin A, malabsorption syndrome, hypervitaminosis A, pregnancy, breastfeeding, impaired renal function, children, hepatic disease, alcoholism, hepatitis
interactions: Mineral oil, cholestyramine, colestipol decrease absorption of Vitamin A

name: VITAMIN D3 (CALCITRIOL)
uses: Hypocalcaemia with chronic renal disease, psoriasis, renal dystrophy, prevention and treatment of rickets, post menopausal osteoporosis
side_effects: Drowsiness, headache, palpitations, Hypertension, photophobia, hypercalcemia, myalgia, arthralgia, weakness, pain in injection site
dosage: Hypocalcaemia (Stage 5 CKD): Adults, oral, 0.25 μg/day; Children 1-5 year, oral, 1-5 μg/day; Rickets, oral, 1 μg/day. Osteoporosis prophylaxis in corticosteroid therapy: oral, 0.5-1 mcg/day.
precautions: Pregnancy, breastfeeding, renal calculi.
interactions: Hypercalcaemia may occur if thiazide diuretics or calcium supplements are concomitantly used; cardiac dysarrythmia may occur with cardiac glycosides or verapamil

name: VITAMIN E (TOCOPHEROL)
uses: Vitamin E deficiency states, impaired fat absorption, hemolytic anemia in premature neonates, prevention of retrolental fibroplasias, sickle cell anemia, supplementation of malabsorption syndrome
side_effects: Headache, fatigue, increased risk of thrombophlebitis, cramps, diarrhea, gonadal dysfunction, weakness
dosage: Deficiency states: adult, oral, 60-75 IU/day, child, oral, 1 IU/day.
precautions: Avoid in patients with hypoprothrombinaemia.
interactions: Increases actions of oral anticoagulants, concomitant use of cholestyramine, sucralfate decrease absorption of vitamin E

name: VITAMIN K
uses: See under Drugs used in blood disorders
side_effects: N/A
dosage: N/A
precautions: See under Drugs used in blood disorders

name: VITAMIN B1 (THIAMINE)
uses: Vitamin B1 deficiency, polyneuritis, cheilosis, beri-beri, Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome, pellagra, metabolic disorders
side_effects: Weakness, restlessness, pulmonary edema, hypotension, collapse, angioneurotic edema, cyanosis, hemorrhage
dosage: Adult, oral (males): 1.2-1.5 mg, (females): 1.1 mg, (pregnancy): 1.4 mg, (breast feeding): 1.4 mg; child, oral: 0.5-0.9 mg; infant, oral: 0.2 mg.
precautions: Monitor for hypersensitivity reactions.

name: VITAMIN B2 (RIBOFLAVIN)
uses: Vitamin B2 deficiency, polyneuritis, cheilosis, migraine prophylaxis
side_effects: Yellow discoloration of urine
dosage: Adult: 5-30 mg/day; child >12 yr: PO 3-10 mg/day then 0.6 mg/1000 calories ingested. Migraine prophylaxis: adult- 400 mg/day for three months.
precautions: Higher doses used for migraine prophylaxis.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to vitamin B2, pregnancy (caution indicated)
interactions: Decrease action of tetracyclines, may cause false elevations of urinary catecholamines
