name: VITAMIN B3 (NIACIN)
uses: Pellagra, hyperlipidemias (types 4, 5), peripheral vascular disease
side_effects: Paraesthesia, headache, dizziness, Postural hypotension, vasovagal attacks, dysrhythmias, vasodilation, blurred vision, ptosis, jaundice, hepatotoxicity, hepatitis, glycosuria
dosage: Pellagra: adult, up to 500 mg daily in divided doses.
precautions: Assess cardiac status, nutritional status, CNS symptoms, Niacin deficiency, Hyperlipidemia.
contraindications: Peptic ulcer, hepatic disease, hemorrhage, severe hypotension, glaucoma, coronary artery disease, diabetes mellitus, gout, schizophrenia
interactions: Statins increase risk of rhabdomyolysis. Cholestyramine, erythromycin, insulin decrease blood level of niacin.

name: VITAMIN B6 (PYRIDOXINE)
uses: Vitamin B6 deficiency, seizures, isoniazid therapy, oral contraceptives, alcoholic polyneuritis
side_effects: Paresthesia, flushing, warmth, lethargy, pain at injected site
dosage: Deficiency states: oral, 25–50 mg up to 3 times daily. Isoniazid neuropathy prophylaxis: oral, 10 mg daily. Treatment: oral, 50 mg 3 times daily. Sideroblastic anemia: oral, 100–400 mg daily in divided doses.
precautions: Patients taking levodopa should avoid supplemental vitamins with >5 mg pyridoxine.

name: VITAMIN B9 (FOLIC ACID)
uses: Megaloblastic or macrocytic anemia caused by folic acid deficiency; hepatic disease, alcoholism, hemolysis, intestinal obstruction, pregnancy to reduce risk for neural tube defects
side_effects: Confusion, depression, excitability, irritability, anorexia, nausea, pruritus, rash, erythema, bronchospasm, anaphylaxis
dosage: Treatment of megaloblastic anemia: oral, adult, 5 mg daily for 4 months (up to 15 mg in malabsorption). Prevention of neural tube defects (first occurrence): oral, adult, 400–500 micrograms daily before conception and during first 12 weeks. Prevention of recurrence: oral, adult, 5 mg daily from 4 weeks before conception until 12th week.
precautions: Should never be given without vitamin B12 in undiagnosed megaloblastic anemia to avoid subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord.
contraindications: Anemia other than megaloblastic/macrocytic anemia, vit B12 deficiency anemia, uncorrected pernicious anemia
interactions: Interacts with estrogen, hydantoins, carbamazepine, glucocorticoids; decreases levels of methotrexate, sulfonamides, trimethoprim

name: VITAMIN B12 (COBALAMIN)
uses: Vitamin B12 deficiency states, malabsorbtion, pernicious anemia, stomach or lower ileal resection; macrocytic anemia
side_effects: Dizziness, memory impairment, restlessness, hypertension, chest pain, tachycardia, dry throat, eye redness, diarrhea, dyspepsia, thrombocytosis, hypokalemia, pain at site
dosage: Deficiency of dietary origin: oral- adult, 50-150 μg/day; child, 25-50 μg twice daily. IM injection: initially 1 mg repeated 10 times then 1 mg monthly. Pernicious anemia: IM injection, initially 1 mg repeated 5 times at intervals of 2 days, then 1 mg every 3 months.
precautions: Parenteral products should be used when deficiency is due to malabsorption. Switch to oral after remission.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to Vitamin B12, uremia, folate deficiency, concurrent infections, iron deficiency, renal dysfunction
interactions: Chloramphenicol/antineoplastics decrease hematologic response; Colchicine, aminosalicylic acid, cimetidine, excess alcohol or Vitamin C decrease absorption

name: VITAMIN C (ASCORBIC ACID)
uses: Vitamin C deficiency, scurvy, delayed wound, bone healing, chronic disease; urine acidification; before gastrectomy; dietary supplement
side_effects: Headache, insomnia, dizziness, fatigue, flushing, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, anorexia, heartburn, cramps, polyuria, hemolysis
dosage: Prophylaxis of scurvy: oral, 25–75 mg daily. Treatment of scurvy: oral, not less than 250 mg daily in divided doses.
precautions: Caution in patients with a history of renal calculi or gout.
contraindications: Tartrazine/sulfite sensitivity; glucose-6-phosphate deficiency. Pregnancy (caution), gout, diabetes, renal calculi
interactions: Excess intake may decrease effectiveness of Vitamin B12.

name: ACETAZOLAMIDE
uses: Open-angle glaucoma, angle-closure glaucoma (preoperatively if surgery delayed), secondary glaucoma, acute altitude sickness, CHF, drug induced edema.
side_effects: Confusion, convulsions, cholestatic jaundice, drowsiness, malaise, metallic taste, metabolic acidosis.
dosage: Angle closure glaucoma: 250 mg 24hr and 250 mg BD (oral/IV). Open-Angle glaucoma: 250 mg/day in divided doses (max 1 g/day).
precautions: Not recommended in non-congestive angle-closure glaucoma, hypercalciuria, diabetes, respiratory acidosis, pulmonary obstruction, emphysema, COPD. Monitor for impaired alertness.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to sulfonamide, severe renal disease, hepatic disease, electrolyte imbalance (hyponatremia/hypokalemia), hyperchloremic acidosis, Addison’s disease, adrenocortical deficiency, cirrhosis.
interactions: Increases action of amphetamines, phenytoin, procainamide, quinidine; increases toxicity of salicylate and cyclosporine; cardiac toxicity with arsenic trioxide/cardiac glycosides.

name: AMILORIDE HYDROCHLORIDE
uses: Oedema, CHF/HTN/Thiazide induced hypokalemia.
side_effects: Hyponatremia, postural hypotension, diarrhoea, loss of appetite, dizziness.
dosage: Oedema (alone): initially 10 mg daily (max 20 mg). Oedema (combination): 5 mg daily (max 20 mg). CHF/HTN induced hypokalemia: 5-10 mg/day q day or divided q12h. Renal impairment: CrCl 10-50 ml/min: 50% normal dose.
precautions: Caution in patients with diabetes mellitus, mild renal impairment, elderly, dehydration. Monitor potassium levels regularly.
contraindications: Hyperkalaemia, Addison’s Disease, Renal failure (CrCL<10), Anuria, Diabetic nephropathy.

name: CHLORTHALIDONE
uses: Hypertension, ascites due to cirrhosis, oedema due to nephrotic syndrome, mild to moderate chronic heart failure, nephrogenic diabetes insipidus.
side_effects: Hypotension, vasculitis, photosensitivity, electrolyte abnormalities, hyperglycemia, hyperuricemia, pancreatitis (rare).
dosage: Hypertension: 12.5-25 mg daily (max 50 mg). Edema: 50-100 mg daily or on alternate days (max 200 mg). CHF: 25–50 mg daily, increase to 100–200 mg for maintenance. Diabetes insipidus: 100 mg twice daily reduced to 50 mg daily.
precautions: Possible hazards include fetal/neonatal jaundice or thrombocytopenia. Lactation not recommended. Take in the morning with food.
interactions: Increases toxicity of aminolevulinic acid. Synergistic hypokalemia risk with amisulpride. Contraindicated with cisapride (QTc risk). Avoid with lithium.

name: EPLERENONE
uses: HTN, heart failure post MI, renal impairment, hepatic impairment.
side_effects: Hyperkalemia, dizziness, fatigue, albuminuria, abdominal pain.
dosage: HTN: Initial 50 mg PO qDay; may increase to 50 mg PO q12h. Heart failure post MI: Initial 25 mg PO qDay; may titrate to 50 mg daily based on potassium levels.
precautions: Risk of hyperkalemia is higher in patients with impaired renal function, proteinuria, and diabetes. Monitor for palpitations.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Serum potassium >5.5 mEq/L at initiation. Renal impairment (CrCl <50ml/min or creatinine >2 mg/dl in males / >1.8 mg/dl in females). Strong CYP3A inhibitors.
interactions: Itraconazole, Nefazodone, and Saquinavir increase eplerenone levels (CYP3A4 inhibition).

name: FUROSEMIDE
uses: Edema, heart failure, hypertension resistant to thiazide, AKI/CKD fluid overload, acute pulmonary edema, hypertensive crisis.
side_effects: Hypokalemia, hyponatremia, tinnitus, hearing impairment, vomitting, diarrhea, hyperuricemia gout.
dosage: Edema: 40 mg morning, maintenance 20-40 mg daily (pediatric 1-3 mg/kg). Pulmonary edema/HTN crisis: 0.5 mg/kg (or 40 mg) IV over 1-2 min; max 160-200 mg/dose. ACLS: Hyperkalemia 40-80 mg IV; Hypermagnesemia 20-40 mg IV q3-4h.
precautions: Monitor for hypokalemia (high potassium diet recommended). Caution in prostatic enlargement, oliguria, and elderly. Monitor for hearing impairment.
contraindications: Renal failure with anuria, comatose/precomatose states with cirrhosis, dehydration, hyperkalemia, hypovolemia, severe hyponatremia.
interactions: Predisposes to digitalis toxicity. Hypotensive effects enhanced by ACE inhibitors. Aminoglycosides increase ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity. Contraindicated with cisapride.

name: HYDROCHLORTHIAZIDE
uses: Edema (CHF, cirrhosis, nephritic syndrome, CKD, glomerulonephritis), hypertension, nephrogenic diabetes mellitus, calcium nephrolithiasis.
side_effects: Anaphylaxis, extracellular fluid volume depletion, hypokalemia, hyponatremia, hyperuricemia, hyperlipidemia, erectile dysfunction, hepatotoxicity.
dosage: Hypertension: 12.5 mg daily (max 25-50 mg) in morning. Edema: 25-50 mg per oral initially, maintenance 25-50 mg on alternate days.
precautions: Use caution in gout, elderly; may unmask diabetes. Monitor fluid/electrolyte balance. Monitor SLE status.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, anuria, hyponatremia, hypercalcemic states (hyperparathyroidism, malignancies), hypokalemia, hyperuricemia, polymorphic ventricular tachycardia.
interactions: Amphotericin B and Corticosteroids increase hypokalemia risk. Concomitant use with Quinidine risks fatal arrhythmias. Increases lithium effects.

name: INDAPAMIDE
uses: Hypertension, congestive heart failure.
side_effects: Skin rash, hypokalemia, anorexia, diarrhea, orthostatic hypotension, palpitation.
dosage: Essential HTN: 2.5 mg daily (immediate-release) or 1.5 mg daily (sustained-release) in the morning. CHF: 2.5 mg daily in the morning.
precautions: Use caution in acute porphyria, hypotension, diabetes, hyperuricemia, gout, SLE. Safety not established in children.
interactions: Avoid with arrhythmogenic drugs (e.g., Amiosulpride, Amitriptyline, Chlorpromazine, Cisapride, Fluconazole). Avoid with other diuretics due to hypokalemia risk.

name: MANNITOL
uses: Cerebral edema, raised intraocular pressure, anuria/oliguria.
side_effects: Acidosis, circulatory overload, pulmonary edema, chest pain, visual disturbances, skin necrosis (extravasation), acute renal failure.
dosage: Cerebral/Intraocular edema: 1.5-2 g/kg IV infused over 30-60 minutes. Anuria/Oliguria: Test dose 200 mg/kg (as 20% solution) IV over 3–5 min; re-evaluate if output <30–50 ml/hour.
precautions: Monitor fluid/electrolyte balance and renal function. Do not give simultaneously with blood. Risk of tissue necrosis on extravasation.
contraindications: Pulmonary edema, intracranial bleeding (except during craniotomy), severe CHF, metabolic edema with capillary fragility, severe dehydration, renal failure (without test dose response).
interactions: Increases excretion of salicylates, barbiturates, imipramine, and bromides.

name: METOLAZONE
uses: Hypertension, Edema.
side_effects: Chest pain, chills, electrolyte abnormalities, glucosuria, hyperuricemia, hepatotoxicity.
dosage: Oedema: 5–10 mg daily (max 20 mg; up to 80 mg in resistant cases). Hypertension: 5 mg daily in morning; maintenance 5 mg daily on alternate days.
precautions: Drug crosses placenta. Monitor for fetal hypokalemia, hypoglycemia, jaundice. Caution in DM, hypercholesterolemia, gout, SLE, and liver disease.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to sulfonamides, anuria, hepatic coma/precoma, acute porphyrias.
interactions: Metolazone + Chlorthalidone increases toxicity. Risks hypokalemia with Amisulpride. Contraindicated with cisapride.

name: SPIRONOLACTONE
uses: Edema and ascites in cirrhosis, nephrotic syndrome, CHF, primary hyperaldosteronism.
side_effects: Hyperkalemia, metabolic acidosis (cirrhotics), gynecomastia, impotence, decreased libido, hirsutism, gastric bleeding.
dosage: Edema: 100-200 mg daily (max 400 mg in resistance); child 1-3 mg/kg daily. Hyperaldosteronism: 400 mg daily for 3-4 weeks. CHF adjunct: 25 mg daily.
precautions: Monitor Blood Urea Nitrogen (BUN) and K+ regularly. Risk of breast cancer increased in chronic use.
contraindications: Hyperkalemia, hyponatremia, Addison disease, moderate to severe renal impairment.
interactions: CYP3A4 inhibitors (Clarithromycin, Ketoconazole, Ritonavir) may induce dangerous hyperkalemia by inhibiting catabolism.

name: TORSEMIDE
uses: Congestive heart failure, Chronic renal failure, Hepatic cirrhosis, Hypertension.
side_effects: Headache, electrolyte imbalance, rhinitis, constipation, diarrhoea, dyspepsia.
dosage: CHF/CRF: 10-20 mg daily initially, doubled up to max 200 mg. Cirrhosis: 5-10 mg daily (max 40 mg). Hypertension: 2.5-5 mg/day initially.
precautions: Monitor for hypokalemia, hyponatremia, hyperglycemia. Rise slowly to avoid orthostatic hypotension. Take with food.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to torsemide or povidone, anuria, hepatic coma.

name: TRIAMTERENE
uses: Edema, potassium conservation with thiazides and loop diuretics.
side_effects: Hyperkalemia, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, muscle cramps, dizziness.
dosage: Initially 15-250 mg daily, reducing to alternate days after 1 week. Lower initial dose if given with other diuretics.
precautions: Regular monitoring of blood K+ required. May cause blue fluorescence of urine. Avoid high K+ diet (avocado, banana).
interactions: Dangerous hyperkalemia when used with other K+ sparing diuretics.

name: DESMOPRESSIN
uses: Diabetes insipidus, primary nocturnal enuresis, post-operative polyuria, nocturia in multiple sclerosis.
side_effects: Fluid retention, headache, nausea, epistaxis, allergic reaction.
dosage: DI: Adult/Child initially 300 μg PO (max 1.2 mg daily); Injection 1-4 μg daily. Enuresis: 200 μg bedtime (max 400 μg). Renal testing: 2 μg (SC/IM).
precautions: Monitor for hyponatremia; therapy may be held if it occurs. Avoid fluid overload. Stop during vomiting/diarrhoea.
contraindications: Hyponatremia, cardiac insufficiency, renal impairment. Conditions treated with diuretics. Polydipsia in alcohol dependence.
interactions: Chlorpropamide and dobutamine increase effects (synergism). Demeclocycline, lithium, and alcohol diminish response.

name: VASOPRESSIN (ANTIDIURETIC HORMONE)
uses: Diabetes insipidus, abdominal distension, abdominal roentgenography, bleeding oesophageal varices.
side_effects: Angina, fluid retention, sweating, tremor, constriction of coronary arteries, pounding in head, vertigo.
dosage: DI: 5-20 units SC/IM q4h. Variceal bleeding: 20 units IV over 15 min. Distension: 5 units IM, repeat q3-4h (max 10 units). Roentgenography: 10 units SC/IM 2 hrs before then 10 units IM 30 min before.
precautions: Controlled infusion via device required. Caution in seizure, migraine, asthma, heart failure. Monitor for desire to defecate.
interactions: Amitriptyline, Carbamazepine, and Urea increase effects. Heparin and lithium decrease effects.

name: NITROFURANTOIN
uses: UTI, cystitis, pyelonephritis, postoperative urinary tract infection.
side_effects: Peripheral neuritis, chest pain, leukopenia, hemolytic anemia, GI intolerance, anorexia, brownish urine.
dosage: Adult: 50-100 mg per oral TID/QID. Child: 3-6 mg/kg body weight per oral in four divided doses.
precautions: Avoid long term use in elderly. Caution in gastritis/diabetes. Enters breast milk (discontinue nursing). Do not crush tablets.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, infant under 1-month, GFR <30 ml/min, pregnancy at term (38-42 weeks), hepatic dysfunction.
interactions: Probenecid increases levels. Antagonistic effect with norfloxacin.

name: BETHANECHOL
uses: Urinary retention.
side_effects: Abdominal cramps, belching, bronchial constriction, flushing, urinary urgency.
dosage: Adult: 10-50 mg PO TID/QID. Some may require 50-100 mg PO twice daily. Take 1 hour before or 2 hours after meal.
precautions: Decision required whether to discontinue nursing. Caution in GI disturbances or anastomosis.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, hyperthyroidism, peptic ulcer, asthma, bradycardia, AV Conduction defects, vagotonia, epilepsy, parkinsonism, obstructive pulmonary disease, HTN.
interactions: Ambenonium increases effects. Bethanechol increases and amitriptyline/flavoxate/solifenacin decrease cholinergic transmission.

name: FLAVOXATE
uses: Overactive bladder (OAB).
side_effects: Blurred vision, confusion, constipation, drowsiness, dry mouth, increased ocular tension, vertigo.
dosage: OAB: 100-200 mg PO q6-8hr.
precautions: May impair ability to perform hazardous tasks. Caution in patients with glaucoma. May cause ocular disturbances.
contraindications: Obstructive uropathy, pyloric/duodenal obstruction, ileus, GI bleeding, achalasia.
interactions: Pramlintide increases effects (contraindicated). Flavoxate decreases effects of secretin.

name: MIRABEGRON
uses: Overactive Bladder (OAB) with symptoms of urge urinary incontinence.
side_effects: Elevated BP, dry mouth, nasopharyngitis, UTI, Steven Johnson syndrome.
dosage: Adult: 25 mg PO qDay; may increase to 50 mg PO qDay. Severe renal impairment (Crcl 15-29ml/min): max 25 mg/day. ESRD: not recommended.
precautions: Discontinue nursing. May increase BP. Urinary retention may occur with bladder outlet obstruction. Angioedema reported.
interactions: Mirabegron increases levels of Amitriptyline, Codeine, Metoprolol, and Tramadol (inhibits CYP2D6).

name: OXYBUTYNIN
uses: Overactive bladder (OAB), detrusor overactivity.
side_effects: Dry mouth, constipation, somnolence, nausea.
dosage: OAB: IR 5 mg PO BID/TID (max 20mg); ER 5-10 mg PO daily (max 30mg). Pediatric IR (≥5 yrs): 5 mg PO q12h; ER (≥6 yrs): 5 mg daily (max 20mg).
precautions: Caution in Myasthenia gravis, tachycardia. May aggravate decreased GI motility. May cause memory loss.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, gastric/urinary obstruction, paralytic ileus, severe UC, uncontrolled narrow-angle glaucoma.
interactions: Avoid solid oral dosage forms of Potassium chloride. Pramlintide increases effects (contraindicated).

name: SOLIFENACIN
uses: Overactive bladder (OAB), Urge incontinence.
side_effects: Dry mouth, Constipation, Abdominal Pain, Blurred Vision, Hallucinations.
dosage: OAB: 5 mg PO daily; may increase to 10 mg PO daily.
precautions: Avoid using drug or stop nursing. Monitor for elevated liver enzymes, hyperkalemia, renal impairment, and GERD.
contraindications: Urinary/gastric retention, uncontrolled narrow angle glaucoma, severe hepatic impairment, hypersensitivity.
interactions: Itraconazole increases levels (CYP3A4 inhibition). Caution with Ondansetron and Ketoconazole.

name: TOLTERODIN
uses: Overactive bladder, Urge incontinence.
side_effects: Dry mouth, blurred vision, constipation, dizziness, drowsiness, dyspepsia.
dosage: OAB: IR 2 mg PO q12h; ER 2-4 mg PO once daily.
precautions: Caution in myasthenia gravis and renal impairment. Reduce dose when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Risk of angioedema.
contraindications: Urinary/gastric retention, uncontrolled narrow angle glaucoma, hypersensitivity.
interactions: Carbamazepine decreases levels. Clarithromycin increases levels (CYP3A4 metabolism).

name: ALBUMIN
uses: Acute nephrosis, acute liver failure, ARDS, burns, hypoproteinemia, renal dialysis, hypovolemic shock, hemolytic disease of newborn.
side_effects: Anaphylaxis, CHF, hypervolemia, tachycardia, pulmonary edema, bronchospasm.
dosage: Initial 25 g (5% or 25% solution) IV infusion; repeat q15-30 min if response adequate (max 250 g/48 hr). Daily max: 2 g/kg. Newborns: 1 g/kg prior to exchange transfusion.
precautions: Monitor for hypervolaemia/pulmonary edema. Do not use sterile water as diluent (risk of ARF/hemolysis). Use within 4 hr of opening.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to albumin/blood products, severe anaemia, cardiac failure, renal/post-renal anuria.

name: GLUCOSE
uses: Fluid replacement without significant electrolyte deficit, hypoglycemia, varicose veins.
side_effects: Venous irritation, thrombophlebitis, fluid/electrolyte disturbances, water intoxication (rapid infusion), hyperglycemia.
dosage: Fluid replacement: IV infusion based on clinical/electrolyte monitoring. Hypoglycemia: 25 ml of 50% solution into a large vein.
precautions: Caution in diabetes mellitus; monitor mannitol fluid balance.
contraindications: Anuria, thiamine deficiency, trauma, intracranial hemorrhage, hemodilution, acute ischemic shock, hypophosphatemia, sepsis.

name: POTASSIUM CHLORIDE
uses: Prevention of hypokalaemia, electrolyte imbalance.
side_effects: Abdominal pain, diarrhea, heart toxicity (rapid infusion).
dosage: Prevention (oral): 2–4 g daily in divided doses. Electrolyte imbalance (IV): 1.5 g (20 mmol) in 10 mL mixed with 500 mL NaCl 0.9%, infused slowly over 2-3 hours.
precautions: Overdose can be fatal. Concentration in peripheral IV should not exceed 40 mmol/L. Regularly monitor plasma potassium and ECG.
contraindications: Plasma-potassium concentration >5 mmol/litre, severe renal impairment.

name: RINGER’S LACTATE
uses: Perioperative fluid/electrolyte replacement, hypovolemic shock, metabolic acidosis, peritoneal dialysis.
side_effects: Metabolic alkalosis, edema, tissue necrosis, hypernatremia, hypervolemia.
dosage: Adult: 1 to 3 L/day IV infusion based on clinical/electrolyte monitoring.
precautions: Caution in renal failure, cardiac failure, hypertension, toxemia of pregnancy, corticosteroid therapy.
contraindications: Metabolic or respiratory alkalosis, hypocalcaemia, hypochlorhydria, hypernatremia.

name: SODIUM BICARBONATE
uses: Metabolic acidosis, cardiopulmonary resuscitation, hyperkalemia, muscle spasm.
side_effects: Hypokalemia, metabolic alkalosis, sodium accumulation, edema seizures, lactic acidosis, pulmonary edema, hyperventilation.
dosage: Metabolic acidosis: IV infusion of strong solution (up to 8.4%) or weak solution (up to 1.4%) as appropriate to body base deficit.
precautions: Use caution in cardiac failure, peripheral edema, toxemia of pregnancy. Monitor electrolytes and acid-base status.
contraindications: Metabolic or respiratory alkalosis, hypocalcaemia, hypochlorhydria, hypoventilation, hypoosmolarity.

name: SODIUM CHLORIDE
uses: Extracellular fluid replacement, metabolic alkalosis with fluid loss, mild sodium depletion, diabetic ketoacidosis, sterile irrigation.
side_effects: Sodium accumulation, hyperchloremic acidosis, hypokalemia, edema. Overdose: pulmonary edema, respiratory arrest, coma.
dosage: Replacement: IV, Adult as per requirement. Diabetic ketoacidosis: 500 mL IV infusion (0.9%) over 10-15 minutes; repeat if BP <90 mmHg.
precautions: Auscultate lungs for crepitations. Monitor JVP and right atrial venous pressure in elderly/seriously ill. Caution in toxemia of pregnancy.
contraindications: Congestive heart failure, severe renal impairment, hypertension, peripheral/pulmonary edema, conditions of sodium retention, liver cirrhosis.

name: IPRATROPIUM BROMIDE
uses: COPD, bronchial asthma.
side_effects: Occasionally dry mouth, urinary retention, constipation, tachycardia, and atrial fibrillation.
dosage: Aerosol pressurized inhalation: 20-40 µg, 3-4 times daily. Pediatric (up to 6 years): 20 µg 3 times daily; (6-12 years): 20-40 µg 3 times daily. Inhalation of powder: 40 µg 3-4 times daily.
precautions: Medical supervision necessary for first dose of nebulized solution (risk of paradoxical bronchospasm); protect eyes from drug powder. Child under 12 years: powder inhalation not recommended.
contraindications: Closed angle glaucoma, urinary outflow obstruction, enlarged prostate.
interactions: Anticholinergic action increased with phenothiazines, antihistamines, disopyramide, belladonna. Bronchodilator effect increased with large amounts of tea.

name: BAMBUTEROL
uses: See under SALBUTAMOL.
side_effects: See under SALBUTAMOL.
dosage: Tablet: Initially 10 mg once daily at bed time, increased if necessary after 1-2 weeks to 20 mg once daily.
precautions: Not recommended in children.

name: FORMOTEROL
uses: Asthma, prophylaxis of exercise-induced bronchospasm, nocturnal asthma, COPD.
side_effects: Very rare QT-interval prolongation, dizziness, nausea, pruritus, taste disturbances.
dosage: Aerosol or Dry powder inhalation: Adult 12 µg twice daily; may be increased to 24 µg twice daily in severe airway obstruction.
precautions: N/A

name: SALBUTAMOL
uses: Bronchial asthma, COPD.
side_effects: Muscle cramps, dizziness, headache, muscle tremor, palpitation, ankle edema, hypokalemia.
dosage: Oral: 4 mg 3-4 times daily (Elderly/Sensitive: 2 mg initially). Pediatric (<2 yrs): 100 µg/kg 4 times daily; (2-6 yrs): 1-2 mg 3-4 times daily. Aerosol Inhalation: 100-200 µg (1-2 puffs) up to 3-4 times daily. Inhalation Powder: 200-400 µg 3-4 times daily. Nebulized Solution: 2.5 mg repeated up to 4 times daily.
precautions: Monitor blood glucose (risk of ketoacidosis with IV use). Caution in hyperthyroidism, myocardial insufficiency, arrhythmias, and hypertension.
contraindications: Should not be used to prevent premature labour in cases of pre-eclampsia, placenta previa, or bleeding.
interactions: Concomitant use with corticosteroids or diuretics increases the risk of hypokalemia.

name: SALMETEROL
uses: Reversible airways obstruction (including nocturnal asthma and prevention of exercise-induced bronchospasm), COPD.
side_effects: Headache, dizziness, tachycardia, palpitation, ventricular arrhythmias, cough.
dosage: Aerosol or Dry powder inhalation (Adult): 50 µg (2 puffs or 1 blister) twice daily. Up to 100 µg twice daily in severe airway obstruction. Pediatric (>4 yrs): 50 µg twice daily.
precautions: Should not be used in children as monotherapy for asthma; use only in combination with inhaled steroid. Not recommended for children under 4 years.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, tachyarrhythmias, severe cardiac disease, pregnancy, breastfeeding, cardiac disorders, hyperthyroidism, diabetes, hypertension, close angle glaucoma, seizure, acute asthma.

name: TERBUTALINE SULFATE
uses: See under SALBUTAMOL.
side_effects: See under SALBUTAMOL.
dosage: Oral: 2.5-5 mg 2-3 times daily; Child: 0.1 µg/kg 3 times daily. SC/IM/Slow IV: 250-500 µg up to 4 times daily. Continuous IV Infusion: 1.5-5 µg/minute for 8-10 hours. Aerosol inhalation: 250-500 µg (1-2 puffs) 3-4 times daily.
precautions: Tolerance develops in long-term therapy; monitor for rebound bronchospasm.
interactions: Increases hypertensive crisis with MAOIs. Decreases action of beta-blockers. Effect increased with large amounts of green tea.

name: BECLOMETHASONE DIPROPIONATE
uses: Chronic asthma (prophylaxis).
side_effects: Oropharyngeal candidiasis, cough, dysphonia, adrenal suppression, growth retardation in children, impaired bone metabolism, glaucoma, cataract.
dosage: Aerosol Inhalation (Standard-dose): Adult 200 µg twice daily or 100 µg 3-4 times daily. Child: 50-100 µg 2-4 times daily. Aerosol Inhalation (High-dose): Adult 500 µg twice daily or 250 µg 4 times daily.
precautions: Not for relief of acute symptoms. Monitor height of children receiving prolonged treatment; review therapy if growth is slowed.
contraindications: Untreated fungal infection, active or quiescent tuberculosis.

name: BUDESONIDE
uses: Bronchial asthma.
side_effects: Oropharyngeal candidiasis, cough, adrenal suppression (higher doses), growth retardation (in children), glaucoma.
dosage: Inhalation Powder: 0.2-1.6 mg daily in 2 divided doses. Child (<12 yrs): 200-800 µg daily in 2 divided doses. Nebulized Suspension: 1-2 mg twice daily. Child (3 mo - 12 yrs): 0.5-1 mg twice daily.
precautions: Caution in quiescent tuberculosis, osteoporosis, and diabetes. Maintain good oral hygiene. Avoid breastfeeding.
interactions: Corticosteroids antagonize the hypotensive effect of ACE inhibitors, alpha-blockers, ARBs, and calcium channel blockers.

name: HYDROCORTISONE
uses: Inflammatory and allergic disorder, asthma, immunosuppression, nephritic syndrome, rheumatic disease, neoplastic disease, adrenal insufficiency.
side_effects: Euphoria, depression, seizure, vertigo, peptic ulceration, thromboembolism, hypertension, glaucoma, cataracts.
dosage: Adult: Slow IV or infusion, 100-500 mg TDS or QID. Child (up to 1 yr): 25 mg daily; (1-5 yr): 50 mg daily; (5-12 yr): 100 mg daily. Local Ointment: 1-2 times daily.
precautions: Avoid live virus vaccines. Long-term therapy requires gradual withdrawal to avoid adrenal crisis.
contraindications: Active untreated infectious disease (except tuberculous meningitis), lactation, peptic ulcer, diabetes mellitus, psychiatric disease, undiagnosed fever.
interactions: Hypokalemia with furosemide, HCTZ, or piperacillin. Reduces action of insulin and oral hypoglycemics.

name: MONTELUKAST
uses: Chronic asthma in adults and children, seasonal allergic rhinitis, bronchospasm prophylaxis.
side_effects: Dizziness, fatigue, headache, behavior change, hallucinations, seizures, Churg-Strauss syndrome.
dosage: Tablet (Adult/Child >15 yr): 10 mg daily in PM. Child (6-14 yr): 5 mg chewable tablet daily in PM. Child (2-5 yr): 1 packet (4 mg) granules daily in PM.
precautions: Alcohol consumption, severe hepatic disease, phenylketonuria, suicidal ideation, depression.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, children <6 yrs (for acute asthma), acute attack of asthma.

name: ZAFIRLUKAST
uses: Prophylaxis and chronic treatment of asthma in adults/children >5yr, allergic rhinitis.
side_effects: Headache, dizziness, nausea, diarrhea, abdominal pain, vomiting, hepatic failure, hepatitis, angioedema.
dosage: Adult and Child (>12 yr): 20 mg twice daily. Child (5-11 yr): 10 mg twice daily.
precautions: Monitor for symptoms of Churg-Strauss syndrome. Liver function test recommended.

name: SODIUM CROMOGLYCATE
uses: Prophylaxis of asthma, allergic rhinitis, allergic conjunctivitis.
side_effects: Throat irritation and cough, nasal congestion, headache, dizziness, arthralgia, rashes, bronchospasm.
dosage: Inhalation of powder (Adult/Child): 20 mg 4 times daily, increased up to 8 times daily in severe cases.
precautions: Caution in cardiac, hepatic, and renal diseases. Use in old age and children.

name: EPHEDRINE HYDROCHLORIDE
uses: Reversible airways obstruction.
side_effects: Arrhythmias, insomnia, tremor, tachycardia.
dosage: Tablet (Adult): 15-60 mg 3 times daily. Child: 3 times daily; (up to 1 yr): 7.5 mg; (1-5 yr): 15 mg; (6-12 yr): 30 mg.
precautions: Use with caution in hypertension, severe renal impairment, and prostate hypertrophy.

name: AMINOPHYLLINE
uses: Bronchial asthma, COPD, Neonatal apnea.
side_effects: Headache, dizziness, extra systoles, sinus tachycardia, anorexia, nervousness, tremor.
dosage: Oral: 100-300 mg three times a day. Injection: IV loading dose 6 mg/kg over 20-30 minutes, then maintenance 0.4 to 0.7 mg/kg/hour. Child loading dose: IV 5-6 mg/kg.
precautions: Therapeutic dose is near the toxic dose. Give carefully. Do not give IM or SC. Not for children under one year except in apnea of prematurity.
interactions: Additive side effects with sympathomimetics. Elevated serum levels with cimetidine, beta-blockers, erythromycin, allopurinol, or oral contraceptives.

name: DOXOFYLLINE
uses: Asthma, COPD.
side_effects: Headache, nausea, vomiting, sleeplessness, dizziness.
dosage: Adult: 400 mg once or twice daily. Children: 12 mg/kg/day.
precautions: Use with caution in hypoxemia, hyperthyroidism, liver disease, renal disease, and history of peptic ulcer.
interactions: Should not be administered with other xanthine derivatives or caffeine-containing products.

name: THEOPHYLLINE
uses: COPD, Bronchial asthma, Nocturnal asthma.
side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, GI upset, headache, dizziness, convulsion.
dosage: Adult: 200 mg bid, can increase to 300 mg bid. Neonatal apnea: Loading PO 5 mg/kg, maintenance 3-6 mg/kg/day. Bronchospasm: PO 12-14 mg/kg/day (Max 300 mg/day).
precautions: Close monitoring required as the effective dose is very close to the toxic dose.
interactions: Do not combine with ciprofloxacin, corticosteroids, erythromycin, or cimetidine (increases levels). Do not combine with carbamazepine, phenytoin, or barbiturates (decreases levels).

name: CODEINE PHOSPHATE
uses: Non-productive cough, pain.
side_effects: Nausea, constipation, drowsiness, confusion, blurred vision, hypotension, bradycardia, respiratory depression (large doses).
dosage: Pain: 30-60 mg every 4 hours (Max 240 mg daily). Child (1-12 yrs): 0.5-1 mg/kg every 6 hours. Cough: 15-30 mg 3-4 times daily. Child (5-12 yrs): 1-1.5 mg/kg 4 times daily.
precautions: Use cautiously in severe prostatic hypertrophy and hepatic disease. Potential for physical dependence on prolonged use.
contraindications: Asthmatics, patients with decreased respiratory reserve, history of drug abuse/drug-seeking behavior.
interactions: Extreme caution with MAO inhibitors. Additive CNS depression with alcohol, antidepressants, antihistamines, sedatives.

name: DEXTROMETHORPHAN
uses: Non-productive cough.
side_effects: Dizziness, sedation, nausea.
dosage: Syrup: 10-20 mg every 4-8 hours. Child (6-12 yrs): 5-10 mg every 4-8 hours (Max 60 mg/24h). Child (2-6 yrs): 2.5-5 mg every 4 hours (Max 30 mg/24h).
precautions: Not for children under four years of age. Caution in patients with history of drug abuse.
contraindications: Allergy to dextromethorphan, patients taking MAOIs or SSRIs, chronic productive cough.
interactions: Use with MAOIs may cause serotonin syndrome. CNS depression increased with alcohol, opioids, amiodarone. Quinidine may increase blood levels.

name: NOSCAPINE
uses: Non-productive cough.
side_effects: Drowsiness, nausea, bronchospasm (large doses), hypertension.
dosage: Linctus (Adult): 15-30 mg daily. Child (6-12 yr): 15 mg 3 times daily. Infant (2-6 yr): 7.5 mg 3 times daily.
precautions: N/A

name: PHOLCODINE
uses: Non-productive cough.
side_effects: Dizziness, loss of attention, swelling of face/neck, difficulty in breathing.
dosage: Adult: 5-10 ml 3-4 times daily. Child (1-2 yr): 2.5-5 ml; (2-5 yr): 5 ml; (5-12 yr): 5-10 ml.
precautions: Acts for 12 hours. Practically no analgesic or addictive property.
contraindications: Chronic lung diseases, liver or kidney failure, productive cough, pregnancy, breastfeeding, asthma, children under 5 years.
interactions: Additive depressant effects with other CNS depressants.

name: BROMHEXINE
uses: Reduction of sputum viscosity in COPD.
side_effects: Gastrointestinal side effects, transient rise in serum aminotransferase, headache, vertigo, sweating.
dosage: Oral: 8-16 mg 3 times daily. Child (2-6 yr): 8 mg 2-3 times daily. Child (6-12 yr): 4-8 mg per dose 3 times daily.
precautions: Caution in patients with history of gastric ulceration (may disrupt mucosal barrier) and in pregnancy/breastfeeding.
contraindications: Not recommended for infants < 1 year, severe hepatic/renal impairment.
interactions: Should not be given with paracetamol (increased risk of hepatitis).

name: CARBOCYSTEINE
uses: Reduction of sputum viscosity in COPD.
side_effects: Skin rashes, occasional gastrointestinal irritation.
dosage: Adult: 750 mg 3 times daily initially, then 1.5 g daily in divided doses. Child (2-5 yr): 200-500 mg daily. Child (6-12 yr): 300-750 mg daily.
precautions: Caution in children under 2 years and patients with history of peptic ulceration.

name: ACETYL CYSTEINE
uses: Mucolytic, management of paracetamol (acetaminophen) overdose.
side_effects: Stomatitis, nausea, vomiting, fever, rhinorrhea, drowsiness, clamminess, chest tightness.
dosage: Nebulized: 1-10 mL of 20% solution or 2-20 mL of 10% solution every 2-6 hours.
precautions: N/A

name: PHENYLEPHRINE
uses: Nasal congestion associated with rhinitis, common cold, and sinusitis.
side_effects: Increased heart rate, palpitation, tremors, ventricular premature contractions, hypertension.
dosage: Oral: 5 mg 3-4 times a day. Nasal Spray: Child (1-6 yr) 1-2 drops 0.01%; (6-12 yr) 1-2 drops 0.25%; (>12 yr) 0.25% or 0.5%.
precautions: Caution in patients with diabetes, hypertension, ischemic heart disease, hepatic/renal impairment. Rinse dropper to prevent contamination.

name: PSEUDOEPHEDRINE
uses: Nasal congestion associated with rhinitis, common cold, sinusitis, otic inflammation.
side_effects: Nervousness, restlessness, dizziness, insomnia, headache, drowsiness, lightheadedness, nausea.
dosage: Tablet (Adult): 60 mg 3-4 times daily. Child: 4 mg/kg/day per oral in 3-4 divided doses.
precautions: Use cautiously in patients with prostatic hypertrophy, ischemic heart disease, glaucoma, and diabetes.
interactions: Do not use with MAOIs or tricyclics (risk of hypertensive crisis).

name: CAFFEINE CITRATE
uses: Neonatal apnea in preterm infants.
side_effects: Lethargy (withdrawal sign), irritability, excessive CNS stimulation, tachycardia, hyperglycemia/hypoglycemia, hemorrhage, lung edema, renal failure.
dosage: Oral or IV: Loading dose 20-25 mg/kg, then 5-10 mg/kg once daily starting 24 hours later; continue for 4-5 days after cessation of apnea.
precautions: Monitor for CNS stimulation and tachycardia (toxicity).
contraindications: Cardiovascular disorders, hepatic or renal impairment.

name: CARBAMAZEPINE
uses: Treatment of tonic-clonic, mixed and complex partial seizures (not used in absence seizures and myoclonic seizure), management of pain in trigeminal neuralgia or diabetic neuropathy, acute mania.
side_effects: Ataxia, drowsiness, CHF, renal damage, agranulocytosis, dilutional hyponatremia, exfoliative dermatitis, decreased platelets, increased risk of lupus.
dosage: Anticonvulsant: PO (adults) 200mg BD, increase by 200mg/day to 600-1200mg/day (max 1g/day in 12-15 year olds). Antineuralgic: 100mg BD or 50mg QID, increase to 400-800mg/day. Children 6-12yr: 100mg BD, increase by 100mg weekly. Children <6yr: 10-20mg/kg/day.
precautions: Use cautiously in cardiac/hepatic disease, renal failure, glaucoma. Monitor for behavioral changes and suicidal ideation.
contraindications: Bone marrow suppression, administration of MAO-I within last 14 days, jaundice, hepatitis.
interactions: Concurrent MAO-I use may result in hyperpyrexia and death. Induces hepatic enzymes; promotes its own metabolism and that of phenobarbital, phenytoin, oral contraceptives.
pregnancy_category: Risk of fetal carbamazepine syndrome (esp. 1st trimester).

name: CLOBAZAM
uses: Adjunct in epilepsy, anxiety.
side_effects: Somnolence, sedation, pyrexia, URTI.
dosage: Epilepsy: 20-30 mg daily (max 60mg); child >3yrs: not more than half adult dose. Anxiety: 20-30 mg daily in divided doses or single dose at bedtime (max 60mg in hospitalized patients); elderly 10-20 mg daily.
precautions: Do not stop the drug abruptly.

name: CLONAZEPAM
uses: Status epilepticus, all types of epilepsy, anxiety disorder.
side_effects: Suicidal thoughts, dizziness, drowsiness, ataxia, muscle hypotonia, salivary/bronchial hypertension in infants, sexual dysfunction, dependence.
dosage: Seizures: 1.5 mg divided into 3 doses, raise by 0.5 mg every 3 days. Panic: 1 mg/day (max 4 mg/day).
precautions: Do not stop the drug abruptly.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, severe liver diseases, respiratory depression, acute pulmonary insufficiency.
interactions: With verapamil, diltiazem: risk of AV block.

name: DIAZEPAM
uses: Adjunct in management of anxiety disorder, prior to cardioversion, preoperative sedation, conscious sedation, status epilepticus, skeletal muscle relaxant, alcohol withdrawal.
side_effects: Apnea, hypotension, thrombophlebitis, dizziness, drowsiness, lethargy, ataxia, dependence.
dosage: IV injection: 10-20 mg at 2.5 mg per 30 sec; repeat if necessary after 30-60 min; IV infusion max 3mg/kg over 24 hrs. Children: 200-300 μg/kg.
precautions: Severe renal/hepatic impairment. Facilities for mechanical ventilation must be available. Administer IV slowly to reduce danger of apnea and hypotension.
contraindications: Acute alcohol intoxication, myasthenia gravis, acute narrow angle glaucoma, sleep apnea, children <6 months.
interactions: Concomitant use with opioids and/or other CNS depressants may result in profound respiratory depression.

name: GABAPENTIN
uses: Adjunct treatment of partial seizures, bipolar affective disorder (BPAD), post-herpetic neuralgia, neuropathic pain.
side_effects: Ataxia, dizziness, drowsiness, fatigue, somnolence, diplopia, nystagmus, tremor, suicidal thoughts.
dosage: Epilepsy: 300mg day 1, 300mg BD day 2, 300mg TID day 3, increase to max 2.4 g/day. Child (6-12yr): 10-35 mg/kg daily. Maintenance: 900 mg daily.
precautions: Safety not established in children <3yrs or pregnant women.
contraindications: Increased blood CPK levels and rhabdomyolysis.
interactions: Antacids may decrease absorption. Increased risk of CNS depression with other CNS depressants.

name: LACOSAMIDE
uses: Monotherapy or adjunctive treatment of focal seizures with or without secondary generalization.
side_effects: Abnormal gait, tremor, impaired coordination, nystagmus, blurred vision, headache, agitation, cardiac arrhythmias.
dosage: Monotherapy: 100 mg PO/IV 12hrly initially, increase at weekly intervals to 150-200 mg BID (300-400 mg/day). Adjunctive: Initial 50 mg PO/IV 12hrly.
precautions: Conduction problems, elderly, severe cardiac disease. Caution in renal/hepatic impairment.

name: LAMOTRIGINE
uses: Partial, secondarily generalized tonic-clonic seizures, Lennox-Gastaut syndrome, bipolar affective disorder.
side_effects: Dizziness, ataxia, blurred or double vision, nausea, vomiting, rash, Stevens-Johnson syndrome.
dosage: Monotherapy: 25mg daily initially, increased to 100-200mg maintenance. Adjunct with valproate: initially 25mg every other day. Adjunct with carbamazepine: initially 50mg/day.
precautions: Cardiac/renal/hepatic disease, severe depression, blood dyscrasias.

name: LEVETIRACETAM
uses: Monotherapy or adjunctive therapy of focal seizures, myoclonic seizures, and tonic-clonic seizures.
side_effects: Abdominal pain, anorexia, agitation, anxiety, convulsion, alopecia, amnesia, diplopia, leucopenia, thrombocytopenia, suicidal ideation.
dosage: N/A (Refer to primary entry in formulary for specific titration).
precautions: Monitor carefully during pregnancy. Cautions in hepatic and renal impairment; monitor renal function regularly.

name: OXCARBAZEPINE
uses: Monotherapy or adjunctive therapy of partial seizures.
side_effects: Suicidal thoughts, dizziness, diplopia, nystagmus, ataxia, abnormal gait, tremor, SJS.
dosage: Initial 300 mg BD, increase to 0.6-2.4 g daily in divided doses. Child >6yr: 8-10mg/kg daily in 2 divided doses.
precautions: Renal impairment. Monitor for behavior changes associated with suicidal thoughts. Monitor for hyponatremia.
interactions: May render oral contraceptives ineffective. Increased CNS depression with CNS depressants.

name: PHENOBARBITAL
uses: Anti-convulsant in tonic-clonic, partial and febrile seizures; pre-operative sedative; hypnotic (short term).
side_effects: Ataxia, dizziness, nystagmus, impairment in cognitive function, respiratory depression, hypotension, angioedema, serum sickness.
dosage: Status epilepticus: 15-18 mg/kg. Maintenance (Adults): 1-3mg/kg/day. Sedation (Adult): 30-120 mg/day in 2-3 divided doses. Hypnotic: 100-300 mg at bedtime.
precautions: Hepatic/renal dysfunction; history of suicide or drug abuse. Monitoring of drug levels in plasma. Be aware of risk of fall among elderly and children.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, porphyria, severe hepatic impairment, COPD, dyspnea, pregnancy and lactation.
interactions: Induces hepatic microsomal enzymes; decreases plasma concentrations of carbamazepine, warfarin, OCPs, and corticosteroids.
pregnancy_category: Chronic use results in drug dependency in infant; risk of fetal malformations and coagulation defects.

name: PHENYTOIN
uses: All forms of epilepsy (except absence, myoclonic, drug-induced), trigeminal neuralgia.
side_effects: Suicidal thoughts, agranulocytosis, aplastic anemia, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, gingival hyperplasia, hirsutism.
dosage: Oral: initially 3-4 mg/kg or 150-300mg daily; child 4-8 mg/kg daily. Status epilepticus: Slow IV injection 15mg/kg at max 50mg/min.
precautions: Pharmacokinetic variability; needs therapeutic drug level monitoring. Monitor for suicidal thoughts and gingival hypertrophy. Not recommended by IM injection.
interactions: Metabolism inhibited by isoniazid, chloramphenicol, sulfonamides. Inducers like carbamazepine/alcohol result in low plasma levels. Induces metabolism of OCPs.

name: TOPIRAMATE
uses: Monotherapy or adjunctive treatment of generalized tonic-clonic or focal seizures, Lennox-Gastaut syndrome, migraine prophylaxis, substance dependence.
side_effects: Anxiety, cognitive impairment, sleep disturbance, GI distress, paraesthesia, speech disorder.
dosage: N/A (Refer to primary entry for specific titration).
precautions: Risk of metabolic acidosis and nephrolithiasis; ensure adequate hydration.

name: VALPROIC ACID
uses: All forms of epilepsy, bipolar affective disorder.
side_effects: Suicidal thoughts, tremor, gastric irritation, weight gain, thrombocytopenia, transient hair loss, drug induced hepatitis.
dosage: Initial 600 mg daily; increase by 200 mg/day every 3 days (max 2.5 g/day). Child up to 20 kg: 20 mg/kg daily. IV initiation: 400-800 mg (up to 10 mg/kg).
precautions: Monitor hepatic function tests before treatment and every 2 months for first six months.
interactions: Increased risk of bleeding with warfarin.

name: AMANTADINE
uses: Parkinsonism, post-herpetic neuralgia.
side_effects: Restlessness, insomnia, excitement, livedo reticularis, peripheral edema, postural hypotension.
dosage: 100mg daily, increase after 1 week to 100mg twice daily (max 400mg daily).
precautions: In patients with cardiac, hepatic or renal disease. Watch for confusion or mottling of skin.
interactions: Increases anticholinergic response of atropine. Metoclopramide and phenothiazines decrease effect.

name: BENZTROPINE
uses: Parkinsonism, EPS associated with neuroleptic drugs, acute dystonic reactions, hypersalivation.
side_effects: Hallucinations, delirium, palpitation, tachycardia, paralytic ileus, hyperthermia, heat stroke.
dosage: 0.5-1 mg at bedtime, increase by 0.5 mg q5-6 days (max 6mg/day).
precautions: Pregnancy, renal/hepatic disease, myasthenia gravis.
contraindications: Children <3yrs, closed angle glaucoma, dementia, tardive dyskinesia, GI/GU obstruction, peptic ulcer, prostrate hypertrophy.
interactions: Amantadine, TCAs, and antihistamines increase effects. Antacids decrease absorption.

name: BROMOCRIPTINE
uses: Parkinsonism, hyperprolactinemia, galactorrhoea, infertility, acromegaly.
side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, postural hypotension, altered taste, cardiac arrhythmia, psychosis.
dosage: Parkinsonism: 1-1.25 mg OD at bedtime (1st week), increase to 7.5-30 mg/day maintenance.
precautions: History of psychosis, peptic ulcer, DM. Ability to drive may be impaired.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to ergot alkaloids, breast carcinoma, severe ischemic heart disease, uncontrolled HTN.
interactions: May result in failure of OCPs. Disulfiram-like reaction with alcohol.

name: ENTACAPONE
uses: Adjunct in Parkinson’s disease with ‘end-of-dose’ motor fluctuations.
side_effects: Abnormal dreams, dyskinesia, dystonia, ischaemic heart disease.
dosage: Oral, adult: 200 mg with each dose of levodopa (max 2 g/day).
precautions: Avoid in pregnancy; avoid in breastfeeding (present in milk).
contraindications: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome, non-traumatic rhabdomyolysis, phaeochromocytoma, hepatic failure.
interactions: Avoid iron-containing products at the same time of day.

name: LEVODOPA AND CARBIDOPA
uses: Parkinsonism.
side_effects: Altered taste, cardiac arrhythmia, angina, delusion, nightmares.
dosage: 100mg levodopa + 25mg carbidopa TID before meal. Increase by 1 tab every 1-2 days (max 8 tabs/day).
precautions: MI, cerebrovascular accidents. Monitor skin lesions for malignant melanoma.
contraindications: Acute angle closure glaucoma, psychotic illness, malignant melanoma.
interactions: Pyridoxine promotes metabolism. Phenothiazines and butyrophenones antagonize effects.

name: PRAMIPEXOLE
uses: Parkinson’s disease, restless leg syndrome.
side_effects: Sudden onset of sleep, dyskinesia, visual disturbances, impulse control disorders (pathological gambling, hypersexuality).
dosage: N/A (Refer to primary entry in formulary for specific titration).
precautions: Psychotic disorders, risk of visual disorders (ophthalmological testing recommended).
contraindications: Severe cardiovascular disease. Avoid in breast feeding.
pregnancy_category: Use in pregnancy only if potential benefit outweighs risk.

name: RASAGILINE
uses: Parkinson’s disease, adjunct for ’end-of-dose’ fluctuations.
side_effects: Weight loss, vertigo, skin carcinoma.
dosage: Oral, adult: 1 mg daily.
precautions: Avoid abrupt withdrawal.
interactions: May cause serotonin syndrome when used with antidepressants.

name: ROPINIROLE
uses: Parkinson’s disease.
side_effects: Gastro-oesophageal reflux, sudden onset sleep, impulse control disorders.
dosage: N/A (Refer to primary entry for specific titration).
precautions: Monitor blood pressure (risk of hypotension). Monitor for impulsive behavior.
pregnancy_category: Avoid in pregnancy unless benefit outweighs risk (toxicity in animal studies).

name: SELEGILINE HYDROCHLORIDE
uses: Parkinson’s disease.
side_effects: Movement disorders, impaired balance, mouth ulcers, stomatitis.
dosage: Tablet: 5 mg daily, increase to 10 mg daily. Lyophilisate: 1.25 mg daily before breakfast.
precautions: Caution in renal and hepatic impairment. Lyophilisates should be allowed to dissolve on tongue.
contraindications: Active duodenal or gastric ulceration, avoid in postural hypotension (with levodopa).
interactions: Increased risk of serotonin syndrome with SSRIs.

name: TRIHEXYPHENIDYL HYDROCHLORIDE (BENZHEXOL)
uses: Drug induced parkinsonism.
side_effects: Atropine like effects (dry mouth, constipation, impaired vision).
dosage: 1 mg daily, gradually increased to maintenance 5-15mg daily in 3-4 divided doses.
precautions: Not recommended in children. Monitor fluid intake and urine output ratio.

name: ERGOTAMINE TARTARATE
uses: Acute attack of migraine unresponsive to analgesics; menopausal hot flushes.
side_effects: Arterial spasm, intermittent claudication, neck stiffness, numbness or tingling.
dosage: Migraine: 2mg sublingual then 1.2mg every 30mins (max 6mg/day, 10mg/week). Menopausal flushes: 0.6mg PO q12h.
precautions: Sepsis, malnutrition, impaired renal/hepatic function. Should be initiated at first sign of vascular headache.
contraindications: PVD, CAD, Raynaud’s disease, pregnancy/lactation, severe HTN. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors (ritonavir, macrolides, antifungals).
interactions: CYP3A4 inhibitors may produce life-threatening peripheral ischemia.

name: RIZATRIPTAN
uses: Acute migraine.
side_effects: Decreased alertness, drowsiness, pharyngeal discomfort.
dosage: Oral, adult: 10 mg as soon as possible, follow with 10 mg after 2 hours if required (max 20 mg/day).
precautions: Hepatic/renal impairment, pregnancy. Drowsiness may affect performance of skilled tasks.
contraindications: Severe hypertension, coronary vasospasm, ischaemic heart disease, peripheral vascular disease, history of MI/TIA/CVA.
interactions: May enhance toxic effects of serotonin modulators.
pregnancy_category: Present in milk; withhold breast-feeding for 24 hours.

name: SUMATRIPTAN
uses: Acute migraine attacks, cluster headache.
side_effects: Injection site reaction, jaw or neck tightness, diaphoresis.
dosage: Oral: 50-100 mg. SC injection: 6 mg (max 12 mg in 24 hours). Cluster headache: 6mg SC; may repeat in > 1hr.
precautions: Should not be given intravenously (may cause vasospasm). Avoid breast feeding for 8-12 hrs after administration.
contraindications: Ischemic cardiac/cerebrovascular/peripheral vascular syndromes, WPW syndrome, uncontrolled HTN, use within 2 weeks of MAO-A inhibitors.

name: FLUNARIZINE
uses: Migraine prophylaxis.
side_effects: Drowsiness, extrapyramidal effects, depression in elderly, weight gain, galactorrhea.
dosage: Oral, adult: 10-20 mg once daily; child: 5 mg once daily.
precautions: May cause CNS depression. Monitor for extrapyramidal symptoms.
contraindications: Depression, acute phase of stroke, extrapyramidal symptoms or Parkinson’s disease.
interactions: Effects of alcohol and sedating drugs can be increased.

name: PREGABALIN
uses: Peripheral and central neuropathic pain, adjunct for focal seizures, generalized anxiety disorder.
side_effects: Appetite changes, weight gain, visual field defects, impaired memory, speech disorder.
dosage: Neuropathic pain: initially 150 mg daily, increase to 600 mg. Focal seizures: initially 25 mg twice daily. GAD: initially 150 mg daily.
precautions: Conditions that may precipitate encephalopathy, severe CHF, renal impairment. Avoid abrupt withdrawal (taper over 1 week).
interactions: Increased CNS depression if taken with alcohol.

name: BUPRENORPHINE
uses: Perioperative analgesia; moderate to severe pain; withdrawing opioid addicts; chronic non-malignant pain.
side_effects: See under Morphine; less abuse potential than Morphine.
dosage: IM/Slow IV: 300-600 µg every 6-8hrs. Sublingual tablet: 200-400 µg every 8hrs.
precautions: Controlled substance; potential for addiction. Keep naloxone on hand.
contraindications: Drug overdose can result in coma/death.

name: CODEINE PHOSPHATE
uses: Management of mild to moderate pain, headache, non-productive cough, opioid withdrawal.
side_effects: Constipation, sedation, nausea/vomiting; less liable than morphine to produce tolerance/dependence.
dosage: Pain: 30-60mg 3-4 times a day.
precautions: BPH, head trauma, dependence. Breastfeeding children <1 year. Protected from light.
contraindications: Respiratory depression, obstructive airway disease, acute asthma attack, paralytic ileus.

name: METHADONE HYDROCHLORIDE
uses: Severe pain, adjunct in treatment of opioid dependence, cough in terminal disease.
side_effects: See under Morphine.
dosage: Opioid dependence: initially 10-40mg daily, increase by max 10mg daily to usual range 60-120 mg.
precautions: Controlled substance; potential for addiction. Not recommended to children.
interactions: Rifampicin and Phenytoin accelerate metabolism (can precipitate withdrawal).

name: MORPHINE SULPHATE
uses: Severe pain, MI, acute pulmonary edema, adjunct during major surgery and post-operative analgesia.
side_effects: Classic triad: pinpoint pupil, respiratory depression, coma. Mental clouding, urinary retention, apnoea in newborn.
dosage: Acute pain (SC/IM): 10mg every 4 hours. MI (IV): 2mg/min, 10mg followed by further 5-10mg.
precautions: Elderly/debilitated, dependence, convulsive disorders. Obtain baseline respiratory rate and pupil size. Bedside rails advisable.
contraindications: Respiratory insufficiency, bronchial asthma, undiagnosed acute abdominal pain, head injury.

name: PETHIDINE HYDROCHLORIDE (MEPERIDINE)
uses: Moderate to severe pain and for obstetric analgesia.
side_effects: Similar to morphine; more severe nausea and hypotension. Equianalgesic doses produce similar respiratory depression.
dosage: PO: 50-150mg every 4 hours. IM/SC: 25-100mg. Obstetrical analgesia: 50-100mg (max 400mg in 24 hours).
precautions: May cause life-threatening respiratory depression. Potential for addiction and abuse.
interactions: With MAO-I may cause serious (possibly fatal) reaction.

name: TRAMADOL HYDROCHLORIDE
uses: Moderate pain, adjunct in chronic pain.
side_effects: Seizures, somnolence, nausea.
dosage: Oral: 50-100mg q4h (total >400mg not usually required). IM/IV/Infusion: 50-100mg every 4-6hrs.
precautions: Do not confuse with Toradol (Ketorolac). Monitor for seizure.
interactions: CNS depressants (increased risk); B-Lactam antibiotics (increased seizure risk).

name: NALOXONE
uses: Opioid overdose (coma and respiratory depression), neonatal asphyxia, postoperative opioid reversal.
side_effects: Sweating, withdrawal symptoms in opioid abusers.
dosage: Adult IV: 0.4-2mg repeated at 2-3 min intervals (max 10mg). Child: 10μg/kg.
precautions: Physical dependence on opioids (may precipitate acute withdrawal).
interactions: Antagonizes the effects of opioid analgesics.

name: NALTREXONE
uses: Opioid dependence, alcohol dependence, herpetic neuralgia, Crohn’s disease in children.
side_effects: Injection site reaction, decreased appetite, arthralgia.
dosage: Chronic opioid dependence: PO 25mg day 1, then 50mg once daily. IM: 380mg every 4 weeks.
precautions: Risk of hepatotoxicity with increasing doses. Discontinue if signs of acute hepatitis develop.
contraindications: Currently dependent on opioids; acute hepatitis or liver failure.

name: PENTAZOCINE
uses: Moderate to severe pain, preoperative/pre-anesthetic supplement.
side_effects: Pulmonary artery hypertension, tolerance, dependence.
dosage: Oral: 50mg q3-4h. Severe pain: 45-60mg IM/IV q3-4h.
precautions: Use cautiously in acute asthma, bradycardia. May produce acute withdrawal symptoms in opioid-dependent users.
contraindications: Toxin-mediated diarrhea, Pseudomonas enterocolitis, respiratory depression, MI.

name: MIRTAZAPINE
uses: Major depression, PTSD (off label), insomnia (off label).
side_effects: Somnolence, xerostomia, weight gain, reversible agranulocytosis.
dosage: Depression (Adult): 15 mg PO HS; increase to max 60 mg HS. Geriatric: 7.5 mg PO HS.
precautions: Start slowly in hepatic/renal dysfunction. Discontinue if neutropenia/agranulocytosis occur.
interactions: Do not use within 14 days of MAOI.

name: FLUOXETINE
uses: Major depression, OCD, bulimia nervosa, panic disorder.
side_effects: Insomnia, sexual dysfunction, taste disturbances, serotonin syndrome.
dosage: Adult Depression/OCD: Initial 20 mg PO daily; max 80 mg/day. Bulimia: 60 mg once daily.
precautions: Monitor closely for suicidal tendencies. Discontinue if symptomatic hyponatremia occurs.
interactions: Do not use with MAO inhibitors (within 14 days). Do not use with linezolid or pimozide.

name: LITHIUM
uses: Prophylaxis and treatment of mania, prophylaxis of bipolar disorder, hyperthyroidism.
side_effects: Fine tremor, polydipsia, weight gain, acne, oedema.
dosage: Up to 1.5 g daily in single or divided doses; adjusted by plasma concentration.
precautions: Regularly monitor serum lithium levels and thyroid/renal function. Lithium crosses placenta.
contraindications: Hypothyroidism, sick sinus syndrome, heart blocks, renal diseases.
interactions: NSAIDs (ibuprofen, diclofenac) and ACE inhibitors increase serum concentrations by reducing excretion.
pregnancy_category: Use during pregnancy only in life-threatening situations.

name: ALPRAZOLAM
uses: Anxiety disorders, agoraphobia, panic disorders, depression.
side_effects: Confusion, physical dependence, changes in libido.
dosage: 0.25 to 0.5 mg TID; max total daily 3 mg. Elderly: 0.25 mg BID/TID.
precautions: Monitor respiratory function. Watch for signs of tolerance and dependence.
contraindications: Respiratory depression, severe hepatic impairment, angle closure glaucoma.
interactions: Increases sedative effect of opioid analgesics.

name: ZOLPIDEM
uses: Insomnia.
side_effects: Nightmares, asthenia, memory disturbances, ataxia.
dosage: 10 mg at bedtime; elderly 5 mg.
precautions: Use with caution in depression.
contraindications: Children, severe hepatic/pulmonary insufficiency, myasthenia gravis, obstructive sleep apnea.

name: HALOTHANE
uses: Induction and maintenance of general anaesthesia
side_effects: Nausea and vomiting, acidosis, dehydration and fever in children (may predispose to convulsions under ether anaesthesia). May cause excessive bleeding during caesarean section and post-partum haemorrhage.
dosage: Induction: Done using a special calibrated vaporizer, increased gradually to 2-4% in oxygen or nitrous oxide-oxygen; child: 1.5-2%. Maintenance: 0.5-2%.
precautions: Careful anaesthetic history should be taken to determine previous exposure and previous reaction to halothane.
contraindications: History of unexplained jaundice or pyrexia in a patient following exposure to halothane. Avoid repeated exposure to halothane in less than three months.
interactions: With adrenaline, heart is sensitized to the actions of catecholamines.

name: ISOFLURANE
uses: Induction and maintenance of general anesthesia (usually not preferred for induction due to ether-like odor)
side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, shivering, dose-dependent hypotension, arrhythmia, respiratory depression (rare), risk of perioperative hyperkalemia and malignant hypertension (especially in Duchenne’s muscular dystrophy).
dosage: Using a special calibrated vaporizer. Induction: Increased gradually from 0.5% to 3% in oxygen or nitrous oxide-oxygen. Maintenance: 1-2.5% in nitrous oxide-oxygen; an additional 0.5-1% may be required when given with oxygen alone.
precautions: Use cautiously in lactation. Safety and efficacy not established in pediatric patients.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to isoflurane and halogenated agents, genetic susceptibility to malignant hyperthermia. Coronary artery disease; should not be used as a sole agent of induction in patients with ventricular dysfunction.
interactions: Concomitant use of succinylcholine has been associated with hyperkalemia and potentiation of muscle relaxant action.

name: NITROUS OXIDE
uses: Used as a carrier gas for more powerful general anesthetic drugs like desflurane and sevoflurane
side_effects: Megaloblastic anemia due to Vit. B12 and folate deficiency; teratogenic (avoid in 1st and 2nd trimester).
dosage: Mixture with 50% O2 during labor.
precautions: Should be used cautiously in 1st and 2nd trimester of pregnancy and in patient with decreased level of consciousness or in violently disturbed psychiatric patient.
contraindications: Pneumothorax, pneumoperitoneum, middle ear or sinus disease, bowel obstruction.
interactions: When given with other strong anesthetic drugs like desflurane and isoflurane, effect of both drugs increases.

name: OXYGEN
uses: Along with inhalational anesthesia, cluster headache, hyperbaric oxygen (decompression sickness, air/gas embolism, gas gangrene, necrotising fasciitis, radiation therapy), respiratory failure.
side_effects: Concentrations >80% have toxic lung effects (pulmonary congestion, exudation, atelectasis). Retinopathy of prematurity. Hyperbaric therapy may cause barotrauma or CNS/pulmonary toxicity.
dosage: During anesthesia/general: Nasal prongs or face mask (up to 60%); Tight-fitting masks or ETT (up to 100%). Respiratory failure: Face masks at 5 L/min. Cluster headache: Inhalation of 100% oxygen. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy: Intermittent inhalation of 100% oxygen under pressure >1 atmosphere in a specialized chamber.
precautions: Valves and taps should not be lubricated with oil or grease. Any fire or spark is highly dangerous in the presence of increased oxygen concentrations.
contraindications: Avoid high concentrations in patients whose respiration is dependent upon hypoxic drive.

name: SEVOFLURANE
uses: Anesthesia
side_effects: Malignant hyperthermia, dose-dependent hypotension, bradycardia, tachycardia, apnea, increased BUN/ALT, nephrotoxicity, glycosuria, proteinuria.
dosage: Surgical anaesthesia: Inhalation. 0.5 months full term neonate: 3.3% in O2; 1-6 months: 3% in O2; 6 mo-3 years: 2.8% in O2; 25-40 years: 2.1% in O2; 60-80 years: 1.4% in O2 (detailed age-based ranges in formulary).
precautions: Caution in patients with anemia, hepatic impairment, myxedema, renal impairment, or QTc prolongation.
contraindications: Should not be used as a sole agent for induction in patients with ventricular dysfunction. Susceptibility to malignant hyperthermia, hypersensitivity, lack of ventilatory support.
interactions: Concomitant use of succinylcholine associated with hyperkalemia.

name: KETAMINE
uses: Induction and maintenance of anesthesia for minor surgical or diagnostic procedures; Analgesia for painful procedures of short duration for patients at risk of hypotension and bronchospasm.
side_effects: Emergence reactions (dreams, hallucinations, delirium), hypertension, increased cardiac output, increased ICP, tachycardia, tonic clonic movements, increased salivation, dependence.
dosage: IM injection (short procedures): Initially 6.5-13 mg/kg. IV injection (diagnostic): Initially 4 mg/kg over at least 60 seconds. IV infusion (short procedures): Initially 1-4.5 mg/kg. Induction: 0.5-2 mg/kg. Maintenance: 10-45 mcg/kg/minute.
precautions: Use cautiously in CNS abnormalities, hydrocephalus, increased IOP, CAD, catecholamine depletion. To be administered only by experienced personnel with immediate availability of respiratory/cardiovascular support.
contraindications: Patients with epilepsy, hypertension, and in patients with increased ICP.
interactions: With diazepam, may cause ventricular tachycardia or ventricular fibrillation.

name: MIDAZOLAM
uses: Status epilepticus, febrile convulsions, conscious sedation for procedures, sedative in combined anaesthesia, premedication, sedation in intensive care, confusion/restlessness in palliative care.
side_effects: Decreased respiratory rate, apnea, drowsiness, seizure-like activity, nausea/vomiting, sedation, delirium, euphoria.
dosage: Status epilepticus (buccal): Child 1–11 months: 2.5 mg; 1–4 years: 5 mg; 5–9 years: 7.5 mg; Adult: 10 mg. Conscious sedation (slow IV): Adult: Initially 2–2.5 mg (max 7.5 mg/course); Elderly: Initially 0.5–1 mg (max 3.5 mg/course). Premedication (IM): Adult: 70–100 mcg/kg. Induction (slow IV): Adult: 150–200 mcg/kg daily.
precautions: Concentration in children under 15 kg not to exceed 1 mg/mL. Monitor neonates under 6 months for airways obstruction. Caution in hepatic/renal impairment. To be avoided in breastfeeding women. Keep patient supine.
contraindications: CNS depression, compromised airway, severe respiratory depression.

name: PROPOFOL
uses: Induction and maintenance of anesthesia, sedation for surgical and diagnostic procedures.
side_effects: Bradycardia, hypotension, apnea, involuntary movements, injection site burning/stinging, respiratory acidosis during weaning, hypertriglyceridemia.
dosage: Induction (IV injection): 1.5-2.5 mg/kg (1-1.5 mg/kg in those >55 years); child 3-16 yrs: 2.5-3.5 mg/kg. Maintenance: IV injection 25-50 mg repeat OR IV infusion 4-12 mg/kg/hour. Sedation: IV injection 0.5-1 mg/kg; IV infusion 1.5-4.5 mg/kg/hour.
precautions: Proper aseptic technique imperative. Risk of fatal propofol infusion syndrome in ICU patients. Closely monitor patients with anemia, hepatic impairment, myxedema, or renal impairment.
contraindications: Lack of ventilator support, severe cardiac dysfunction, egg/soybean/soy allergy. Sedation of ventilated children and adolescents <17 years. Use in labor and delivery (causes neonatal depression).
interactions: Additive CNS and respiratory depression with alcohol, antihistamines, opioid analgesics, and sedative/hypnotics.

name: THIOPENTAL SODIUM
uses: Induction of anesthesia, rapid control of convulsions like status epilepticus
side_effects: Respiratory and myocardial depression, cardiac arrhythmias, bronchospasm and laryngospasm with cough, rash, prolonged somnolence.
dosage: Induction of anesthesia: Adult: 100-150 mg (4-6 ml of 2.5% solution); repeat after 30-60 sec depending on response. Child dose: 2-7 mg/kg.
precautions: Anesthesia is deeper whenever protein binding is less (e.g., in liver disease). Slight extravasation risk (severe pain, necrosis). Never give into the arteries.
contraindications: Porphyria, hypersensitivity, breast feeding, hypotension, status asthmaticus, severe cardiovascular diseases, hepatic or renal dysfunction.
interactions: Chemically reacts with succinylcholine; never give in same syringe.

name: BUPIVACAINE
uses: Local infiltration, peripheral nerve block, epidural block, sympathetic block.
side_effects: Headache, bradycardia, hypotension, cardiac arrhythmias, cardiac arrest, anxiety, restlessness, tremor, dizziness, respiratory arrest.
dosage: Adjusted per site. Local infiltration: 0.25% (up to 60 ml). Peripheral nerve block: 0.25% (max 60 ml) or 0.5% (max 30 ml). Epidural: 0.5% (max 20-30 ml). Labour (lumbar): 0.25-0.5% (max 12 ml).
precautions: Caution in severely debilitated patients, liver disease, renal impairment, pregnancy, impaired cardiac condition, and myasthenia gravis.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Do not use for IV anesthesia (QT interval prolongation risk). Do not use for obstetric paracervical block.

name: LIDOCAINE (LIGNOCAINE)
uses: Arrhythmia, Local anaesthesia
side_effects: See Bupivacaine.
dosage: Infiltration (by injection): Maximum dose 200 mg (or 500 mg with adrenaline; maximum adrenaline dose 500 µg). Nerve blocks: 1% to maximum of 40 ml (with adrenaline 1 in 200,000). Surface anaesthesia: Mouth/throat max 200 mg; Urethra 2% gel max 400 mg.
precautions: Store at 8-15º C. Discard any gel not used in a single application.

name: PRILOCAINE HYDROCHLORIDE
uses: Infiltration for dentistry, nerve block
side_effects: See Lidocaine.
dosage: Adjusted per site. 100-200 mg/minute to maximum 400 mg.
precautions: N/A

name: PROCAINE HYDROCHLORIDE
uses: Infiltration, peripheral nerve block, sympathetic nerve block, spinal anesthesia
side_effects: See Bupivacaine.
dosage: Adjusted per site. By injection: up to 1g (200ml of 0.5% solution or 100ml of 1% solution).
precautions: N/A

name: FENTANYL
uses: Induction and maintenance of anesthesia, analgesia (pre-operative and post-operative)
side_effects: Confusion, delirium, Paradoxical excitation, bradycardia, hypotension/HTN, respiratory depression/arrest, laryngospasm, double vision, miosis, constipation, biliary spasm, muscle rigidity.
dosage: IV for spontaneous respiration: Adult: 50-100 μg then 50 μg as required; children: 3-5 μg/kg then 1 μg as required. For assisted ventilation: Adult: 0.3-3.5 mg then 100-200 μg as required; children: 15 μg/kg then 1-3 μg as required.
precautions: Pregnancy, breast feeding, geriatric patients, increased ICP, seizure disorders, cardiac dysrhythmias, severe respiratory disorders.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, myasthenia gravis, within 2 hours of MAOI use. Do not use fentanyl within 2 weeks of use of MAOIs.
interactions: With MAOI may produce fatal reactions. CYP3A4 inhibitors increase plasma levels leading to risk of CNS/respiratory depression.

name: PANCURONIUM
uses: Neuromuscular blockade (long duration) during surgery, intubation, or intensive care.
side_effects: Acute myopathy (after prolonged use in intensive care), hypertension, tachycardia.
dosage: Surgery/Intubation (IV injection): Adult: Initially 100 mcg/kg, then 20 mcg/kg as required. Intensive care (IV injection): Adult: Initially 100 mcg/kg, then 60 mcg/kg every 60–90 minutes. Use ideal body weight for obese patients.
precautions: Ventilator support is mandatory. In renal impairment: avoid use if CrCl <10 mL/min; administer 50% normal dose if CrCl 10-50 mL/min.
contraindications: Avoid in neuromuscular disease, hypersensitive to drug and/or bromides.
interactions: With or following an opioid, sedative, or anesthetic agent: additive/synergistic effects.

name: ROCURONIUM BROMIDE
uses: Neuromuscular blockade (intermediate duration) during surgery, intubation, or intensive care.
side_effects: Anaphylactoid reactions, acute myopathy (ICU), bronchospasm, hypotension, skin flushing, tachycardia.
dosage: Surgery/Intubation (IV injection): Adult: Initially 600 mcg/kg; maintenance 150 mcg/kg OR IV infusion 300–600 mcg/kg/hour. Elderly maintenance injection: 75–100 mcg/kg. Intensive care: Adult: Initially 600 mcg/kg; maintenance IV infusion 300–600 mcg/kg/hour for first hour then adjusted.
precautions: Ventilator support is mandatory. Hepatic/Renal impairment: reduce dose/maintenance dose; risk of prolonged paralysis.
contraindications: Avoid in neuromuscular disease, hypersensitive to drug and/or bromides.
interactions: With or following an opioid, sedative, or anesthetic agent: additive/synergistic effects.

name: VECURONIUM
uses: Neuromuscular blockade (intermediate duration) during surgery or intubation.
side_effects: Anaphylactoid reactions, acute myopathy (ICU), bronchospasm, hypotension, skin flushing, tachycardia.
dosage: Surgery/Intubation (IV injection): Adult: 80–100 mcg/kg; maintenance injection: 20–30 mcg/kg. Maximum dose in caesarean section: 100 mcg/kg. Maintenance IV infusion: 0.8–1.4 mcg/kg/minute. Use ideal body weight for obese patients.
precautions: Ventilator support is mandatory. Hepatic/Renal impairment: reduce dose/use caution. Do not dilute reconstituted solution with sterile water alone (risk of fatal hemolysis).
contraindications: Avoid in neuromuscular disease, hypersensitive to drug and/or bromides.
interactions: With or following an opioid, sedative, or anesthetic agent: additive/synergistic effects.

name: NEOSTIGMINE
uses: Treatment of myasthenia gravis, reversal of non-depolarising (competitive) neuromuscular blockade.
side_effects: Anaphylactoid reactions, acute myopathy, bronchospasm, hypotension, skin flushing, tachycardia.
dosage: Myasthenia gravis (Oral): Adult: Initially 15-30 mg repeated (max 180 mg daily). SC/IM injection: Adult: 1-2.5 mg repeated (usual daily 5–20 mg). Reversal (IV injection): Adult: 2.5 mg (max 5 mg) over 1 minute.
precautions: Renal impairment: reduce dose. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: use with caution.
interactions: With or following an opioid, sedative, or anesthetic agent: additive/synergistic effects.

name: ALLOPURINOL
uses: Primary hyperuricemia of gout, secondary hyperuricemia due to haematological malignancies or anti-neoplastic therapy; recurrent renal stones.
side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, maculopapular rash, rarely exfoliative dermatitis, Steven’s Johnson syndrome, aplastic anaemia, acute hepatic failure.
dosage: Adults: 300 mg/day after meal initially, gradually increased to maximum 800 mg/day. Maintenance dose: 200-300 mg (mild), 400-600 mg (moderate to severe). Children: 150-300 mg/day once daily.
precautions: Caution in pregnancy, breast feeding, hepatic and renal impairment. Maintain high fluid intake (2 L/day). Risk of hypersensitivity increased with thiazides.
interactions: Increased risk of hypersensitivity with aspirin, azathioprine, captopril, enalapril, warfarin. Reduce dosages of azathioprine/mercaptopurine to 25-33% of usual.

name: COLCHICINE
uses: Treatment of acute gout, prophylaxis of recurrent acute attacks during initiation of allopurinol therapy.
side_effects: GI disturbance, bloody diarrhoea, abdominal cramps, kidney damage, agranulocytosis, myopathy, hair loss.
dosage: Acute: 1 mg initially followed by 0.25-0.5 mg every 2-3 hours until attack is controlled or diarrhoea starts (max 4 mg). Prophylaxis: 0.5 mg/day.
precautions: Renal diseases, elderly. Do routine blood tests during medication.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity, blood disorders, cardiac disease, pregnancy, lactation.
interactions: Clarithromycin, darunavir, itraconazole, ritonavir, aspirin, atorvastatin, carbamazepine.

name: FEBUXOSTAT
uses: Chronic gout.
side_effects: Elevated liver function tests, GI disturbances, headache, oedema, rash, atrial fibrillation, bronchitis.
dosage: Initially: 40 mg/day oral. Maintenance: 40-80 mg/day (increased if serum uric acid >6 mg/ml after 2 weeks). Use prophylactic colchicine or NSAID for at least 3 months.
precautions: Pregnancy, congestive heart failure, ischemic heart disorders, transplant recipients. Not for monotherapy in acute gouty arthritis.
contraindications: Co-administration with azathioprine, mercaptopurine, or theophylline.

name: PROBENECID
uses: Chronic gout, secondary hyperuricemia, prolonging penicillin action in SABE and gonorrhoea.
side_effects: Gastric irritation, hypersensitivity, seizures and respiratory failure (overdose).
dosage: Gout: 250 mg BD for 1 week followed by 500 mg BD. Gonorrhoea: 1 g oral with 2 g cefotaxime IM.
precautions: May precipitate an acute gouty attack; used concomitantly with NSAID or colchicine.
contraindications: Peptic ulcer, hypersensitivity, renal impairment, history of renal calculi.

name: SULPHINPYRAZONE
uses: Chronic gout, secondary hyperuricemia (Same as probenecid).
side_effects: Acute renal failure, GI bleeding, ulceration, jaundice, elevated liver enzymes.
dosage: 100-200 mg/day taken with food initially; increased to 600-800 mg/day over 2-3 weeks until serum acid is normal.
precautions: Same as probenecid.

name: ABATACEPT
uses: Moderate to severe Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA), psoriatic arthritis.
side_effects: Infection, nasopharyngitis, nausea, cough, back pain, hypertension, UTI.
dosage: Wt <60 kg: 500 mg IV (on day 1, then day 15, then 4 weekly); Wt 60-100 kg: 750 mg IV; Wt >100 kg: 1000 mg IV.
precautions: COPD patients (higher infection risk), latent TB. Do not give live vaccines within 3 months of discontinuation.
interactions: Increased risk of side-effects when given with adalimumab.

name: ADALIMUMAB
uses: Moderate to severe active RA, psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, Crohn’s disease, ulcerative colitis.
side_effects: Anxiety, benign tumours, chest pain, GI haemorrhage, impaired healing, skin cancer, reactivation of latent TB.
dosage: RA (Adult): 40 mg SC every 2 weeks. Crohn’s/UC (Accelerated): 160 mg initially (divided over 2 days), then 80 mg after 2 weeks, then 40 mg every 2 weeks.
precautions: Screen for latent TB/HBV before therapy. Risk of malignancy and demyelinating disorders.
contraindications: Moderate to severe heart failure, severe infection, active tuberculosis.
interactions: Increased side-effects with abatacept; avoid use with anakinra.

name: ANAKINRA
uses: Rheumatoid arthritis (in combination with methotrexate) not responding to methotrexate alone.
side_effects: Neutropenia, antibody formation, headache, injection site reactions, malignancy.
dosage: 100 mg SC once daily.
precautions: History of asthma, chronic infections, immunosuppression. Discontinue if severe infection develops.

name: ETANERCEPT
uses: Ankylosing arthritis, RA, polyarticular idiopathic juvenile arthritis, plaque psoriasis.
side_effects: Serious infection and malignancy risk, headache, rhinitis.
dosage: Ankylosing spondylitis/RA: 50 mg SC once weekly or 25 mg SC twice weekly. Plaque psoriasis: 50 mg SC twice weekly for 3 months, then once weekly.
precautions: Concomitant use of live vaccines.

name: HYDROXYCHOLOROQUINE SULFATE (HCQS)
uses: Early and mild acute rheumatoid arthritis, dermatologic conditions aggravated by sunlight.
side_effects: GI disturbances, skin reactions, convulsions, ECG changes, ototoxicity, retinal damage, keratopathy.
dosage: Oral: 400 mg once daily for 4-6 weeks; maintenance dose 200 mg daily.
precautions: G6PD deficiency, neurological disorders, psoriasis. Discontinue if ocular toxicity suspected. Monitor for retinal changes.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to 4-aminoquinoline derivatives, retinal or visual field changes.
interactions: Avoid concurrent use of hepatotoxic drugs.

name: INFLIXIMAB
uses: Severe active Crohn’s Disease, ulcerative colitis, RA (with methotrexate), ankylosing spondylitis, psoriatic arthritis, plaque psoriasis.
side_effects: Risk of infection (TB, HBV), long-term risk of lymphoma and skin cancer, GI haemorrhage, paraesthesia.
dosage: RA: IV initially 3 mg/kg, then 3 mg/kg at 2 and 6 weeks, then every 8 weeks. Crohn's/UC: initially 5 mg/kg at 0, 2, and 6 weeks, then maintenance every 8 weeks.
precautions: Conception avoided for 6 months after last dose. Active TB screening required. Risk of demyelinating disorders and colon cancer.
interactions: Abatacept, adalimumab, anakinra, live vaccines, cyclosporine.

name: LEFLUNOMIDE
uses: Active rheumatoid arthritis, active psoriatic arthritis.
side_effects: Hepatotoxicity, alopecia, oral mucosal disorders, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, tenosynovitis.
