dosage: Adult: 10-20 mg once a day. Refractory polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis: up to 10 mg once a day.
precautions: Avoid in pregnancy for 3 years after treatment. Monitor liver enzymes and CBC. Avoid live vaccines.
contraindications: Active serious infection, severe hypoproteinaemia, liver disease, severe immunodeficiencies, significant anaemia.

name: METHOTREXATE
uses: Rheumatoid arthritis, choriocarcinoma, acute leukaemia, psoriasis, juvenile idiopathic arthritis.
side_effects: Bone marrow toxicity, pancytopenia, mucositis, pneumonitis, pulmonary fibrosis, hepatic cirrhosis.
dosage: Adult RA: 15 mg ONCE WEEKLY initially (increases by 5 mg every 4-6 weeks). Pediatrics: 5-7.5 mg ONCE WEEKLY (increases by 2.5 mg every 4-6 weeks).
precautions: Monitor closely for hepatic, renal, and bone marrow toxicity. Taking with folic acid (1 mg/day) reduces toxicity. Administer folic acid 5 mg once a week preceding methotrexate dose.
contraindications: Pregnancy (X), alcoholism, alcoholic liver disease, immunodeficiency.

name: PENICILLAMINE
uses: Wilson’s disease, autoimmune hepatitis, cystinuria, chronic lead and arsenic poisoning.
side_effects: Anorexia, taste loss, myasthenia gravis precipitation, proteinuria, kidney damage, Stevens-Johnson syndrome.
dosage: Wilson’s: 1.5-2 g/day divided. Autoimmune hepatitis: 500 mg/day initially, increased to 1.25 g/day. Cystinuria: 1 g/day.
precautions: Monitor for neurologic involvement and hematologic disorders.
contraindications: Lupus erythematosus, simultaneous with gold therapy.
interactions: Ferrous fumarate, ferrous gluconate, MgSO4, sodium bicarbonate.

name: RITUXIMAB
uses: Moderate to severe active RA not responsive to methotrexate, NHL, CLL, refractory lupus, vasculitis.
side_effects: Tumour lysis syndrome, reactivation of hepatitis B, Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML), cardiac arrest, neuropathy.
dosage: RA: 1 g IV infusion on Day 1 and Day 15, then repeat after 6 months. Pre-medicate with glucocorticoid 30 mins before infusion.
precautions: Caution in angina, arrhythmia. Avoid pregnancy for at least 12 months after treatment. No immunization without consent.
interactions: Concomitant cisplatin increases risk of fatal infusion reaction.

name: SULFASALAZINE
uses: Rheumatoid arthritis, IBD, ankylosing spondylitis, juvenile chronic arthritis.
side_effects: Reversible oligospermia, GI distress, haemolytic anaemia, rash, pruritus.
dosage: RA: oral 2-3 g/day (enteric coated). Crohn’s: 3-6 g/day.
precautions: Caution in bronchial asthma, blood dyscrasias. Risk of neural tube defects and neonatal jaundice.
pregnancy_category: B (D if used for prolonged periods or near term)

name: TOCILIZUMAB
uses: Moderate to severe active RA.
side_effects: Infections, gastritis, elevated lipid levels, infusion related skin reactions.
dosage: IV infusion: 4-8 mg/kg every 4 weeks (max dose 800 mg). SC infusion: Wt <100 kg: 162 mg every other week; Wt >100 kg: 162 mg per week.
precautions: Discontinue if ANC <500/mm3, Platelets <50,000/mm3, or ALT/AST >5x normal. Do not give live vaccines.

name: TOFACUTINIB
uses: Moderate to severe active RA with inadequate response to methotrexate, psoriatic arthritis, refractory JIA.
side_effects: Infections.
dosage: 5 mg twice a day or 11 mg (extended release) once daily.
precautions: Renal and hepatic impairment. Do not give live vaccines.
interactions: CYP3A4 inhibitors (fluconazole, erythromycin, omeprazole) increase levels; do not exceed 5 mg/day.

name: ACELECOFENAC
uses: Non-selective COX inhibitor: Rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, fibromyalgia.
side_effects: Allergy and cross-sensitivity, exacerbation of asthma, angioedema, colitis, pancreatitis.
dosage: 100 mg twice daily.
precautions: Avoid in acute porphyria, cardiac impairment, coagulation defects. Use caution in hypertension, elderly.
contraindications: Active GI bleeding, active GI ulceration, history of recurrent GI haemorrhage, severe heart failure.

name: ASPIRIN
uses: Non-selective COX inhibitor: Mild to moderate pain and fever, rheumatic fever.
side_effects: Dyspepsia, GI bleeding, mucosal lesions, tinnitus, hearing loss (high dose), prolongation of bleeding time.
dosage: 300-900 mg every 4-6 hours when necessary (max 4 g daily). Child/Adolescent: not recommended.
precautions: Impaired renal/hepatic function, asthma. Not for children with flulike symptoms (Reye’s syndrome risk).
contraindications: Haemophilia, children under 16 years, breast-feeding, gout, heart disease, erosive gastritis.
interactions: Acetazolamide (toxicity), Heparin (enhanced anticoagulation), Methotrexate (reduced excretion), Spironolactone (antagonism of diuretic effect).

name: DICLOFENAC
uses: Non-selective COX inhibitor: Rheumatic disease, osteoarthritis, juvenile arthritis, acute gout, post-operative pain, dysmenorrhea.
side_effects: Fluid retention (precipitating heart failure), GI ulceration and bleeding, renal failure, NSAID induced headache.
dosage: Adult: Oral 75-150 mg daily in 2-3 divided doses. Acute exacerbations/Post-op pain: 75 mg once daily. Ureteric colic: 75 mg, then further 75 mg after 30 mins if needed. Max total dose: 150 mg daily. Child (1yr+): 1-3 mg/kg daily.
precautions: Withdraw if cardiogenic shock develops. Take with food, milk or antacids.
contraindications: Active GI bleeding/ulceration, ischemic heart disease, heart failure, 3rd trimester pregnancy, breast-feeding.
interactions: Increases hyperkalaemia with K-sparing diuretics; increases toxicity of phenytoin, lithium, methotrexate, digoxin.

name: FLURBIPROFEN
uses: Non-selective COX inhibitor: Rheumatic disease, musculoskeletal disorders, mild to moderate pain, dysmenorrhea.
side_effects: Similar to ibuprofen but with more GI adverse effects.
dosage: Oral: 150-200 mg daily in divided doses (increased in acute conditions to 300 mg daily). Dysmenorrhea: initially 100 mg then 50-100 mg q4-6h (max 300 mg daily).
precautions: Regular lab tests (Hgb, LFT, KFT, audiometry, eye test). Monitor for GI bleeding.

name: IBUPROFEN
uses: Non-selective COX inhibitor: RA, OA, primary dysmenorrhea, dental pain, musculoskeletal disorders, fever, migraine.
side_effects: GI irritation, bleeding, angioedema, bronchospasm, tinnitus, fluid retention.
dosage: Adult: initially 1.2-1.8 g daily in 3-4 divided doses (max 2.4 g daily). Child: 20-30 mg/kg daily. Not for children under 5 kg.
precautions: Caution in bleeding disorders, cardiac disorders. Use sunscreen to prevent photosensitivity.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to NSAIDs, asthma, severe renal/hepatic disease, 3rd trimester pregnancy.

name: INDOMETHACIN
uses: Non-selective COX inhibitor: Rheumatic disease, musculoskeletal disorders, acute gout, dysmenorrhea, closure of ductus arteriosus.
side_effects: Nausea (oral), rectal irritation/bleeding (rectal). General side effects same as diclofenac.
dosage: Rheumatic: 50-200 mg daily in divided doses. Rectum: 100 mg twice daily. Acute gout: 150-200 mg daily divided. Dysmenorrhea: up to 75 mg daily.
precautions: Epilepsy, parkinsonism, renal impairment. Ophthalmic and blood exams advisable during long-term therapy.
contraindications: Active GI bleeding/ulceration, severe heart failure, neonates, aortic coarctation, lactating mother, 3rd trimester pregnancy.

name: MEFENAMIC ACID
uses: Non-selective COX inhibitor: RA, OA, postoperative pain, dysmenorrhea/menorrhagia.
side_effects: Diarrhea (withdraw treatment), rashes (withdraw), stomatitis, aplastic anemia, glucose intolerance.
dosage: 500 mg 3 times a day.
precautions: Pregnancy Category C and D. Caution in acute porphyria, renal/cardiac impairment.
contraindications: Active GI bleeding/ulceration, IBD, severe heart failure, lactating mother.

name: NAPROXEN
uses: Non-selective COX inhibitor: Rheumatic disease, musculoskeletal disorders, dysmenorrhea, acute gout.
side_effects: See under NSAIDs as general.
dosage: Rheumatic: 0.5-1 g daily in 1-2 divided doses. Dysmenorrhea: initially 500 mg then 250 mg q6-8h. Acute gout: initially 750 mg then 250 mg every 8 hours.
precautions: Uncontrolled hypertension, asthma, breastfeeding.
contraindications: Active GI bleeding/ulceration, severe heart failure, children <2 years.

name: PARACETAMOL
uses: Non-selective COX inhibitor: Mild to moderate pain or fever, arthralgia, dysmenorrhea, headache, OA.
side_effects: See under Indomethacin.
dosage: Adult: 0.5-1 g every 4-6 hours (max 4 g/day). Adult IV (50 kg+): 1 g q4-6h. Children: 10-15 mg/kg/dose every 4-6 hours (max 5 doses/day).
precautions: Hepatic toxicity risk at doses >0.4 g/day with chronic use.
interactions: Alcohol, barbiturates, isoniazid, and carbamazepine increase hepatotoxicity. Warfarin (long-term high dose paracetamol increases hypoprothrombinemia).

name: PIROXICAM
uses: Non-selective COX inhibitor: RA, juvenile RA, OA, ankylosing spondylitis.
side_effects: Indigestion, upper respiratory infection, anemia, dizziness. Topical: photosensitivity, rash.
dosage: Oral: Up to 20 mg once daily. Topical (Gel 0.5%): apply 3-4 times a day.
precautions: Increases risk of asthma, cardiac disease, CHF. For topical use, avoid excessive sunlight on treated area.

name: CELECOXIB
uses: Selective COX-2 inhibitor: Acute pain, primary dysmenorrhoea, ankylosing spondylitis, OA, RA.
side_effects: Headache, hypertension, fever, dyspepsia, peripheral oedema.
dosage: Acute pain/Dysmenorrhoea: initially 400 mg then 200 mg. Ankylosing spondylitis: 200-400 mg/day. OA: 200 mg/day. RA: 100-200 mg/day.
precautions: Increased risk of adverse cardiovascular events. Risk of GI bleeding and perforation.
contraindications: Aspirin allergy, chronic hepatitis, perioperative pain in CABG surgery.

name: ETORICOXIB
uses: Selective COX-2 inhibitor: Ankylosing spondylitis, osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, acute gout.
side_effects: Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis, upper GI ulceration, alveolar osteitis, increased ALT/AST.
dosage: OA: 30-60 mg once daily. RA/Ankylosing spondylitis: 90 mg once daily. Acute gout: 120 mg once daily (max 8 days).
precautions: History of bronchospasm, acute rhinitis, nasal polyps.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, active GI ulceration/bleeding, heart failure, ischaemic heart disease, uncontrolled HTN.

name: DIACEREIN
uses: Anthraquinone: Osteoarthritis.
side_effects: Diarrhea, pain abdomen, intense yellow coloring of urine.
dosage: Oral: 50 mg twice daily.
precautions: Monitor CBC, LFT and urinalysis every 6 months. Take with food.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to anthraquinone derivatives, renal/hepatic impairment.
interactions: Aluminium/magnesium hydroxide antacids decrease absorption; laxatives increase diarrhea risk. Avoid fibers/phytates co-administration.

name: ALENDRONATE
uses: Bisphosphonate: Osteoporosis, Paget’s disease.
side_effects: Heart burn, gastric erosion, retrosternal pain, fall in serum Ca2+ level.
dosage: 5-10 mg OD or 35-70 mg weekly.
precautions: Take in empty stomach in morning. Do not lie down or take food for at least 30 min to prevent oesophagitis.
contraindications: Hypocalcaemia, oesophageal stricture or achalasia, serum kidney problem.
interactions: NSAID, prednisolone, calcium, iron, antacids, tea, coffee, fruit juice.

name: ETIDRONATE
uses: Bisphosphonate: Paget’s disease, total hip replacement, spinal cord injury, PTH-induced bone resorption.
side_effects: Convulsion, fever, hypocalcaemia, abnormal renal function.
dosage: Paget's: 5-10 mg/kg qday (max 6 months). Hip replacement: 20 mg/kg qday (1 month pre- and 3 months post-surgery).
precautions: N/A
interactions: Aluminium hydroxide, calcium carbonate, sodium bicarbonate.

name: IBANDRONATE
uses: Bisphosphonate: Treatment and prevention of osteoporosis in postmenopausal women.
side_effects: URI, back pain, dyspepsia, bronchitis, tooth disorder.
dosage: Oral: 150 mg every month. IV: 3 mg every 3 months administered over 15-30 seconds.
precautions: Adequate intake of calcium and vitamin D recommended. Do not lie down after taking.
interactions: Human parathyroid hormone, calcium, ferrous fumarate.

name: PAMIDRONATE
uses: Bisphosphonate: Hypercalcemia of malignancy, Paget’s disease, osteolytic bone metastasis, multiple myeloma.
side_effects: Anaemia, hypokalaemia, hypophosphatemia, seizure, osteonecrosis.
dosage: Hypercalcemia: 90 mg single IV infusion (2-24 hrs). Paget’s: 30 mg IV infusion (4 hrs qday) for 3 days. Metastases: 90 mg IV infusion every month.
precautions: Monitor for electrolyte abnormalities and myelosuppression.

name: RISEDRONATE
uses: Bisphosphonate: Postmenopausal osteoporosis, glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis, Paget’s disease.
side_effects: Arthralgia, rash, pharyngitis, prostatic hyperplasia, nephrolithiasis, arrhythmia.
dosage: Postmenopausal: 5 mg daily or 35 mg weekly or 150 mg monthly. Glucocorticoid-induced: 5 mg/day. Paget's: 30 mg/day for 2 months.
precautions: Monitor for SJS, toxic epidermal necrolysis.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, angioedema, hypocalcemia, esophagus stricture, osteonecrosis of jaw.

name: ZOLEDRONATE
uses: Bisphosphonate: Hypercalcemia, cancer chemotherapy, multiple myeloma, osteoporosis.
side_effects: Bone pain, fever, fatigue, anaemia, urinary tract infection, hypomagnesemia.
dosage: Hypercalcemia: 4 mg IV (repeatable in 7 days). Myeloma/Metastases: 4 mg IV every 3-4 weeks. Postmenopausal prevention: 5 mg IV every 2 years.
precautions: N/A
contraindications: Pregnancy, severe renal impairment, shock hypocalcemia.

name: BACLOFEN
uses: Centrally acting muscle relaxant: Chronic severe spasticity (MS, spinal cord section), pain of muscle spasm in palliative care, hiccup.
side_effects: Cardiovascular depression, hallucinations, hyperhidrosis, respiratory depression, urinary disturbances.
dosage: Oral spasticity: initially 5 mg TID, maintenance up to 60 mg daily (max 100 mg/day). Intrathecal: test dose 25-50 mcg, then titrated maintenance dose.
precautions: Stroke, seizure disorder, diabetes mellitus, geriatric patients. Do not discontinue quickly (taper over 1-2 weeks).
interactions: Increase CNS depression with alcohol, tricyclics, opiates, MAOIs. Increase hypotension with anti-hypertensives.

name: DEXMEDETOMIDINE
uses: Centrally acting muscle relaxant: Maintenance of sedation during intensive care.
side_effects: Blood pressure changes, hyperthermia, myocardial infarction, abdominal distension, AV block, hypoalbuminemia.
dosage: IV infusion: 0.7 mcg/kg/hour adjusted to response (usual range 0.2-1.4 mcg/kg/hour).
precautions: Direct supervision by anesthesia-trained personnel required. Monitor cardiac/respiratory function.

name: TIZANIDINE
uses: Centrally acting muscle relaxant: Spasticity associated with multiple sclerosis or spinal cord injury.
side_effects: Somnolence, dizziness, dyskinesia, psychosis, increased ALT, urinary frequency, pharyngitis.
dosage: Initially 2 mg for 1 dose, then increased by 2 mg every 3-4 days (usual dose up to 24 mg daily, max 36 mg/day).
precautions: Monitor liver function monthly for first four months. Discontinue gradually.
interactions: Alcohol increases CNS depression. Fluvoxamine and ciprofloxacin increase tizanidine levels (avoid concurrent use). Rasagiline effect increased.

name: DENOSUMAB
uses: Osteoporosis, androgen deprivation induced bone loss, giant cell tumour, hypercalcemia of malignancy.
side_effects: Back pain, cystitis, sciatica, osteonecrosis of jaw, pruritus, hypocalcaemia.
dosage: Osteoporosis: 60 mg SC every 6 months (with Ca/Vit D supplements). Bone loss (Prostate cancer): 60 mg SC every 6 months. Giant cell tumour: 120 mg SC q4wk (loading: extra doses on Day 8 and 15 of 1st month).
precautions: History of systemic hypersensitivity/anaphylaxis. Monitor for cellulitis and dermatologic reactions.
interactions: Increased infection risk with adalimumab, abatacept, corticosteroids, immunosuppressants.

name: DILOXANIDE FUROATE
uses: Asymptomatic cyst passers and extra intestinal amoebiasis (together with tissue amoebicide).
side_effects: Flatulence, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, pruritus, urticaria.
dosage: Adult: 500 mg every 8 hours for 10 days. Child: 20 mg/kg daily in 3 divided doses for 10 days.
precautions: N/A

name: METRONIDAZOLE
uses: Giardiasis, amoebic dysentery, extra-intestinal amoebiasis (amoebic liver abscess), Trichomonas vaginalis, Giardia lambia, Helicobacter pylori, Balantidium coli, anaerobic bacterial infections, surgical and gynaecological sepsis due to colonic anaerobes (Bacteroides fragilis).
side_effects: Metallic taste, nausea, headache, furred tongue, dizziness, vertigo, dark brown urine, reversible peripheral neuropathy.
dosage: Invasive intestinal amoebiasis: oral 800 mg q8h for 5 days; Child 1-3 yrs: 200 mg q8h; 3-7 yrs: 200 mg q6h; 7-10 yrs: 400 mg q8h. Extra-intestinal/cyst passers: oral 400-800 mg q8h for 5-10 days. Giardiasis: oral 2 g daily for 3 days or 400 mg TID for 5 days. Anaerobic infections: oral 800 mg initially then 400 mg q8h (usually 7 days). Bacterial vaginosis: 400 mg BID for 5-7 days or 2 g single dose. Acute ulcerative gingivitis: 200 mg q8h for 3 days. Surgical prophylaxis: 400 mg started 2 hours before surgery, then q8h.
precautions: Carcinogenic in rats and mice but no clinical evidence of increased malignancy risk in humans. Avoid alcohol during use or for 4-8 hours after. Nursing mothers should not breastfeed during high-dose treatment. Caution in geriatric patients, candida infections, heart failure, and CNS disorders.
interactions: Avoid use with zalcitabine, norfloxacin, disulfiram. Potentiates effects of oral anticoagulants.

name: SECNIDAZOLE
uses: Trichomoniasis, amoebiasis, giardiasis, invasive (hepatic) amoebiasis.
side_effects: Vulvovaginal candidiasis, nausea, headache, dysgeusia, diarrhea, vomiting, abdominal pain, vulvovaginal pruritus.
dosage: Trichomoniasis/Amoebiasis/Giardiasis: oral, adult: single dose 2000 mg; child: single dose 30 mg/kg. Invasive (hepatic) amoebiasis: oral, adult: 1.5 g daily in single or divided doses for 5 days; child: 30 mg/kg daily for 5 days.
precautions: Avoid chronic use.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to secnidazole or other nitroimidazole derivatives.

name: TINIDAZOLE
uses: Amoebic infections, bacterial vaginosis, acute ulcerative colitis, intestinal amoebiasis.
side_effects: See under METRONIDAZOLE.
dosage: Anaerobic infections: oral 2 g initially, then 1 g daily or 500 mg BID for 5-7 days. Prophylaxis: 2 g dose ~12 hours before surgery. Intestinal amoebiasis: 2 g daily for 2-3 days; Child: 50-60 mg/kg for 3 days. Liver involvement: 1.5-2 g daily for 3-6 days. Urogenital: single 2 g dose.
precautions: Avoid in alcoholism.
contraindications: Pregnancy, breastfeeding, hypersensitivity, CNS depression, blood dyscrasias.
interactions: Don’t use within 2 weeks of disulfiram. Cimetidine and ketoconazole increase effects. Phenobarbital and rifampin decrease effects. Increases action of anticoagulants, cyclosporine, tacrolimus.

name: CEFACLOR
uses: Susceptible gram-positive and gram-negative infections, pneumonia, lower UTI.
side_effects: Urticaria, pruritus, rash, fever, joint pain, exfoliative dermatitis, nausea, vomiting, positive Coomb’s test, elevated liver enzymes.
dosage: 250 mg every 8 hours (doubled for severe infection); max 4 g daily. Child (>1 month): 20 mg/kg daily in 3 divided doses (doubled for severe infections); max 1 g daily.
precautions: Cross-allergenicity with penicillins (10% of cases). Prolonged use may result in overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms (Pseudomonas, Enterococci, Candida).

name: CEFADROXIL
uses: Skin and soft tissue infection, uncomplicated UTI, pharyngitis, tonsillitis, endocarditis.
side_effects: See under CEFACLOR.
dosage: 250 mg oral q6h or 500 mg q8-12h (max 1-1.5 g q6-8h for severe infections). Child: 30 mg/kg daily divided; max 100 mg/kg daily. UTI Prophylaxis (Adult): 125 mg at night.
precautions: See under CEFACLOR.

name: CEFALEXIN
uses: Susceptible gram-positive and gram-negative infections, pneumonia, lower UTI.
side_effects: See under CEFACLOR.
dosage: 250 mg oral every 8 hours (doubled for severe); max 4 g daily. Child (>1 month): 25-50 mg/kg daily in 3 divided doses. UTI Prophylaxis (Adult): 125 mg at night; Child: 10 mg/kg at night.
precautions: See under CEFACLOR.
interactions: Increases effects of anticoagulants; increases toxicity of aminoglycosides, loop diuretics, probenecid. Decreases effects of oral contraceptives.

name: CEFAZOLIN
uses: Surgical prophylaxis, susceptible gram-positive and gram-negative infections.
side_effects: See under CEFACLOR.
dosage: IM/IV: 0.5-1 g every 6-12 hours. Child: 25-50 mg/kg daily in divided doses (up to 100 mg/kg in severe cases).
precautions: Adjust dose in severe renal insufficiency. Caution in patients with seizures.

name: CEFEPIME
uses: See under CEFACLOR.
side_effects: See under CEFACLOR.
dosage: IV: 2 g every 12 hours. Child: 100-150 mg/kg/day.
precautions: See under CEFACLOR.

name: CEFIXIME
uses: See under CEFACLOR.
side_effects: See under CEFACLOR.
dosage: Adult/Child (>10 yrs): 200-400 mg daily in 1-2 divided doses. Child: 8 mg/kg in 1-2 divided doses. Gonorrhoea: 400 mg single dose.
precautions: See under CEFACLOR.

name: CEFOPERAZONE
uses: Pelvic infections, urinary-tract infections, bone and joint infections.
side_effects: See under CEFACLOR.
dosage: IM/IV: 1-2 g (base) every 12 hours.
precautions: May produce disulfiram-like reaction with alcohol.

name: CEFOTAXIME
uses: URTI, uncomplicated UTI, gonorrhea.
side_effects: See under CEFACLOR.
dosage: IM/IV: 1 g q12h (2 g q6h for severe/less sensitive organisms). Child: 100-150 mg/kg/day in 3-4 divided doses (max 200 mg/kg/day).
precautions: See under CEFACLOR.

name: CEFPODOXIME
uses: URTI, sinusitis, uncomplicated UTI, skin and soft tissue infections, uncomplicated gonorrhea.
side_effects: See under CEFACLOR.
dosage: URTI: 100-200 mg BID for 10 days; Child: 8 mg/kg/day divided. UTI: 100-200 mg BID. Gonorrhea: 200 mg single dose. Skin: 400 mg BD 7-14 days.
precautions: Renal impairment.

name: CEFTAZIDIME
uses: See under CEFPODOXIME; Pseudomonal lung infection in cystic fibrosis, meningitis, surgical prophylaxis (prostatic surgery), febrile neutropenia.
side_effects: See under CEFACLOR.
dosage: IM/IV: 1 g q8h (2 g q12h for severe). Child (<2 mo): 25-60 mg/kg daily; (>2 mo): 30-100 mg/kg daily (max 6 g/day in meningitis/immunocompromised). Cystic Fibrosis (Adult): 100-150 mg/kg daily; (Child): up to 150 mg/kg. Prostatic surgery: 1 g at induction.
precautions: See under CEFACLOR.

name: CEFTRIAXONE
uses: See under CEFPODOXIME, epiglottitis, early syphilis, meningitis.
side_effects: Headache, dizziness, fever, seizures, nausea, vomiting, agranulocytosis, anaphylaxis, TEN.
dosage: IM/IV: 1 g daily single dose (2-4 g in severe). Surgical Prophylaxis: 1 g 30 min before procedure. Early syphilis: IM 500 mg daily for 10 days. Meningitis (Child 1 mo - 11 yrs): IV 50-75 mg/kg (max 100 mg/kg/day). Epiglottitis: 1 g BID + steroid, then step down to cefixime.
precautions: Risk of fatal calcium-ceftriaxone precipitant in lungs/kidneys of neonates. May increase INR in nutritionally deficient patients.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, hyperbilirubinemic neonates, neonates <28 days receiving calcium-containing products.
interactions: Increases cyclosporine level. Increases bleeding with anticoagulants/NSAIDS. Increases toxicity of aminoglycosides and probenecid. Decrease absorption with iron-rich cereals.

name: CEFUROXIME
uses: Surgical prophylaxis, Haemophilus influenzae, Neisseria gonorrhoeae, tonsillitis, pharyngitis, UTI, pyelonephritis.
side_effects: See under CEFACLOR.
dosage: Oral (as axetil): 250 mg BID. UTI: 125 mg BID. Gonorrhoea: 1 g single dose. Child: IV 50-100 mg/kg/day and Oral 20-40 mg/kg/day. Prophylaxis: 1.5 g IV at induction. Tonsillitis/Pharyngitis (Adult): 250 mg daily for 4 days; (Child): 10 mg/kg BID for 4-10 days.
precautions: If diabetic, use blood glucose test.
interactions: Increases toxicity of aminoglycosides, furosemide, probenecid. Increases bleeding with anticoagulants. Decreases oral contraceptive effects. Absorption decreased by antacids/H2 blockers.

name: AMOXICILLIN
uses: URTI (S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae), otitis media, sinusitis, pneumonia, pharyngitis, skin/soft tissue, UTI, H. pylori, diphtheria.
side_effects: Anaphylaxis, mucocutaneous candidiasis, AST/ALT elevation, pseudomembranous colitis.
dosage: Mild-Moderate: 500 mg q12h or 250 mg q8h (10-14 days). Severe: 875 mg q12h or 500 mg q8h. Tonsillitis: 875 mg daily for 10 days. H. pylori (Triple therapy): 1 g BID for 14 days. Diphtheria: 500 mg TID for 2 weeks.
precautions: Monitor for Clostridium difficile-associated diarrhoea (CDAD). Use cautiously in infectious mononucleosis. Medication can be taken regardless of meals.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to penicillins, cephalosporins, or imipenem.
interactions: BCG/Cholera vaccines, tetracyclines, mycophenolate, allopurinol, warfarin, methotrexate.

name: AMOXICILLIN with CLAVULANATE
uses: LRTI (beta-lactamase producing H. influenzae/Moraxella), acute bacterial sinusitis, mastoiditis, bite wounds, erysipelas, pyelonephritis, skin abscess, diabetic foot.
side_effects: Diarrhea, mycosis, rash, candidiasis, vaginitis.
dosage: Mild-Moderate LRTI: 500/125 mg q12h or 250/125 mg q8h for 10 days. Severe: 875/125 mg q12h. Sinusitis: 2000 mg (ER tabs) q12h. Mastoiditis: 1.2 g IV q8h then step down. Group A Streptococci: 40 mg/kg/day divided q8h (max 2000 mg/day).
precautions: Hepatic dysfunction more common in elderly/males. Take with meals.
contraindications: Allergy to penicillins, previous history of cholestatic jaundice/hepatic dysfunction with this combination.
interactions: Decreases BCG vaccine effects. Doxycycline/Minocycline decrease effects. Allopurinol increases hypersensitivity risk.

name: AMPICILLIN
uses: UTI (E. coli, Proteus), chronic bronchitis, otitis media, invasive salmonellosis.
side_effects: Erythema multiforme, exfoliative dermatitis, enterocolitis, agranulocytosis, increased AST.
dosage: Oral: 0.25-1 g q6h (at least 30 min before food). UTI: 500 mg q8h. IM/IV: 500 mg q4-6h. Meningitis (Child <10 yrs): half adult dose.
precautions: Adjust dose in renal failure. Take on empty stomach with a full glass of water.

name: AMPICILLIN with SULBACTAM
uses: Gynecological, intra-abdominal, skin, orbital cellulitis, PID, pneumonia (aspiration/community).
side_effects: Diarrhea, thrombophlebitis, rash, abdominal distension.
dosage: IM/IV: 1.5 g (1 g amp + 0.5 g sulb) to 3 g (2 g amp + 1 g sulb) q6h; max 12 g/day. Pneumonia: treat for 5+ days.
precautions: Monitor hepatic function in hepatic impairment. May cause TEN or SJS.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, previous history of cholestatic jaundice with this drug.

name: BACAMPICILLIN
uses: See under AMPICILLIN.
side_effects: See under AMPICILLIN.
dosage: 400-800 mg daily; Child (>5 yrs): 200 mg TID. Uncomplicated gonorrhoea: 1.6 g single dose + 1 g probenecid.
precautions: See under AMPICILLIN.

name: BENZYL PENICILLIN (PENICILLIN G)
uses: Otitis media, meningitis, cellulitis, endocarditis, pneumococcal pneumonia, streptococcal infections, diphtheria.
side_effects: Skin rashes, serum-sickness like reactions, Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction, pseudomembranous colitis.
dosage: IM: 2.4-4.8 g daily in 4 divided doses. Neonate: 50 mg/kg daily. Infant (1-4 wks): 75 mg/kg. Child: 100 mg/kg. Bacterial Endocarditis: 7.2 g daily in 4-6 divided doses. Diphtheria: 1200 mg IV q6h for 2 weeks.
precautions: Serious and occasionally fatal reactions reported. Caution in neonates.
contraindications: Only deep IM administration; do not administer IV, SC, or IT. Do not inject near nerve or artery.

name: CARBENICILLIN
uses: Infections due to Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Proteus.
side_effects: Hypokalaemia, prolonged bleeding/prothrombin time, abnormal platelet aggregation.
dosage: Slow IV/Infusion: 5 g q4-6h; Child: 250-400 mg/kg divided. IM: 2 g q6h; Child: 50-100 mg/kg divided.
precautions: Use immediately after preparation.

name: CLOXACILLIN
uses: Exclusively for infection caused by Staphylococcus aureus.
side_effects: Abdominal pain, impaired LFTs, nephritis.
dosage: Oral: 500 mg 4 times daily (doubled in severe). IM: 250 mg q4-6h (doubled in severe). IV: 1-2 g q6h. Child (<2 yrs): quarter adult dose; (2-10 yrs): half adult dose.
precautions: Monitor PT if taking warfarin concurrently. Superinfection risk with prolonged use.

name: FLUCLOXACILLIN
uses: Otitis externa, furunculosis, pneumonia, impetigo, osteomyelitis, staphylococcal endocarditis.
side_effects: See under BENZYL PENICILLIN.
dosage: Adult: 250-500 mg q6h (oral/IM). Child (<2 yrs): quarter dose; (2-10 yrs): half dose. Furunculosis: 1 g q6h for 5 days. Endocarditis (<85 kg): 8 g daily in 4 divided doses.
precautions: See under BENZYL PENICILLIN.

name: PHENOXY METHYL PENICILLIN (PENICILLIN V)
uses: Streptococcal pharyngitis, actinomycosis, erysipelas, periodontal infections, recurrent rheumatic fever.
side_effects: Interstitial nephritis, anaphylaxis, positive Coomb's reaction.
dosage: Pharyngitis: 500 mg q12h or 250 mg q6h for 10 days. Actinomycosis (Mild): 2-4 g/day oral q6h for 8 weeks (Surgical: 6-12 months). Prophylaxis: 250 mg q12h.
precautions: IgE mediated anaphylaxis reported in severe renal impairment and asthma. Use with caution in neonates; some forms contain sodium benzoate (risk of gasping syndrome).
contraindications: Allergy to penicillins, cephalosporins, or imipenem.
interactions: Decreases effects of BCG vaccine. Tetracyclines decrease its effects.

name: PIPERACILLIN
uses: Urinary tract infection (uncomplicated), community acquired pneumonia, acute cholangitis, uncomplicated gonorrhea, Pseudomonas infections.
side_effects: Hemolytic anemia, interstitial nephritis, prolonged prothrombin time, injection site pain.
dosage: Usual: IV 3-4 g/dose q4-6h (max 24 g/day); IM 2-3 g/dose q6-12h (max 24 g/day). UTI/Pneumonia: 100-125 mg/kg/day divided q6-12h. Cholangitis: 4 g IV q6h. Gonorrhea: 2 g once + 1 g probenecid. Pseudomonas: 4 g IV/IM q4h. Renal Adjust: CrCl 20-40: 3-4 g q8h; CrCl <20: 3-4 g q12h.
precautions: Risk of bleeding complications in renal impairment. Monitor hematopoietic functions during prolonged treatment. IVPreparation: reconstitute each gram w/ 5ml NS/D5W.
interactions: Increases effects/toxicity of antithrombin alfa, argatroban, heparin, vancomycin. Azithromycin and Doxycycline decrease effects. Piperacillin decreases BCG vaccine effects.

name: PIPERACILLIN with TAZOBACTAM
uses: Severe infections, nosocomial pneumonia, community acquired pneumonia, intra-abdominal abscess, skin/soft tissue, malignant otitis externa.
side_effects: Diarrhea, constipation, headache, insomnia, nausea, fever, oral candidiasis.
dosage: Severe: IV 3.375 g q6h (Total 13.5 g) for 7-10 days. Nosocomial: 4.5 g IV + aminoglycoside for 7-14 days. Complicated Intra-abdominal: 3.375 g q6h for 4-7 days. Malignant Otitis Externa: 4.5 g IV q8h then step down to ciprofloxacin.
precautions: Discontinue if thrombocytopenia or bleeding occurs. Serious skin reactions (SJS, TEN) reported.
contraindications: Allergy to penicillin, cephalosporins, imipenem, beta-lactamase inhibitors.

name: AMIKACIN
uses: Serious gram-negative infections resistant to gentamicin.
side_effects: See under GENTAMICIN.
dosage: Adult: IV once daily 15 mg/kg/day (max 1.5 g/day); max 15 g per course. Child: 15 mg/kg daily in 2-3 doses. Neonate: loading 10 mg/kg then 15 mg/kg daily in 2 divided doses.
precautions: N/A

name: GENTAMICIN
uses: Pseudomonas UTIs, meningitis/neonatal sepsis, endocarditis, biliary tract disease, prostatitis, surgical prophylaxis, medical labyrinthectomy, otitis externa.
side_effects: Vestibular damage, reversible nephrotoxicity, muscle weakness, respiratory paralysis.
dosage: IM/IV: 3-5 mg/kg daily (divided q8h). Child (<2 wks): 3 mg/kg q12h; (2 wks-12 yrs): 2 mg/kg q8h. Intrathecal: 1 mg daily (max 5 mg). Endocarditis: 1 mg/kg q8h. Surgical Prophylaxis: 1.5 mg/kg (max 3 min before procedure); can repeat q8h. Medical Labyrinthectomy: intra tympanic 2-3 drops, 3-4 times daily.
precautions: Monitor blood levels in neonates, elderly, and renal impairment. Report hearing loss, ringing in ears, or head fullness. Myasthenia gravis and parkinson's disease risk.
interactions: Do not mix with penicillins. Increased ototoxicity/nephrotoxicity with vancomycin, cisplatin, furosemide, mannitol. Increases effects of non-depolarizing neuromuscular blockers.

name: CHLORAMPHENICOL
uses: Life threatening infections (Hemophilus influenza), typhoid fever, acute otitis externa.
side_effects: Erythema multiforme, optic neuritis, grey baby syndrome.
dosage: Adult: 12.5 mg/kg every 6 hours (can double in septicemia/meningitis). Otitis externa: intra-aural 2-3 drops, BID/TID for 7 days.
precautions: Monitor blood counts regularly; discontinue if leucopenia or anemia appears. Do not give IM (ineffective). Take on empty stomach.

name: CLINDAMYCIN
uses: Staphylococcal bone/joint infections (osteomyelitis), peritonitis, MRSA, bronchiectasis, skin/soft tissue, pneumocystis pneumonia (with primaquine), falciparum malaria (after quinine), acne vulgaris, tonsillitis/pharyngitis (penicillin allergy).
side_effects: Antibiotic-associated colitis (discontinue), jaundice, esophageal ulcers, vesiculobullous dermatitis.
dosage: Infections: Adult 150-300 mg q6h (max 450 mg). Child: 3-6 mg/kg 4 times daily. IM/IV: Adult 0.6-2.7 g daily; max 4.8 g. Pneumocystis: 600 mg q8h. Malaria (Child): 7-13 mg/kg q8h; (Adult): 450 mg q8h. Acne: 2% gel BID.
precautions: Severe skin reactions (DRESS, SJS, TEN) reported. Endocarditis prophylaxis: use only for high-risk.
interactions: Increases effects of atracurium (pharmacodynamic synergism). Risk of respiratory depression.

name: LINEZOLID
uses: Pneumonia (when glycopeptides/vancomycin cannot be used), complicated skin/soft tissue infections.
side_effects: Diarrhea, pseudomembranous colitis, vaginal candidiasis, visual field defect, pancytopenia.
dosage: Adult: 600 mg q12h (10-14 days; max 28 days). Child: 10 mg/kg TID. Preterm infant: 10 mg/kg BID. IV: 600 mg q12h.
precautions: Monitor visual function if >28 days. Weekly FBC monitoring. Avoid tyramine-rich foods (mature cheese, yeast, soy, undistilled alcohol). Plasma concentration reduced by rifampin.
interactions: Reduced by rifampicin. Avoid with MAOI, SSRIs, TCAs (wait 2 weeks).

name: AZITHROMYCIN
uses: Community-acquired pneumonia, lyme disease, URTI, otitis media, skin/soft tissue, non-gonococcal urethritis, multi-drug resistant typhoid, pharyngitis (penicillin allergy).
side_effects: Headache, drowsiness, arthralgia, taste/vision disturbance, pancreatitis.
dosage: Susceptible: 500 mg once daily for 3 days; Child: 10 mg/kg. Prophylaxis: 15 mg/kg stat. Non-gonococcal: 1 g single dose. Typhoid: 500 mg once daily for 7 days. Lyme: 500 mg daily for 7-10 days.
precautions: Caution in renal/cardiac disease. Not for otitis media <6 months or pharyngitis <2 years. Avoid sunlight. Take suspension 1 hour before or 2 hours after meal.

name: CLARITHROMYCIN
uses: URTI, skin/soft tissue, otitis media, H. pylori eradication (with PPI), pharyngitis.
side_effects: Tooth and tongue discoloration, smell and taste disturbances, hyperhydrosis, insomnia.
dosage: URTI: Adult 250 mg q12h for 7 days (Severe: 500 mg q12h for 14 days). Child: 15 mg/kg BID for 10 days. H. pylori: 250-500 mg BID. Tonsillitis (penicillin allergy): 250 mg q12h for 10 days.
precautions: Use in pregnancy only if benefit outweighs risk.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to macrolides, torsade de pointes, QT prolongation.

name: ERYTHROMYCIN
uses: Lyme disease, chronic prostatitis, pertussis, diphtheria, rheumatic fever recurrence, acute laryngitis.
side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, skin rashes, fever, cholestatic hepatitis (primarily with estolate form).
dosage: Lyme: 500 mg QID for 14-21 days. Prostatitis: 250-500 mg QID. Diphtheria (non-immune): 500 mg q6h for 7-17 days. Acne: 500 mg BID for 3 months. Syphilis: 500 mg QID for 14 days. Child (Amoebiosis): 30-50 mg/kg/day.
precautions: Monitor hepatic function in previous liver disease. QT prolongation risk.
contraindications: Macrolide hypersensitivity, history of cholestatic jaundice.
interactions: Potentiates effects of carbamazepine, corticosteroids, digoxin, theophylline, sildenafil.

name: CIPROFLOXACIN
uses: Complicated/uncomplicated UTIs, prostatitis, airway disease, typhoid, gonorrhea, diffuse otitis externa, surgical prophylaxis.
side_effects: Pancreatitis, tachycardia, tinnitus, joint/cartilage damage, tendinitis, tendon rupture.
dosage: URTI/UTI: 250-500 mg BID. Gonorrhea: 500 mg single dose. Prostatitis: 500 mg BID for 28 days. Otitis externa: 500 mg BID for 7 days. Surgical Prophylaxis: 750 mg 60-90 min before procedure. Child (UTI): 10-30 mg/kg daily divided.
precautions: Caution in epilepsy or history of epilepsy, renal/hepatic impairment.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to quinolones, children under 12 years (unless benefit outweighs risk), breastfeeding.
interactions: Antacids reduce absorption. Concomitant use with warfarin prolongs PT.

name: LEVOFLOXACIN
uses: Prostatitis, UTI, chronic bronchitis, community-acquired pneumonia, skin/soft tissue, bacterial sinusitis, pharyngitis.
side_effects: See under CIPROFLOXACIN; also hypoglycemia and pneumonitis.
dosage: UTI: 250 mg daily for 7-10 days. Bronchitis: 250-500 mg daily. Prostatitis: 500 mg once daily for 28 days. Pneumonia: 500 mg daily for 7-14 days. Child (Pneumonia): 10-15 mg/kg single dose.
precautions: Monitor convulsions, tendon weakness, MI, atrial fibrillation, colitis. Administer 4 hours before or 2 hours after antacids, iron, zinc.

name: MOXIFLOXACIN
uses: Sinusitis, pneumonia, bronchitis, PID, tuberculosis.
side_effects: Angina, arrhythmias, hyperlipidemia, vasodilation, xerostomia.
dosage: Adult: 400 mg once daily. Sinusitis: 7 days. Pneumonia/PID: 7-14 days. Bronchitis: 5-10 days.
precautions: Assess ECG, renal impairment, epilepsy. Monitor for pseudomembranous colitis.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, uncontrolled hypokalemia, prolonged QT interval.
interactions: Probenecid increases levels. Increases warfarin and cyclosporine effect. Seizure risk with NSAIDs.

name: NALIDIXIC ACID
uses: Urinary tract infections.
side_effects: Cranial nerve palsy, increase in intra-cranial pressure, metabolic acidosis, toxic psychosis.
dosage: 900 mg q6h for 7 days (reduce to 600 mg for chronic). Child (>3 mo): max 50 mg/kg daily divided. Prolonged: 30 mg/kg daily.
precautions: See under CIPROFLOXACIN.

name: NORFLOXACIN
uses: Uncomplicated UTI, recurrent UTI prophylaxis, chronic prostatitis.
side_effects: Epiphora. See under CIPROFLOXACIN.
dosage: UTI: 400 mg BID for 7-10 days. Chronic Relapsing: 400 mg BID for 12 weeks. Prostatitis: 400 mg BID for 28 days. Child: 10-15 mg/kg/day divided.
precautions: Risk of tendon rupture.

name: OFLOXACIN
uses: UTI, prostatitis, MDR-TB, PID, septicemia, skin, otitis externa/media.
side_effects: See under CIPROFLOXACIN.
dosage: Skin: 400 mg BID for 10 days. PID: 400 mg BID for 14 days. Septicemia: Inj 200 mg BID (up to 400 mg). UTI: 200-400 mg daily. Non-gonococcal: 400 mg daily for 7 days. Otitis externa: 10 drops daily for 7 days.
precautions: See under CIPROFLOXACIN.

name: COTRIMOXAZOLE (SULPHAMETHOXAZOLE and TRIMETHOPRIM)
uses: Uncomplicated lower UTI, prostatitis, bronchitis (H. influenzae/Strep), otitis media, maxillary sinusitis, Pneumocystis carinii pneumonia.
side_effects: Erythema multiform (SJS), leucopenia, granulocytopenia, glossitis, megaloblastic anaemia.
dosage: Oral (Adult): 960 mg q12h. Child: 5-8 mg/kg/day trimethoprim + 25-50 mg/kg/day sulfamethoxazole divided. Pneumocystis (High dose): 120 mg/kg daily for 14 days. Prophylaxis (Adult): 960 mg daily.
precautions: Monitor for pseudomembranous colitis. Risk of crystalluria; maintain 1.5L urine output daily.
contraindications: Blood donors, infants <6 weeks, G-6PD deficiency, hypersensitivity, pregnancy, lactation.

name: DOXYCYCLINE
uses: UTI, acne, early syphilis, late latent syphilis, non-gonococcal urethritis, anthrax prophylaxis, Lyme disease, periodontitis, lymphangioma.
side_effects: See under Tetracyclines.
dosage: UTI: 200 mg day 1, then 100 mg daily. Acne: 100 mg daily (6-12 weeks). Syphilis (Early): 100 mg BID for 14 days; (Late): 200 mg BID for 28 days. Non-gonococcal: 100 mg BID for 7 days. Periodontitis: 20 mg BID for 3 months. Lymphangioma: 10-20 mg/ml injection.
precautions: Avoid breastfeeding. Caution in hepatic impairment, excessive sunlight, and sulfite hypersensitivity.
interactions: Increases effects of digoxin, anticoagulants, methotrexate. Decreased by antacids, dairy, iron, cholestyramine, rifampin. Decreases effects of penicillin and OCPs.

name: MINOCYCLINE
uses: Acne vulgaris, Gonococcal Infection.
side_effects: N/A
dosage: Gonococcal: 100 mg BID. Acne: 50 mg BID for min 6 weeks.
precautions: Monitor dialysis and hypertension.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, breastfeeding, children, renal/hepatic impairment, bladder obstruction.
interactions: Increases effects of warfarin, digoxin, insulin, neuromuscular blockers. Risk of pseudo-tumor cerebri with retinoids.

name: OXYTETRACYCLINE
uses: See under TETRACYCLINE.
side_effects: See under TETRACYCLINE.
dosage: 250-500 mg every 6 hours.
precautions: See under TETRACYCLINE.

name: TETRACYCLINE
uses: Chronic bronchitis, sinusitis, chlamydial infections (NGU, trachoma), acne, brucellosis, cholera, syphilis (penicillin allergy), diabetic diarrhea, rosacea.
side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, urticaria, glossitis, fungal superinfection (in periodontitis).
dosage: Infections: 250 mg q6h (up to 500 mg q8h severe). Acne (Adult/Child 12-17): 500 mg BID for 3 months. Syphilis: 500 mg q6h for 15 days. Rosacea: 500 mg BID for 6-12 weeks.
precautions: Renal/Hepatic impairment, UV exposure.
interactions: Fatal nephrotoxicity with methoxyflurane. Increases digoxin/warfarin effects. Decreased by iron, antacids, cimetidine, dairy.

name: VANCOMYCIN
uses: Clostridium difficile infection, gram-positive infections (endocarditis, osteomyelitis, septicaemia, soft-tissue), surgical prophylaxis (MRSA risk).
side_effects: Red man syndrome (flushing upper body), blood disorders (reversible neutropenia), ototoxicity (discontinue if tinnitus occurs), cardiac arrest on rapid infusion.
dosage: C. difficile (Oral): 125 mg 4 times daily for 10-14 days (max 500 mg TID). Gram-positive (IV): Adult 1-1.5 g q12h; Elderly 500 mg q12h. Prophylaxis: 1 g IV.
precautions: Monitor plasma trough levels: 10-15 mg/L (15-20 in MRSA). Avoid extravasation (necrosis). Adjust dose in renal impairment. Use caution in pregnancy.
interactions: Cross-sensitivity with teicoplanin. Avoid with bacitracin, BCG, typhoid vaccine.

name: AMPHOTERICIN B
uses: Intestinal candidiasis, oral/perioral infections, severe systemic/deep mycosis, aspergillosis, visceral leishmaniasis, febrile neutropenia.
side_effects: Chills, fever, hypokalemia, convulsions, anaphylactoid reactions.
dosage: Aspergillosis (Liposomal): IV test dose 1 mg, then 3 mg/kg daily. Visceral Leishmaniasis: 1-3 mg/kg daily for 10-21 days (cumulative 21-30 mg/kg) or 3 mg/kg for 5 days. Systemic (Adult): IV test 1 mg, then 250 mcg/kg increasing to 1 mg/kg. Oropharyngeal: 0.1 mg/ml rinse q8h.
precautions: Monitor hepatic/renal function tests and plasma electrolytes. Notify doctor of soft tissue swelling or bruising.
interactions: Increased hepatotoxicity/ototoxicity with cidofovir. Increased nephrotoxicity with aminoglycosides, vancomycin, cisplatin. Hypokalemia with steroids, digoxin, diuretics.

name: CLOTRIMAZOLE
uses: Candidiasis, Tinea infections, Otomycosis.
side_effects: Vaginal burning, rash, pruritus.
dosage: Vaginal: 100 mg for 6 days or 200 mg for 3 days or 500 mg single dose. Otomycosis: 3 drops TID for 7-10 days. Oropharyngeal: 10 mg tablet mix in water 5 times daily.
precautions: Ophthalmic use. Do not use near eyes, nose, or mouth.

name: FLUCONAZOLE
uses: Invasive candidal infections, cryptococcal infections (meningitis), balanitis, dermal/oropharyngeal candidiasis.
side_effects: Diarrhoea, headache, nausea, rash.
dosage: Recurrent Vaginal: 150 mg q12h (3 doses) then 150 mg weekly for 6 months. Mucosal: 50-100 mg daily (7-14 days). Tinea: 50 mg daily for 2-4 weeks. Cryptococcal (Adult): 400 mg day 1, then 200-400 mg daily (min 8 weeks). Child: 6-12 mg/kg. Prevention in immunocompromised: 50-400 mg daily.
precautions: Monitor liver function. If used for oral candidiasis, don’t rinse mouth for 15-30 mins after use. Use alternative contraception.
interactions: Increases anticoagulation (warfarin), increases levels of phenytoin, theophylline, zidovudine, methadone, fentanyl. PPIs decrease fluconazole effects.

name: GRISEOFULVIN
uses: Dermatophyte infections.
side_effects: Heartburn, photosensitivity, skin rashes.
dosage: Tinea capitis (Adult): 1 g daily. Child: 15-20 mg/kg daily (max 1 g). Failed topical therapy: 500 mg daily.
precautions: Avoid breastfeeding. May impair driving. Use alternative contraception.
interactions: Decreases effect of warfarin and OCPs. Phenobarbitone decreases griseofulvin effects. Enhances alcohol effects.

name: ITRACONAZOLE
uses: Systemic candidiasis, onychomycosis, aspergillosis, histoplasmosis, esophageal candidiasis (HIV+), cryptococcal meningitis.
side_effects: Hyperglycemia (IV use), hepatitis, hypokalemia, SJS, visual disturbances.
dosage: Recurrent Vulvovaginal: 50-100 mg daily for 6 months. Onychomycosis: 200 mg daily for 3 months (alternately 200 mg BID for 7 days then 21-day break). Aspergillosis: 200 mg BID. Histoplasmosis: 200 mg TID for 3 days then 200 mg 1-2 times daily. Oropharyngeal (HIV+): 100 mg BID for 2 weeks.
precautions: Caution in renal/hepatic impairment, achlorhydria, dialysis, hearing loss. Potential for life-threatening hepatotoxicity.
interactions: Increased toxicity with benzodiazepines, digoxin, statins, warfarin. Decreased by antacids, H2 antagonists, PPIs.

name: KETOCONAZOLE
uses: Candidiasis, coccidioidomycosis, histoplasmosis, paracoccidioidomycosis, tinea, seborrheic dermatitis, dandruff.
side_effects: Irritation, stinging, pustules, pruritus.
dosage: Systemic/Candidiasis (Adult): 200-400 mg/day for 1-2 weeks. Seborrheic: foam/gel BID for 4 weeks. Dandruff (Shampoo): massage for 1 min, rinse; 2 times per week for 8 weeks.
precautions: Hepatic impairment (monitor ALT/AST/bilirubin). Avoid driving if dizziness occurs. Topical: wash hands before/after; don't wash area for 3 hours after application.
interactions: Decreased by H2 blockers, PPIs, antacids. Increases effect of phenytoin, warfarin, digoxin, omeprazole, statins.

name: NYSTATIN
uses: Oral, esophageal, intestinal, vaginal, cutaneous, corneal candidiasis.
side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea (at high doses).
dosage: Vaginal: Pessary 100,000 IU at night. Intestinal (Adult): 500,000 units q6h; (Child): 100,000 units QID. Cutaneous: apply cream BID.
precautions: If used for oral candidiasis, don't rinse mouth for 15-30 mins after use.

name: ALBENDAZOLE
uses: Ascaris, pinworm, hookworm, whipworm, strongyloides, Echinococcus granulosus, neurocysticercosis.
side_effects: Gastro-intestinal discomfort, headache.
dosage: Single/Mixed Nematode: 400 mg single dose. Strongyloidiasis: 400 mg BID for 3 days. Enterobiasis (Child 2+): 400 mg repeated after 14 days. E. granulosus: 800 mg daily (divided) for 1-6 months; Child: 15 mg/kg. Neurocysticercosis (>60 kg): 800 mg daily for 8-30 days; (<60 kg): 15 mg/kg daily.
precautions: Avoid pregnancy for one month after use (fetal harm risk). Take with food.
contraindications: First trimester of pregnancy, children <1 year.
interactions: Reduced by carbamazepine, phenytoin, ritonavir. Increased by corticosteroids.

name: MEBENDAZOLE
uses: Threadworm, roundworm, hookworm, whipworm.
side_effects: Abdominal pain, diarrhea, rash. Worms may be expelled through mouth/nose in heavy infection.
dosage: Whipworm (Adult/Child): 100 mg BID for 3 days. Threadworm (Child 2+): 100 mg single dose (repeat after 2 weeks). Round/Hookworm: 100 mg BID for 3 days.
precautions: Breast-feeding, IBD, hepatic disease. Monitor AST, ALT, ALP, BUN, CBC.
interactions: Decreased effect by carbamazepine, hydantoins. Increased absorption with high fat meal.

name: MILTEFOSINE
uses: Visceral and cutaneous leishmaniasis.
side_effects: Vomiting, diarrhea, reversible rise in hepatic transaminases/serum creatinine.
dosage: Oral (>25 kg): 100 mg daily for 28 days. Child: 2.5 mg/kg daily.
precautions: Encourage fluid intake. Advise effective non-hormonal contraception.
interactions: Combination with paromomycin/Amphotericin B prevents resistance.

name: NICLOSAMIDE
uses: Tapeworm (Taenia solium, saginata, H. nana, Diphyllobothrium latum).
side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort, pruritus.
dosage: T. solium (Adult/Child 6+): 2 g single dose after breakfast + purgative 2 hours later; (Child 2-6): 1 g; (<2): 500 mg. H. nana (Adult/Child 6+): 2 g day 1, then 1 g daily for 6 days.
precautions: Inactive against cysticercosis cellulose; danger of cysticercosis in T. solium. Avoid alcohol during treatment.
interactions: Alcohol enhances its absorption and adverse effects.

name: PENTAMIDINE
uses: Visceral leishmaniasis, Pneumocystis pneumonia.
side_effects: Acute renal failure, hyperkalaemia, megaloblastic anaemia, acute pancreatitis, pain at site.
dosage: Leishmaniasis: deep IM 3-4 mg/kg on alternate days (max 10 injections). Pneumonia: IV infusion 4 mg/kg daily for 14 days.
precautions: Blood dyscrasias, renal/hepatic disease, diabetes, hypocalcemia. Monitor blood counts.
interactions: Increases nephrotoxicity of vancomycin/cisplatin. QT prolongation with class III antiarrhythmics/chloroquine. Myelosuppression with radiation.

name: PIPERAZINE
uses: Ascariasis, enterobiasis.
side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, urticaria.
dosage: Ascariasis: max 3.5 g/day; Child 75 mg/kg for 2 consecutive days. Enterobiasis: max 2.5 g/day; Child 65 mg/kg for 7 days.
precautions: Pregnancy, breastfeeding (use only if no alternative). Treat all household members concurrently for pinworms. Wash bedding/nightclothes.
interactions: Enhances phenothiazines; risk of seizures. Antagonistic to Pyrantel Pamoate.

name: PRAZIQUANTEL
uses: Taeniasis (T. solium/saginata), hymenolepiasis, diphyllobothriasis, Schistosoma haematobium/japonicum.
side_effects: Rectal bleeding, urticaria, dizziness.
dosage: T. solium: 10-20 mg/kg single dose. H. nana: 25 mg/kg single dose. S. haematobium: oral 20 mg/kg, then 20 mg/kg after 4-6 hours. S. japonicum: 20 mg/kg TID for 1 day.
precautions: Discontinue if cerebral cysticercosis present. Do not drive for 24 hours after treatment.
interactions: Reduced by chloroquine/dexamethasone. Increased by grapefruit/cimetidine.

name: PYRANTEL PAMOATE
uses: Ascariasis, hookworm, pinworm.
side_effects: Headache, dizziness, drowsiness, mild GI disturbance.
dosage: Adult/Child (>2 yrs): single 10 mg/kg (max 1 g). Pinworms: repeat after 2 weeks. Treat entire household.
precautions: Hepatic impairment, lactation. Wear tight underwear both day and night while taking.

name: SODIUM STIBOGLUCONATE
uses: Leishmaniasis.
side_effects: Skin rashes, vomiting, abdominal pain, severe cough.
dosage: 20 mg/kg daily (max 850 mg) for at least 20 days (IM/IV). Skin lesions: treat for 10 days.
precautions: Withdraw if conduction disturbances occur. Monitor ECG. Rapid IV injection can result in cardiovascular collapse.

name: CLOFAZIMINE
uses: Multibacillary leprosy (with rifampicin/dapsone), Type II lepra reaction.
side_effects: Red discoloration of skin, feces, urine, and infant skin; dry eyes, dry skin, phototoxicity.
dosage: Adult (Multibacillary): supervised 300 mg once a month + self-administered 50 mg daily for 1 year.
precautions: Avoid if persistent abdominal pain/diarrhea. May discolor soft contact lenses. Risk of ventricular arrhythmias with bedaquiline.

name: DAPSONE
uses: Leprosy, dermatitis herpetiformis, Pneumocystis pneumonia prophylaxis, rhinosporidiosis recurrence.
side_effects: Hemolytic anaemia (G6PD deficiency), anorexia, nausea, vomiting.
dosage: Multibacillary: 100 mg daily for 1 year. Paucibacillary: 100 mg daily for 6 months. Child (<35 kg): 50 mg or 1-2 mg/kg. Pneumocystis: 100 mg daily.
precautions: N/A
contraindications: Cardiac disease, G6PD deficiency, pulmonary disease.
interactions: Pregnancy- Neonatal methemoglobinemia reported in 3rd trimester.

name: ARTEMETHER with LUMEFANTRINE
uses: Acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria, chloroquine-resistant non-falciparum malaria.
side_effects: Palpitation, anorexia, abdominal pain, rash.
dosage: Adult/Child (>12 yrs): 4 tabs then 5 doses of 4 tabs at 8, 24, 36, 48, 60 hrs (Total 24 tabs) with food. Child (5-14 kg): 1 tab initially then 5 further doses. (Detailed weight brackets in formulary).
precautions: If trouble swallowing, tablet may be crushed. Dizziness may affect tasks.

name: ARTESUNATE
uses: P. falciparum malaria, especially multidrug resistance.
side_effects: Drug induced fever, neutropenia, cardiotoxicity (high dose), hemolysis (2 wks post-treatment).
dosage: IV/IM: Loading 2 mg/kg, then 1 mg/kg at 4 and 24 hours. Thereafter 1 mg/kg daily until patient tolerates oral (max 7 days).
precautions: Must be used immediately after reconstitution; discard if cloudy. Protect from light.

name: CHLOROQUINE
uses: Malaria chemoprophylaxis/treatment, RA, lupus erythematosus.
side_effects: Epigastric discomfort, pruritus, reversible visual disturbance.
dosage: Prophylaxis: 300 mg base once weekly (start 1 wk before, end 4 wks after). Presumptive Treatment: 600 mg base + 45 mg primaquine. Radical Cure (Relapsing): 600 mg base, then 300 mg at 6, 24, 48 hrs + 15 mg primaquine (15 days). RA/Lupus: 150 mg daily.
precautions: Baseline and periodic ophthalmic test (>150 mg/day).
contraindications: Retinal field changes, auditory damage, torsade de pointes, G6PD deficiency, seizures.
interactions: Cimetidine reduces clearance. Increases QT with antiarrhythmics. Increases 2D6 inhibitors/CYP3A inhibitors. Chloroquine decreases rabies vaccine effects.

name: MEFLOQUINE
uses: Treatment and prophylaxis of Malaria (P. falciparum/P. vivax).
side_effects: Tinnitus, bradycardia, extrasystoles, dizziness, vertigo.
dosage: Prophylaxis: 250 mg weekly (start 2.5 wks before, end 4 wks after). Long term (>3 mo): on individual assessment. Child (<15 kg): not recommended.
precautions: Cardiac conduction disorder, brain injury. Disturbed balance may persist for months after stopping.
contraindications: History of convulsion, psychiatric disorder, infants <3 months, pregnancy.
interactions: Avoid beta-blockers/calcium channel blockers (risk of bradycardia).

name: PRIMAQUINE
uses: Adjunct in P. vivax and P. ovale malaria.
side_effects: Abdominal cramps, vomiting, leucocytosis, haemolytic anaemia.
dosage: Presumptive: 45 mg single dose. Radical cure: 15 mg daily for 5 days; child 250 mcg/kg daily.
precautions: G6PD deficiency risk. Always give in conjunction with chloroquine.
contraindications: Children <1 yr, lupus, RA, methemoglobin reductase deficiency, bone marrow suppression.
interactions: Grapefruit decreases effect. Don't use with other drugs liable to induce hemolysis.

name: QUININE
uses: Treatment of uncomplicated malaria.
side_effects: Cinchonism (tinnitus, temporary blindness, blurred vision, hot skin), hypoglycemia, nephrotoxicity.
dosage: Oral: Adult 300-600 mg q8h for 5-7 days; Child 25 mg/kg. IV Infusion (if unable to swallow): Loading 900 mg - 1.4 g over 4 hrs, then 300-600 mg q8h.
precautions: Monitor blood glucose/electrolytes during IV use.
contraindications: Myasthenia gravis, optic neuritis, digoxin toxicity, blood dyscrasia.
interactions: Additive vagolytic effect with anticholinergics. QT prolongation by macrolides/quinolones.

name: SULFADOXINE and PYRIMETHAMINE
uses: Combination therapy in P. falciparum malaria.
side_effects: Hyperkalemia, rash, headache.
dosage: Treatment: adult 3 tablets single dose; child: 1.25 mg/kg pyrimethamine and 25 mg/kg sulphadoxine.
precautions: Predisposition to folate deficiency or hyperkalemia. Maintain fluid intake to avert crystalluria.
contraindications: Acute porphyrias, sulfonamide allergy, infants <6 weeks.
interactions: Folic acid decreases effects. Increases chlorpromazine levels.

name: ETHAMBUTOL
uses: Tuberculosis in combination.
side_effects: Optic neuritis (reversible; dose-dependent), hyperuricemia, joint pain.
dosage: 15-25 mg/kg daily.
precautions: Check visual acuity (Snellen chart) and renal function before treatment. Monitor children ophthalmologically.
contraindications: Children <5 yrs, optic neuritis, severe renal impairment.
interactions: Decreases live BCG vaccine effects. Aluminium hydroxide increases levels.

name: ISONIAZID
uses: Tuberculosis in combination, TB prophylaxis.
side_effects: Peripheral neuritis (common), hepatic damage, skin rash.
dosage: 300 mg daily; Child: 10 mg/kg daily (max 300 mg).
precautions: Assessment of liver damage monthly. Administer Pyridoxine (25-100 mg daily) to prevent peripheral neuropathy. Caution in alcohol dependence (assess liver in first 2 months).
interactions: Increases toxicity with alcohol, cycloserine, rifampin, phenytoin. Serotonin syndrome risk with SSRIs. Aluminium antacids decrease absorption.

name: PYRAZINAMIDE
uses: Tuberculosis.
side_effects: Hepatotoxicity, hyperuricemia, sideroblastic anaemia, thrombocytopenia.
dosage: Adult (<50 kg): 1.5 g/day; (>50 kg): 2 g/day. Child: 25-35 mg/kg daily.
precautions: Assess RFT and LFT at onset. Monitor for gout.

name: RIFAMPIN
uses: Short course chemo for TB and leprosy, meningococcal prophylaxis, H. influenzae, atrophic rhinitis.
side_effects: Flu-like syndrome, thrombocytopenic purpura, transient rise in bilirubin.
dosage: TB (>50 kg): 600 mg daily. Leprosy (Multibacillary): 600 mg once monthly supervised. Meningococcal Prophylaxis: 600 mg q12h for 2 days. Child (>1 yr): 10 mg/kg. Atrophic Rhinitis: 600 mg daily for 12 weeks.
precautions: Induces hepatic enzymes. Urine, saliva, feces, sputum, sweat, and tears may be colored red-orange; soft contact lenses permanently stained. Avoid alcohol.
interactions: Accelerates metabolism of corticosteroids, digitalis, OCPs, oral hypoglycemics. Increases hepatotoxicity with isoniazid. Don't use with protease inhibitors.

name: STREPTOMYCIN
uses: TB resistant to other treatment, brucellosis, bacterial endocarditis.
side_effects: Vestibular damage (increases with dose and age >40), nephrotoxicity, skin rashes.
dosage: Adult: 0.75 g daily; child 15-20 mg/kg IM.
precautions: Avoid whenever possible in pregnancy/elderly. See under GENTAMICIN.

name: BEDAQUILINE
uses: Combination regimen for pulmonary MDR-TB when other treatments are not available.
side_effects: Arthralgia, nausea, QT interval prolongation, myalgia.
dosage: Adult: 400 mg once daily for 2 weeks, then 200 mg 3 times a week (at least 48 hrs between doses) for 22 weeks.
precautions: Monitor ECG baseline and at least monthly (QT prolongation risk). Caution in cardiac impairment, heart failure, syncope, thyroid disease.
interactions: Increases QT with class IA/III antiarrhythmics, haloperidol, chloroquine. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase effect (avoid >14 days). Lopinavir/ritonavir increase adverse reactions.

name: CAPREOMYCIN
uses: TB resistant to 1st line drugs.
side_effects: Induration at site, hearing loss with tinnitus/vertigo, leucocytosis, leucopenia, nephrotoxicity.
dosage: Deep IM (Adult): 1 g daily (max 20 mg/kg) for 2-4 months, then 1 g 2-3 times a week.
precautions: Monitor renal, hepatic, auditory and vestibular function. Caution in breastfeeding/elderly.
interactions: Increased nephrotoxicity/ototoxicity with colistin, polymyxins, vancomycin, aminoglycosides.

name: CYCLOSERINE
uses: TB resistant to 1st line drugs.
side_effects: Confusion, convulsions, tremor, allergic dermatitis, megaloblastic anemia.
dosage: Initially 250 mg q12h for 2 weeks, then 500 mg q12h. Child: 10 mg/kg/day divided.
precautions: Blood concentration monitoring required (should not exceed 30 mg/litre). Monitor hematological/renal function.
contraindications: Alcohol dependence, depression, epilepsy, psychotic states.
interactions: Alcohol increases convulsion risk. Isoniazid increases CNS toxicity.

name: ETHIONAMIDE
uses: Second line drug for TB.
side_effects: Gynaecomastia, hypoglycemia, impotence, peripheral neuropathy, optic neuritis.
dosage: Initial 250 mg/day for 1-2 days, then 250 mg BID for 1-2 days, then gradual increase to highest tolerated. Avg 750 mg/day; max 1 g/day in divided doses.
precautions: Pregnancy, lactation, psychiatric cases.
interactions: Increases toxicity with cycloserine. Increases isoniazid levels. Decreases magnesium oxide effect.

name: KANAMYCIN
uses: 2nd line drug in TB.
side_effects: See under GENTAMICIN.
dosage: IM: 250 mg q6h or 500 mg q12h. IV Infusion: 15-30 mg/kg q8-12h.
precautions: See under GENTAMICIN.
contraindications: Pregnancy, renal impairment, myasthenia gravis, cochlear implant.

name: P-AMINOSALICYLIC ACID (PAS)
uses: 2nd line drugs in TB.
side_effects: Epigastric pain, goiter, blood dyscrasias.
dosage: Granules: 4 g or 9.2 g sachet. Tablet: 500 mg.
precautions: Take with meals to decrease epigastric pain.

name: ENTECAVIR
uses: Chronic hepatitis B (HBV).
side_effects: Raised serum amylase/lipase, sleep disturbances, alopecia, thrombocytopenia.
dosage: Compensated liver (Naive): 0.5 mg once daily. Lamivudine-resistant: 1 mg once daily. Decompensated liver: 1 mg once daily.
precautions: Reduce dose if eGFR <50 ml/min. Monitor liver function every 3 months. Recurrent hepatitis may occur on discontinuation.

name: PEGINTERFERON ALFA
uses: Combined with ribavirin for chronic Hep C, monotherapy for Hep C or Hep B.
side_effects: Anorexia, lethargy, arrhythmias, cardiovascular problems, myelosuppression, psoriasiform rash, seizures (elderly high dose).
dosage: Adult: SC 1.5 mcg/kg/week (max 150 mcg/week). Naive/Relapsed: 12 weeks. Non-responders: up to 24 weeks.
precautions: Monitor lipid concentration. Monitoring closely in mild-moderate hepatic impairment. Renal impairment: reduce dose.

name: SOFOSBUVIR
uses: Chronic hepatitis C.
side_effects: Hyperbilirubinemia, headache, fatigue, anaemia.
dosage: Oral: 400 mg once daily.
precautions: Use two forms of reliable contraceptives. Avoid breastfeeding.
interactions: Decreased by P-glycoprotein inducers (carbamazepine, rifampin). Bradycardia with amiodarone. Increased by carvedilol.

name: ACYCLOVIR
uses: Herpes infections, mucocutaneous HSV, infectious mononucleosis, Varicella, Herpes zoster.
side_effects: Rashes, urticaria, increase in blood urea/creatinine, fatigue.
dosage: HSV Treatment: 200 mg 5 times daily (5 days). Recurrence prevention: 200 mg QID or 400 mg BID. Varicella/Zoster (Adult): 800 mg 5 times daily (7 days); (Child): 20 mg/kg. Mucocutaneous: 400 mg 5 times daily. Topical: apply every 4 hrs.
precautions: Caution in renal impairment. Do not give concurrently with live vaccines. Immunization should be up to date before treatment.
interactions: Increases serious infections when used with TNF-alpha blockers.

name: OSELTAMIVIR
uses: Prevention and treatment of influenza A or B.
side_effects: Seizures, toxic epidermolysis necrolysis, SJS.
dosage: Influenza: 75 mg twice daily for 5 days. Prevention: 75 mg once daily for 10 days. Post-exposure Prophylaxis: up to 6 weeks.
precautions: Avoid use with H1N1 virus vaccine or intranasal influenza vaccine.

name: DIDANOSINE
uses: HIV infection.
side_effects: Acute renal failure, optic nerve changes, parotid gland enlargement, gynaecomastia.
dosage: Oral Adult (60 kg): 250 mg daily (1-2 divided doses); (>60 kg): 400 mg daily. Take 2 hours before or after food.
precautions: Monitor annually: visual acuity, color vision, dilated fundus. Risk of peripheral neuropathy (dose-related). Sodium restricted diets caution. Monitor amylase.
interactions: Increased by allopurinol, tenofovir. Pancreatitis risk increased by stavudine. Decreased absorption by antacids, ketoconazole, dapsone, quinolones.

name: EFAVIRENZ
uses: HIV infections.
side_effects: Rash, SJS, depression, ataxia, cognitive impairment.
dosage: 600 mg once daily (Adult/Child >40 kg).
precautions: Moderate-severe hepatic impairment. Monitor liver function if co-administering hepatotoxic drugs. If dose missed, take as remembered; do not double.
interactions: Increased CNS depression with alcohol, antidepressants. Increases ritonavir/estrogens. Increases warfarin/statins. Decreases OCPs, ketoconazole.

name: INDINAVIR
uses: See under SAQUINAVIR.
side_effects: Hyperglycemia, pancreatitis, paraesthesia.
dosage: 800 mg q8h. Child: 500 mg/m2 q8h (max 800 mg q8h).
precautions: Ensure adequate hydration (risk of nephrolithiasis). Caution in diabetes, hemophilia, chronic Hep B/C.
interactions: Dysrhythmias with ergots, amiodarone. Increases statins (myopathy risk). Increased by CYP3A4 inhibitors. Decreased by CYP3A4 inducers (St. John's wort, rifamycins).

name: LAMIVUDINE
uses: HIV infection in combination.
side_effects: Alopecia, anaemia, peripheral neuropathy.
dosage: Adult: 150 mg BID or 300 mg daily. Infant (<1 mo): 2 mg/kg BID. Child (1 mo+): 4 mg/kg BID (max 300 mg).
precautions: Renal disease, pancreatitis, peripheral neuropathy. Caution in Hep B/C co-infection.
interactions: Increased by cotrimoxazole, amiloride, entecavir, metformin. Interferons decrease its effects.

name: LOPINAVIR + RITONAVIR
uses: HIV infection.
side_effects: Amenorrhoea, neuropathy, weight changes, anaphylaxis, myalgias.
dosage: Adult: Oral 400/100 mg BID (Alternatively 800/200 mg once daily if <3 protease mutations).
precautions: Monitor LFT, blood glucose, lipid profile. Monitor for cardiomyopathy, immune reconstitution syndrome. Not a cure; others can contract HIV from patient.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to polyoxyethylated castor oil (oral solution).
interactions: Increases toxicity of amiodarone, cisapride, clozapine, ergotamine, triazolam. Increases QT with local anesthetics/tricyclics. Ritonavir increases didanosine. Decreases OCPs.

name: NELFINAVIR
uses: HIV infection.
side_effects: Suicidal ideation, flatulence, hyperlipidemia.
dosage: 750 mg TID or 1250 mg BID.
precautions: Monitor serum lipids/blood glucose. Loperamide can be used for nelfinavir-induced diarrhea.
interactions: Severe dysrhythmias with amiodarone, quinidine. Increased by ketoconazole. Decreased by rifampicin, phenytoin, nevirapine. Decreases methadone and OCPs.

name: NEVIRAPINE
uses: HIV infection, PMTCT of HIV.
side_effects: SJS, hepatitis, fever, anaemia.
dosage: 200 mg daily for first 14 days, then 200 mg BID. Child (1 mo - 13 yrs): 120 mg/m2 daily for 14 days, then 200 mg/m2 BID.
precautions: Monitor liver function every 2 weeks for 2 months. Monitor skin reactions closely (first 18 weeks). Females at greater risk of hepatic side effects.
interactions: Increased by cimetidine, macrolides. Decreases OCPs, ketoconazole, methadone. Decreased by rifamycins, anticonvulsants.

name: RITONAVIR
uses: HIV infections.
side_effects: Decreased blood thyroxine, menorrhagia, seizures, syncope.
dosage: High-dose: Initially 300 mg q12h (3 days), increase to 600 mg q12h (within 14 days). Low-dose booster: 100-200 mg 1-2 times daily.
precautions: Monitor AST/ALT every 3 months in hepatic impairment.
contraindications: Hepatic impairment, pancreatitis, hemophilia, AV block, immune reconstitution syndrome.
interactions: Increases fluconazole. Decreased by rifamycins, phenytoin. Decreases anticoagulants, OCPs, divalproex.

name: SAQUINAVIR
uses: HIV infection in combination.
side_effects: Buccal and mucosal ulceration, peripheral neuropathy, changes in libido.
dosage: In combo with low-dose ritonavir: Adult 1 g q12h. In combo without low-dose ritonavir: Adult 500 mg q12h for 7 days, then 1 g q12h.
precautions: Monitor ECG (do not initiate if QT >450ms). Safety not established in children <16 yrs.
contraindications: Bradycardia, congenital QT prolongation, severe hepatic impairment.
interactions: Decreases anti-parkinsonism effects of levodopa. Clozapine increases risperidone effects.

name: STAVUDINE
uses: HIV infection in combination.
side_effects: Peripheral neuropathy (dose-related), pancreatitis, gynaecomastia, elevated serum amylase.
dosage: Adult (<60 kg): 30 mg q12h; (>60 kg): 40 mg q12h.
precautions: High risk of lipotrophy (especially with didanosine). Monitor for bone marrow suppression.
interactions: Decreased by probenecid, methadone. Increased peripheral neuropathy with lithium, dapsone, isoniazid, hydralazine.

name: TENOFOVIR DISOPROXIL
uses: HIV infection.
side_effects: Pancreatitis, neutropenia, hypophosphataemia, polyuria, renal failure.
dosage: Adult: 245 mg once daily.
precautions: Monitor RFT and serum phosphate before and during treatment (monthly for 1 yr). Not to breastfeed.
interactions: Increased by acyclovir, valacyclovir. Increases didanosine.

name: ZIDOVUDINE
uses: Prevention of maternal-fetal HIV transmission, HIV infections in combination.
side_effects: Bone marrow depression with severe anaemia, granulocytopenia, pancreatitis, gynaecomastia, myopathy.
dosage: Adult: 250-300 mg BID. Oral Child: 500-600 mg daily divided. IV: 0.8-1 mg/kg q4h. Maternal-Fetal: Mother (if CD4 <250) 300 mg + lamivudine 150 mg BID + nevirapine 200 mg once daily (start ASAP in pregnancy; for life). Neonate: 4 mg/kg BID for 7 days (continue for 4 weeks if mother had <4 wks HAART).
precautions: Monitor FBC monthly (initially) then q3 months.
contraindications: Granulocyte count <1000/mm3 or Hb <9.5 g/dl, severe renal disease.
interactions: Increased risk of toxicity with nephrotoxic/myelosuppressive drugs. Increased bone marrow depression with anti-neoplastics, clotrimazole. Increased by fluconazole, probenecid, valproic acid. Decreased by interferons, NRTIs.

name: BECLOMETHASONE
uses: Prophylaxis of bronchial asthma, prophylaxis and treatment of allergic rhinitis.
side_effects: Bronchospasm and wheezing, rash, Candida infections in mouth or throat.
dosage: See under respiratory system (Chapter 7).
precautions: See under respiratory system.

name: BETAMETHASONE
uses: Replacement therapy in adrenocortical insufficiency states, Cushing's syndrome, inflammatory and allergic conditions.
side_effects: Hypertension, sodium retention, potassium loss, muscle weakness, diabetes, osteoporosis, increased susceptibility to infection, mental disturbance, suppression of growth in children.
dosage: Oral: 0.5-5 mg daily; IM or slow IV injection/infusion: 4-20 mg, repeated up to 4 times in 24 hours; child: by slow IV injection, up to 1 year 1 mg, 1-5 years 2 mg, 6-12 years 4 mg.
precautions: Caution in cirrhosis, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, ocular herpes simplex, peptic ulcer.
contraindications: Untreated serious infections (except tubercular meningitis or septic shock), ITP, premature infants, baby on live vaccine.
interactions: Barbiturates, phenytoin, rifampicin may increase metabolism; antagonizes hypotensive effect of alpha-blockers, beta-blockers, and calcium channel blockers.

name: CORTISONE ACETATE
uses: Adrenocortical insufficiency.
side_effects: See under glucocorticoids general entry.
dosage: Oral, for replacement therapy: 25-37.5 mg in divided dose.
precautions: See under glucocorticoids general entry.

name: DEXAMETHASONE
uses: Inflammatory conditions, adrenal crisis, bacterial meningitis, cerebral edema.
side_effects: See under glucocorticoids general entry.
dosage: Physiological replacement (oral): Adult: 0.03-0.15 mg/kg/day in 2-4 divided doses; Anti-inflammatory (oral): adult: 0.75-9mg/day; Adrenal crisis: 4-10 mg/day as single dose; Bacterial meningitis (children >2 months): 0.6 mg/kg/day in 4 divided doses for 4 days; Cerebral edema: 10 mg IV followed by 4 mg 6 hourly.
precautions: Should be protected from light.

name: FLUDROCORTISONE ACETATE
uses: Mineralocorticoid replacement in adrenocortical insufficiency.
side_effects: See under glucocorticoids general entry.
dosage: Adrenocortical insufficiency: adult 50-300 µg daily; child 5 micrograms/kg daily.
precautions: N/A

name: HYDROCORTISONE
uses: Adrenocortical insufficiency, inflammatory and allergic conditions.
side_effects: See under glucocorticoids general entry.
dosage: Adult: by IM injection or slow IV injection or infusion: 100-500 mg, 3-4 times in 24 hours or as required; Child: by slow IV injection up to 1 year 25 mg, 1-5 year 50 mg, 6-12 years 100 mg.
precautions: Hydrocortisone acetate injection should be protected from light; container should be gently shaken before dose is withdrawn.

name: METHYLPREDNISOLONE
uses: See under prednisolone.
side_effects: See under prednisolone.
dosage: Oral: 2-40 mg daily; IM injection or slow IV injection or infusion: initially 100-500 mg.
precautions: See under prednisolone.

name: PREDNISOLONE
uses: Replacement therapy in adrenocortical insufficiency, inflammatory and allergic conditions.
side_effects: See under glucocorticoids general entry.
dosage: Oral: Adult 5-60 mg/day; children: 0.14-2 mg/kg/day in 3-4 divided doses. IV: 10-40 mg, 1-2 times weekly; IM: 100 mg, 1-2 times weekly.
precautions: Cushingoid side effects more likely with doses above 7.5 mg daily; should be protected from light.

name: TRIAMCINOLONE ACETONIDE
uses: Inflammatory and allergic conditions.
side_effects: See under glucocorticoids general entry.
dosage: By deep IM injection: 40 mg for depot effect, repeated at intervals according to response, maximum single dose 100 mg.
precautions: N/A

name: INSULIN ASPART
uses: Diabetes mellitus.
side_effects: Hypoglycaemia, localised allergic reactions, fat hypertrophy at injection sites.
dosage: By SC injection: immediately before meals or when necessary shortly after meals, according to requirements; By IV injection or infusion according to requirements.
precautions: Can be given during pregnancy and breastfeeding. Should be taken before meal or immediately after meal.

name: INSULIN GLARGINE
uses: Diabetes mellitus.
side_effects: Hypoglycaemia, localised allergic reactions, fat hypertrophy at injection sites.
dosage: By SC injections: start as 1/3rd of total daily insulin dose; use remaining 2/3 of daily dose on short-acting, premeal insulin. Usual initial dose: 0.2-0.4 units/kg.
precautions: Should be injected with evening meal. Optimal glucose lowering effect may take 5 days to fully manifest.

name: INSULIN ISOPHANE (NPH)
uses: Diabetes mellitus.
side_effects: Hypoglycaemia, localised allergic reactions, fat hypertrophy at injection sites.
dosage: By SC injection: according to patient’s requirements.
precautions: Intermediate duration of action.

name: INSULIN LISPRO
uses: Diabetes mellitus.
side_effects: Hypoglycaemia, localised allergic reactions, fat hypertrophy at injection sites.
dosage: SC injection: Start with 0.2-0.6 unit/kg/day in divided doses. Total maintenance daily requirement is usually between 0.5 and 1 unit/kg/day.
precautions: Recommended to start with lower dose to reduce risk of hypoglycemia.

name: INSULIN PROTAMINE ZINC (PZI)
uses: Diabetes mellitus.
side_effects: Hypoglycaemia, localised allergic reactions, fat hypertrophy at injection sites.
dosage: By SC injection: according to patient’s requirement as described under insulin glargine.
precautions: Long duration of action.

name: INSULIN SOLUBLE
uses: Diabetic ketoacidosis, diabetes mellitus.
side_effects: Hypoglycaemia, localised allergic reactions, fat hypertrophy at injection sites.
dosage: By SC, IM or IV injection: according to patient’s requirements.
precautions: Short duration with relatively rapid action.

name: INSULIN ZINC SUSPENSION (LENTE)
uses: Diabetes mellitus.
side_effects: Hypoglycaemia, localised allergic reactions, fat hypertrophy at injection sites.
dosage: By SC injection: according to patient’s requirements.
precautions: Intermediate (Lente) or Long (Ultralente) duration of action.

name: ACARBOSE
uses: Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
side_effects: Abdominal pain, flatulence, diarrhoea, jaundice.
dosage: Initially 50 mg/day, increased to 50 mg 3 times daily; then increased if necessary to 100 mg 3 times daily; maximum 200 mg 3 times daily.
precautions: N/A
contraindications: <18 years age, pregnancy, breast-feeding, hepatic impairment and severe renal impairment.
interactions: Used with caution with insulin and sulphonylureas (enhance hypoglycaemia).

name: METFORMIN
uses: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, gestational diabetes, polycystic ovarian syndrome.
side_effects: Anorexia, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, metallic taste, abdominal discomfort, vitamin B12 deficiency, hepatitis, and lactic acidosis (rare).
dosage: Adult and child over 10 years: initially 500 mg with breakfast for at least 1 week, then 500 mg q12h with or after food for at least 1 week; maximum 2 g daily in divided doses.
precautions: Suspend metformin on the morning of surgery and restart when baseline returns to normal.
contraindications: Renal impairment, hepatic impairment, recent MI, pregnancy, chronic alcoholics, ketoacidosis, general anaesthesia.

name: SITAGLIPTIN
uses: Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
side_effects: Hypoglycemia, acute pancreatitis, acute kidney injury, bundle branch block, exfoliative dermatitis, arthralgia.
dosage: Oral: 100 mg/day.
precautions: N/A

name: LIRAGLUTIDE
uses: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, chronic weight management.
side_effects: Hypoglycemia, tachycardia, headache, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, constipation.
dosage: Chronic weight management: SC injection 0.6 mg once daily for one week, increase weekly to target 3 mg once daily. Type 2 DM: SC 0.6 mg daily for 1 week then 1.2 mg once daily, may increase up to 1.8 mg daily.
precautions: Delay dose escalation if not tolerated. Discontinue if 3 mg dose not tolerated for weight management.
contraindications: Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 (MEN-2), personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC), breastfeeding.

name: REPAGLINIDE
uses: Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
side_effects: Hypoglycaemia, diarrhoea, constipation, abdominal pain, nausea, pruritus, vasculitis.
dosage: Initially 500 µg within 30 minutes before main meals, adjusted according to response at intervals of 1-2 weeks.
precautions: Substitute by insulin during peri-operative period and during intercurrent illness (MI, coma, infection); child and adolescent under 18 years not recommended.
contraindications: Ketoacidosis, pregnancy, breast-feeding, severe hepatic impairment.

name: CHLORPROPAMIDE
uses: Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
side_effects: Hypoglycaemia, nausea, vomiting, disulfiram-like reaction with alcohol, water intoxication (mental confusion, decreased sodium).
dosage: Initially 250 mg/day with breakfast or meal; maximum 500 mg daily.
precautions: Safety during pregnancy and breast-feeding has not been established.
contraindications: Ketoacidosis, diabetic coma, severe infection, severe kidney or liver impairment.

name: GLIBENCLAMIDE
uses: Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
side_effects: Hypoglycaemia, photosensitivity, hyponatremia, neonatal hypoglycaemia in first trimester use.
dosage: Initially 5 mg/day (elderly 2.5 mg) with breakfast or meal; maximum 15 mg daily.
precautions: See under chlorpropamide.
interactions: Signs of hypoglycaemia masked by beta-blockers. Flushing if taken with alcohol.

name: GLICLAZIDE
uses: Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
side_effects: See under glibenclamide.
dosage: Initially 40-80 mg daily with breakfast or meal; maximum 320 mg daily.
precautions: N/A

name: GLIMEPERIDE
uses: Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
side_effects: Hyponatremia. Also see under glibenclamide.
dosage: Initially 1 mg daily, max up to 4 mg daily.
precautions: Comparatively safer than other sulphonylureas.

name: GLIPIZIDE
uses: Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
