side_effects: Dizziness, drowsiness, hyponatremia, hepatic/renal impairment.
dosage: Initially 2.5-5 mg daily before breakfast or meal; maximum 20 mg daily.
precautions: To be ingested 30 min before breakfast because food decreases its absorption.

name: PIOGLITAZONE
uses: Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
side_effects: Anemia, peripheral edema, weight gain, impotence, risk of bladder cancer.
dosage: Initially 15-30 mg/day, increased to 45 mg/day according to response.
precautions: Substitute insulin during peri-operative period; ask patient to immediately report hematuria.
contraindications: Ketoacidosis, pregnancy, breast-feeding, hepatic impairment, cardiac failure, bladder cancer, uninvestigated macroscopic hematuria.

name: GLUCAGON
uses: Acute hypoglycaemia, insulin induced hypoglycemia, beta-blocker poisoning.
side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, hypotension, hypokalaemia.
dosage: SC, IM, or IV injection: adult/child over 8 years 1 mg. If no response after 15 minutes, IV glucose should be given.
precautions: Should be used immediately after preparation; discard if it shows gel formation.

name: LEVOTHYROXINE (L-THYROXINE)
uses: Cretinism, adult hypothyroidism, myxoedema coma, non-toxic goitre, thyroid carcinoma after surgery.
side_effects: Palpitation, tachycardia, diarrhoea, cardiac arrhythmias, tremor, weight loss, sweating, insomnia, increased appetite.
dosage: Initially 50-100 µg/day (before morning meal); Neonate (up to 1 month): 5-10 µg/kg/day; Child (>1 month): initially 5 µg/kg adjusted in steps of 25 µg.
precautions: Protect from light. Pregnancy/breast-feeding.
contraindications: Angina pectoris and other cardiovascular disorders, diabetes mellitus, hypertension.

name: CARBIMAZOLE
uses: Hyperthyroidism,控制 Grave’s disease and toxic nodular goitre, pre-operatively, thyroid storm.
side_effects: Hepatitis, SLE like syndrome, agranulocytosis (serious but reversible), hypothyroidism, skin rashes, loss of hair/taste.
dosage: 15-40 mg daily until euthyroid (4-8 weeks), then maintenance 5-15 mg for 12-18 months.
precautions: Pregnancy, breastfeeding.

name: IODINE
uses: Prevention and treatment of iodine deficiency.
side_effects: Hypothyroidism, goitre, hypersensitivity, mucous membrane inflammation.
dosage: Iodine deficiency (IM): infant 190 mg; child/adult 380 mg; (Oral): infant <1 year 100 mg; child (1-5 years) 200 mg yearly; adult/child (>6 years) 400 mg yearly; pregnancy 200 mg single dose.
precautions: Breast-feeding.

name: LUGOL’S IODINE
uses: Thyrotoxicosis (pre-operative).
side_effects: Angioedema, fever, arthralgia, metallic taste, salivary gland swelling.
dosage: 0.1-0.3 ml 3 times daily well diluted with water or milk.
precautions: Keep in closed container resistant to iodine.

name: PROPYLTHIOURACIL
uses: Hyperthyroidism (See under carbimazole).
side_effects: Thrombocytopenia, aplastic anaemia, hypoprothrombinaemia and bleeding.
dosage: 200-400 mg daily until euthyroid, then maintenance 50 to 150 mg daily.
precautions: N/A

name: OCTREOTIDE
uses: Acromegaly, carcinoid tumor, VIPoma, esophageal variceal bleeding.
side_effects: Gallstones, cholecystitis, cholestatic hepatitis, dysglycemia, bradycardia.
dosage: Acromegaly: 50 µg SC q8-12h, titrate up to 500 µg; maintenance: 20 mg IM every 4 weeks. Variceal bleeding: 50 µg IV bolus, then 25-50 µg/hr for 1-5 days.
precautions: Caution in renal/hepatic impairment. Pregnancy Category B.
contraindications: Inhibition of gallbladder contractility, gallstone formation.

name: SOMATROPIN
uses: Pituitary dwarfism, Turner’s syndrome, renal failure, adult GH deficiency, AIDS related wasting.
side_effects: Pain at injection site, lipodystrophy, glucose intolerance, hand stiffness, salt/water retention.
dosage: Pituitary dwarfism: 0.03-0.06 mg/kg daily in the evening. Adult GH deficiency: 150-300 µg/day SC adjusted accordingly.
precautions: May increase intracranial tension.

name: CALCITONIN
uses: Postmenopausal osteoporosis (greater than 5 years post menopause).
side_effects: Facial/peripheral edema, hypertension, syncope, chest pain, loss of taste/smell, rhinitis, epistaxis.
dosage: Nasal spray: 1 spray per day intranasally, alternating nostrils daily.
precautions: Known hypersensitivity, hypocalcaemia, nasal changes, malignancy.

name: SODIUM ALDRONATE
uses: Prevention and treatment of post-menopausal osteoporosis, osteoporosis in men, corticosteroid-induced osteoporosis.
side_effects: Oesophageal ulcers/stricture, dyspepsia, melaena, severe skin reactions (SJS).
dosage: Prevention: 5 mg daily; Treatment: 10 mg daily or 70 mg once weekly.
precautions: Caution in history of ulcers, GI bleeding, renal impairment.
contraindications: Pregnancy, breast-feeding, stricture or achalasia of oesophagus.
interactions: NSAID, prednisolone, calcium, iron, antacids, tea, coffee, fruit juice.

name: TERIPARATIDE
uses: Severe osteoporosis with fractures.
side_effects: Arthralgia, rhinitis, nausea, dizziness, leg cramps.
dosage: 20 µg SC daily into thigh or abdominal wall.
precautions: N/A

name: ORLISTAT
uses: Obesity management (BMI >30 kg/m2 or >27 kg/m2 with risk factors).
side_effects: Oily rectal leakage, steatorrhea, frequent bowel movements, infectious diarrhoea, cholelithiasis, acute renal failure, calcium oxalate nephrolithiasis.
dosage: 120 mg 3 times daily with each main meal containing fat (up to 1 hour after meal).
precautions: Fat soluble vitamin supplementation >=2hrs before/after orlistat.
contraindications: Pregnancy, chronic malabsorption, cholestasis, renal impairment.

name: MESTEROLONE
uses: Androgen deficiency, male infertility associated with hypogonadism.
side_effects: Prostate abnormalities, gynaecomastia, increased bone growth, male-pattern baldness, weight gain.
dosage: Orally, 25 mg 3-4 times daily for several months; maintenance 50-75 mg daily in divided doses.
precautions: Ischaemic heart disease, hypertension, elderly, diabetes, pre-pubertal boys.
contraindications: Breast cancer in men, prostate cancer, pregnancy, breastfeeding, hypercalcaemia, history of primary liver tumours.

name: METHYL-TESTOSTERONE
uses: Hypogonadism, breast cancer.
side_effects: Jaundice, frequent erection, changes in menstrual periods.
dosage: Hypogonadism: orally 10-50 mg per day. Breast cancer: 50 mg one to four times a day.
precautions: See under testosterone.
contraindications: Carcinoma of prostate, male breast, liver/kidney disease, pregnancy.

name: TESTOSTERONE
uses: Hypogonadism, breast cancer in females.
side_effects: Virilization, excessive body hair, menstrual irregularity, changes in libido, gynaecomastia, premature closure of epiphyses.
dosage: Hypogonadism: IM Propionate 50 mg 2-3 times weekly; Enanthate 250 mg every 2-3 weeks. Breast cancer: IM Propionate 100 mg 2-3 times weekly; Enanthate 250 mg every 2-3 weeks.
precautions: Renal/hepatic impairment, ischaemic heart disease, diabetes; extreme caution in children.
contraindications: Males with carcinoma of breast or prostate, pregnancy, breastfeeding.

name: NANDROLONE
uses: Aplastic anaemia, antineoplastic.
side_effects: Virilism, oedema, acne, amenorrhoea, inhibition of spermatogenesis, liver tumour.
dosage: Deep IM injection: 50 mg every 3 weeks.
precautions: Cardiac, hepatic, renal impairment. Possible premature closure of epiphysis.

name: OXYMETHOLONE
uses: Aplastic anaemia.
side_effects: See under nandrolone.
dosage: 1-5 mg/kg daily in divided doses; child 0.175 mg/kg daily as a single dose.
precautions: Protect from sunlight.

name: STANOZOLOL
uses: Hereditary angioedema.
side_effects: See under nandrolone.
dosage: Initially 2-4 mg daily orally.
precautions: N/A

name: BICALUTAMIDE
uses: Prostate cancer (advanced/high-risk).
side_effects: Pruritus, asthenia, alopecia, dry skin, hypersensitivity reaction (angioedema).
dosage: 50 mg daily.
precautions: Monitor serum PSA levels. Impaired glucose tolerance.

name: DANAZOL
uses: Endometriosis, palliative treatment of fibrocystic breast disease, menorrhagia, gynaecomastia.
side_effects: Hirsutism, decreased breast size, weight gain, oedema, cholestatic jaundice.
dosage: Endometriosis: initially 400 mg daily (up to 4 divided doses). Menorrhagia: 200 mg daily for 3 months. Gynaecomastia: 400 mg daily for 6 months.
precautions: Unsuitable for those desiring conception. Start during menstruation.
contraindications: Abnormal genital bleeding, pregnancy, renal/cardiac dysfunction.

name: FINASTERIDE
uses: Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), male-pattern baldness.
side_effects: Impotence, decreased libido, breast tenderness/enlargement, decrease volume of ejaculate.
dosage: BPH: 5 mg daily. Baldness: 1 mg daily.
precautions: Review BPH treatment after 6 months.

name: CONJUGATED ESTROGEN
uses: Menopausal symptoms.
side_effects: See under ethinyl estradiol.
precautions: Risk of endometrial cancer if used long-term without progesterone.
contraindications: See under ethinyl estradiol; also breast cancer and thromboembolism.

name: ESTRADIOL
uses: Menopausal symptoms.
side_effects: See under ethinyl estradiol.
dosage: 1-2 mg daily.
precautions: Assess BP before and periodically during therapy.

name: ETHINYL ESTRADIOL
uses: Female hypogonadism, post-menopausal HRT, primary ovarian failure, contraception, dysmenorrhea, prostate/breast cancer.
side_effects: Nausea, bloating, breast tenderness, ankle swelling, spotting, thromboembolic disorder.
dosage: Estrogen deficiency: 10-50 µg daily for 21 days, repeated after 7 days tablet free. Prostate cancer: 0.15 to 1.5 mg daily.
precautions: Obesity (BMI >= 30), family history of breast cancer, cardiovascular disease.
contraindications: Estrogen dependent neoplasm, undiagnosed vaginal bleeding, thromboembolic disorder, liver disease, pregnancy, heavy smokers.
interactions: Endometrial/breast cancer risk reduced when combined with progesterone.

name: CHORIONIC GONADOTROPHIN (HCG)
uses: Treatment of infertility in women.
side_effects: Headache, multiple pregnancy, gynaecomastia.
dosage: 5000-10000 units IM injection once 1 day following the last dose of menotropins.
precautions: Cardiac/renal impairment, epilepsy, asthma, migraine.

name: CLOMIPHENE
uses: Anovulatory infertility in females.
side_effects: Ovarian enlargement, hot flushes, blurred vision, abdominal discomfort, weight gain.
dosage: 50 mg daily for 5 days, starting within 5 days of onset of menstruation.
precautions: May cause visual disturbances.
contraindications: Ovarian cysts, liver disease, pregnancy, uterine fibroids, ectopic pregnancy.

name: DYDROGESTERONE
uses: Endometriosis, dysfunctional uterine bleeding, dysmenorrhoea, amenorrhoea, HRT.
side_effects: See under norethisterone.
dosage: Endometriosis: 10 mg 2-3 times daily (cycle days 5-25). DUB: 10 mg BID for 5-7 days to arrest; 10 mg BID (days 11-25) to prevent.
precautions: N/A

name: HYDROXYPROGESTERONE
uses: Secondary amenorrhoea, dysfunctional uterine bleeding, induction of menses.
side_effects: See under norethisterone.
dosage: Amenorrhoea/DUB: IM 375 mg. Induction: IM 125-250 mg on day 10 of cycle.
precautions: Administer IM only. Protect from light.

name: MEDROXYPROGESTERONE
uses: Contraceptive, secondary amenorrhoea, DUB, endometriosis.
side_effects: See under norethisterone.
dosage: Contraception: Deep IM 150 mg within first 5 days of cycle, repeated every 3 months. Endometriosis: 10 mg TID for 90 days.
precautions: Delay until 6 weeks after parturition if breast-feeding.

name: NORETHISTERONE
uses: DUB, contraception, endometriosis, PMS, postponement of menstruation.
side_effects: Virilising effects, liver disturbances, jaundice, weight gain, breast discomfort.
dosage: Endometriosis: 10-15 mg daily starting 5th day of cycle. Postponement: 5 mg TID starting 3 days before anticipated onset.
precautions: Protect from light.
contraindications: Pregnancy, breast/genital cancer, conditions aggravated by fluid retention, liver function impairment.

name: COMBINED ORAL CONTRACEPTIVE PILLS (OCPS)
uses: Temporary contraception.
side_effects: Spotting, nausea, breast tenderness, headache, increased risk of stroke/gallbladder disease/cervical cancer (>5yr use).
dosage: One tablet daily starting within 0-5 day of menstruation.
precautions: Smoker >35 (<15 cigs/day), controlled hypertension, migraine >35, gallbladder disease, mild cirrhosis.
contraindications: <6 weeks postpartum, smoker >35, hypertension (>160/100), history of thromboembolism, ischemic heart disease, breast cancer, diabetes with complications.

name: LEVONORGESTREL
uses: Emergency contraceptive.
side_effects: Nausea, low abdominal pain, dizziness, menstrual irregularities.
dosage: 1.5 g as a single dose as soon as possible after sex (preferably within 12 hours but not later than 72 hours).
precautions: Less effective than IUD insertion.

name: ERGOT ALKALOIDS (ERGOMETRINE, METHYL ERGOMETRINE)
uses: Postpartum haemorrhage, post abortion haemorrhage.
side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, rise in BP, gangrene of toes, bowel infarction (high dose).
dosage: IM or IV: 0.2 mg (Methyl ergometrine) or 0.25 mg (Ergometrine), can repeat every 15 min; max 5 doses.
precautions: Given only after foetal delivery; may decrease milk secretion.
contraindications: Induction of labour, cardiac disease, eclampsia, multiple pregnancy, Rh-negative mother.

name: MIFEPRISTONE
uses: Medical termination of intra-uterine pregnancy up to 63 days gestation.
side_effects: Vaginal bleeding, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, headache.
dosage: Oral: 200 mg single dose, followed 24-48 hours later by misoprostol 800 μg.
precautions: Caution in renal/hepatic impairment, age over 35.
contraindications: Suspected ectopic pregnancy, uncontrolled severe asthma.

name: OXYTOCIN
uses: Induction of labour, augmentation of labour, management of 3rd stage, postpartum haemorrhage.
side_effects: Uterine hyperstimulation, foetal asphyxia, uterine rupture, water intoxication.
dosage: Induction: 2.5 units in 500ml Dextrose/NS at 10 drops/min. Increase by 10 drops every 30 min (max 60 drops/min). Post-partum: IM 10 IU; IV infusion 20 units in 1L at 40 drops/min.
precautions: Uterine hypertonia. Avoid IV bolus injection. Use only if cervix has ripened.
contraindications: Cephalo-pelvic disproportion, malpresentation, placenta previa, obstructed labour, foetal distress.

name: MISOPROSTOL
uses: Termination of pregnancy, induction of labour, active management of 3rd stage, postpartum haemorrhage.
side_effects: Nausea, fall in blood pressure, tachycardia, uterine cramps, fever, rigor.
dosage: Induction: 25-50 μg every 4-6 hours (max 200 μg). 3rd stage: 600 μg oral (if no injectable access).
precautions: N/A
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, previous uterine scar, bronchial asthma, active cardiac/renal disease.

name: NIFEDIPINE
uses: Inhibit uncomplicated premature labour (24-33 weeks gestation).
side_effects: Tachycardia, flushing, headache, oedema, tremor.
dosage: Sublingual (IR): 10 mg every 15 min (max 40 mg in 1st hour), then oral (SR) 60-160 mg daily in 3-4 divided doses.
precautions: Sublingual route is not practiced now.
contraindications: Within 1 month of MI, cardiogenic shock, acute angina, breast feeding.

name: ISOXSUPRINE
uses: Premature labour.
side_effects: Flushing, hypotension, foetal tachycardia, maternal pulmonary oedema.
dosage: IV infusion: 200-300 μg/minute until control. Prophylaxis: oral 40-80 mg daily.
precautions: Monitor BP, pulse.
contraindications: Recent arterial haemorrhage, premature detachment of placenta, severe anaemia.

name: SALBUTAMOL
uses: Arrest uncomplicated premature labour (24-33 weeks gestation).
side_effects: See general salbutamol entry.
dosage: IV infusion: 10 μg/min, increase at 10-min intervals until contractions cease (max 45 μg/min). Maintain for 1 hour, then reduce by 50% every 6 hours; then oral 4 mg q6-8h.
precautions: N/A

name: TERBUTALINE
uses: Premature labour.
side_effects: Chest pain, arrhythmia, allergic reactions, headache, tremor.
dosage: IV infusion: 10 to 25 μg/min (max 80 μg/min). Then 2.5 to 7.5 mg orally every 6 hours until 36-37 weeks gestation.
precautions: Caution in lactation.
contraindications: Renal/liver diseases, diabetes, hyperthyroidism, hypertension, myocardial insufficiency.

name: ALUMINIUM PHOSPHIDE POISONING
uses: Severe pulmonary irritation, pulmonary edema, hepatic and myocardial injury, breathlessness, cyanosis.
side_effects: Phosphine gas is released from tablets in the presence of atmospheric moisture; can be fatal up to 36 hours after exposure.
dosage: N/A
precautions: Supportive management; Oxygen for pulmonary edema; Assisted ventilation in serious cases; Patients must be kept under observation.

name: ASPIRIN (SALICYLATE) POISONING
uses: Salicylism with tachypnoea, tinnitus, vomiting, metabolic acidosis, altered mental state, seizures.
side_effects: <150 mg/kg: Minimal symptoms; 150-300 mg/kg: Mild to moderate; 300-500 mg/kg: Severe intoxication; >500 mg/kg: Potentially lethal.
dosage: N/A
precautions: Resuscitation (ventilation, seizure control); Fluid and electrolyte balance; Decontamination: Activated charcoal in repeated doses (50 g 4 hourly) for overdose >150 mg/kg; Intravenous sodium bicarbonate (optimum urinary pH 7.5 to 8.5); Hemodialysis for severe cases.
contraindications: 12-lead ECG, Serum electrolytes, blood glucose level, Arterial blood gas analysis (metabolic acidosis).

name: ATROPINE AND BELLADONNA POISONING
uses: Antimuscarinic features: Dry and flushed skin, dry mucous membrane, dilated pupils, hyperthermia, tachycardia, decreased bowel sounds, ileus, urinary retention, drowsiness, stupor, convulsions, coma.
side_effects: Dose of 10 mg or more causes excitement, hallucinations, delirium, and coma; in children 10 mg or less may be fatal.
dosage: Adult dose 2 mg I.M. or I.V. or S.C., followed by 1 mg every 20 to 30 minutes until desired effect is obtained (up to 4 mg total). Effect lasts less than an hour, so dose should be repeated.
precautions: Resuscitation and symptomatic support; Antidote administration.

name: BARBITURATE POISONING
uses: CNS depression, toxic neurological symptoms, profound coma.
side_effects: Ingestion of >8 mg/kg produces toxic neurological symptoms; multiples of this dose produce profound coma. CNS depression correlates with serum levels: >80-100 mg/L suggests coma requiring intubation.
dosage: N/A
precautions: Resuscitation (intratracheal tube if in coma); Monitor blood gases and electrolytes; Gastric lavage; Multiple dose activated charcoal (MDAC); Hemodialysis for severe cases.
contraindications: Screening 12-lead ECG, blood glucose level, Serum barbiturate levels.

name: BENZODIAZEPINE POISONING
uses: Mild sedation; risk increases significantly if co-ingested with other CNS depressants (alcohol, opioids).
side_effects: Benzodiazepines have a large therapeutic index; isolated overdose usually only causes mild sedation.
dosage: Initial dose of 0.1-0.2 mg IV, repeat every minute until reversal of sedation, maximum 2 mg. Resedation occurs at ~90 minutes; repeat if required. (Contraindicated in seizure disorders, pro-convulsant co-ingestion, or QRS prolongation).
precautions: Supportive treatment; Resuscitation; Activated charcoal is usually not indicated; Specific antidote administration if not contraindicated.

name: CARBAMATE POISONING
uses: Symptoms closely resemble organophosphates (DUMBBELS: Diarrhoea, Urination, Miosis, Bronchorrhea, Bronchospasm, Emesis, Lacrimation, Salivation).
side_effects: Reversible acetylcholinesterase inhibitors used as insecticides (e.g., Baygon, aldicarb).
dosage: Refer to ORGANOPHOSPHORUS INSECTICIDE protocol (Note: Pralidoxime is not recommended for Carbamate).
precautions: Skin decontamination (wash with warm water and soap); Gastric lavage if within the past hour.

name: CARBON MONOXIDE POISONING
uses: Neurological complications; risk of long-term neuropsychological sequelae.
side_effects: High concentration CO for short duration: low risk; Lower concentration CO for longer duration: high risk of sequelae.
dosage: N/A
precautions: Immediate treatment; Remove from exposure; Administer high-flow 100% oxygen; Correct acidosis and maintain BP; Cerebral edema in severe cases may require IV mannitol.
contraindications: Screening 12-lead ECG, blood glucose, Carboxyhemoglobin levels, Arterial blood gas, serum lactate, Cranial CT or MRI.

name: CHLORINATED HYDROCARBON INSECTICIDES POISONING
uses: CNS depression, cardiac dysrhythmias, hepatic or renal damage, chemical pneumonitis (if aspirated).
side_effects: Includes DDT, BHC, chlordane, aldrin, dieldrin.
dosage: N/A
precautions: Decontamination (remove clothing, wash skin); GI decontamination contraindicated; Activated charcoal has no role; Avoid milk and oils (facilitate absorption); Diazepam IV for convulsions.

name: CORROSIVES (ACIDS AND ALKALIS)
uses: Visible burns in mouth/throat, respiratory distress.
side_effects: Includes Hydrochloric, Sulfuric, Nitric acid and Ammonia, Caustic soda.
dosage: N/A
precautions: Prehospital: dilution with water or milk; Emesis and gastric lavage are contraindicated; Maintain airway; Analgesics (pethidine); Corticosteroids and prophylactic antibiotics suggested; Oesophagoscopy within 24h; Endoscopically guided dilation if strictures develop.

name: ETHYLENE GLYCOL POISONING
uses: Initial (1-2 hrs): Euphoria, nystagmus, vomiting; Subsequent (4-12 hrs): Dyspnea, tachycardia, hypertension, progressing to coma and death. Flank pain/oliguria suggests renal failure.
side_effects: Ingestion of >1ml/kg is potentially lethal.
dosage: Ethanol (Oral/NG): Load 1.8 ml/kg of 43% ethanol, Maintain 0.2-0.4 mL/kg/hour. Ethanol (IV): Load 8 mL/kg of 10% ethanol, Maintain 1-2 mL/kg/hour. Fomepizole: Load 15 mg/kg IV over 30 mins, then 10 mg/kg every 12 hrs for 48 hrs.
precautions: Resuscitation; Correct metabolic acidosis with IV bicarbonate (Bolus 1-2 mmol/kg); IV benzodiazepines for seizures; Hemodialysis is definitive; Administer Thiamine and Pyridoxine.
contraindications: Serum electrolytes, urea, creatinine, lactate, osmolality, ABG (Anion gap acidosis).

name: INSECT STINGS (ANTS, BEES, WASPS)
uses: Local pain and swelling; seldom cause severe systemic toxicity unless anaphylactic.
side_effects: N/A
dosage: Adrenaline (for anaphylaxis)
precautions: Clean area with antiseptics; Remove stings immediately; Topical corticosteroids or oral antihistaminics; Anaphylactic reactions require adrenaline.

name: KEROSENE POISONING
uses: Pulmonary edema, aspiration pneumonia.
side_effects: Aspiration risk is the primary concern.
dosage: N/A
precautions: Gastric lavage is contraindicated; Treatment is supportive; Furosemide (25-100 mg IV) for pulmonary edema; Ventilatory support; Antibiotics for aspiration pneumonia.

name: METHANOL POISONING
uses: Initially (1hr): Nausea, vomiting, CNS depression. Latent (12-24 hrs): headache, dizziness, blurred vision, photophobia. Severe: tachypnoea, progressive blindness, papilloedema, coma. Extrapyramidal movement disorders in survivors.
side_effects: Ingestion of >0.5 ml/kg is potentially lethal; >0.25 ml/kg is toxic.
dosage: Same as for Ethylene Glycol poisoning.
precautions: Similar to Ethylene Glycol management; Bicarbonate in 50 mmol aliquots if pH <7.30; Dialysis recommended if >30 ml pure methanol ingested.

name: MORPHINE AND OTHER OPIOIDS POISONING
uses: Classical triad: CNS depression, respiratory depression, and miosis (pinpoint pupils).
side_effects: Toxicity occurs just above analgesic dose. High risk in opioid-naive patients or co-ingestion with CNS depressants. Dextropropoxyphene >20mg/kg causes cardiac dysrhythmias. Tramadol >500mg causes seizures.
dosage: Initial bolus 100 mcg IV (or 400 mcg IM/SC). Repeated doses of 100 mcg IV every 30-60 seconds until respiration re-established. Infusion rate at 2/3rd of the initial dose required per hour.
precautions: Resuscitation; Monitor respiratory rate, GCS, and oxygen saturation; IV bolus sodium bicarbonate for dysrhythmias in dextropropoxyphene intoxication.

name: MUSHROOM POISONING
uses: Early GI (<2 hrs): Abdominal pain, vomiting, diarrhea. Delayed GI (5-12 hrs): intractable vomiting, watery diarrhea, hypoglycemia, hepatotoxicity. Neurological: Hallucinations, loss of co-ordination, seizures.
side_effects: Delayed symptoms (5-12 hours) are associated with higher risk of fulminant hepatic failure and death.
dosage: N/A
precautions: Adequate fluid and electrolyte replacement; Antiemetics (promethazine); GL or AC if presents early; Continuous glucose monitoring; Monitor liver function; IV benzodiazepines for seizures.
contraindications: Liver function tests, Blood glucose levels.

name: ORGANOPHOSPHORUS INSECTICIDE POISONING
uses: Muscarinic (DUMBBELS): Diarrhoea, Urination, Miosis, Bronchorrhea, Bronchospasm, Emesis, Lacrimation, Salivation; Bradycardia. Nicotinic: Fasciculation, tremor, respiratory muscle paralysis. CNS: Agitation, coma, seizures.
side_effects: Manifestations may be delayed up to 12 hours. Risk of Intermediate Syndrome (delayed paralysis 2-4 days) or OPIDN (1-5 weeks post-exposure).
dosage: Atropine: 1.8 mg IV, double dose every 5 minutes until atropnization (dry armpit, dilated pupil, clear chest). Maintenance: 10-20% of required dose per hour. Pralidoxime: Initial 2 g in 100 ml NS IV over 20 mins; followed by infusion 0.5 g/hour (6 g in 500 ml NS) for at least 24 hours.
precautions: Resuscitation and support; Skin decontamination; Activated charcoal usually not beneficial.
contraindications: Red cell and plasma cholinesterase levels.

name: PARACETAMOL POISONING
uses: Initially asymptomatic or mild GI distress; latent period followed by hepatic necrosis.
side_effects: Single dose 7.5 g (adult) or 150 mg/kg (child) can cause severe necrosis. Predict risk via Rumack-Matthew nomogram (Serum level >200 mg/L at 4h or >25 mg/L at 16h).
dosage: IV 150 mg/kg in 200 ml D5 over 15 mins; then 50 mg/kg in 500 ml D5 over 4 hours; then 100 mg/kg in 1 liter D5 over 16 hours.
precautions: Resuscitation; Activated charcoal within 1st hour of overdose.
contraindications: Serum paracetamol (not before 4h), Hepatic transaminases (>1000 IU/L), Coagulation studies, Renal function, Urinalysis.

name: TRICYCLIC ANTIDEPRESSANT POISONING
uses: CNS: Sedation, delirium, seizures. CVS: Sinus tachycardia, hypotension, broad complex tachyarrhythmias/bradycardia. Anticholinergic: Agitation, mydriasis, urinary retention, dry/flushed skin.
side_effects: Ingestion >10 mg/kg life-threatening; symptoms appear within 2h. Toxicity: <5 mg/kg minimal; 10-30 mg/kg major effects; >30 mg/kg severe/lethal.
dosage: 100 mEq (2 mEq/kg) IV, repeated every 1-2 minutes until restoration of normal rhythm.
precautions: Continuous cardiac monitoring for 6h; Ventilator support for CNS depression; AC if >10 mg/kg; Sodium bicarbonate 100 mEq (2 mEq/kg) IV repeated q1-2 min for dysrhythmias (target pH 7.50-7.55); Lignocaine (1.5 mg/kg) second-line; IV benzodiazepines for seizures. Avoid type 1a antiarrhythmics, amiodarone, beta-blockers.
contraindications: Serial ECGs (Monitoring for PR/QRS prolongation, QRS >100ms predicts seizures, >160ms predicts VT).

name: ZINC PHOSPHIDE POISONING
uses: Typical garlic odor, severe gastro-intestinal irritations, coughing, hepatic necrosis.
side_effects: Common rodenticide; reacts with stomach acid to produce phosphine gas.
dosage: N/A
precautions: Supportive management; Decontamination may help; Patients must be kept under observation.

name: ACTINOMYCIN D (DACTINOMYCIN)
uses: Cytotoxic drug: Wilm’s tumor, trophoblastic neoplasms, testicular cancer.
side_effects: Pancytopenia, thrombocytopenia, myelosuppression, stomatitis, hypocalcaemia, hepatotoxicity, anaphylaxis, hyperpigmentation of radiated areas.
dosage: Wilm’s tumor/Ewing sarcoma: 15 mcg/kg I.V. once a day for five days.
precautions: VESICANT: Administer slowly by IV push to avoid extravasation. Caution in hepatic/renal impairment. Toxic effects may take 1-2 weeks to reach maximum severity; discontinue if severe diarrhoea, myelosuppression, or stomatitis occur. Avoid use within 2 weeks of radiation. Avoid live virus vaccines.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, active chickenpox or herpes zoster.
interactions: Increased risk of hepatotoxicity when used within 2 weeks of radiation treatment for right-sided tumors.

name: ARSENIC TRIOXIDE
uses: Cytotoxic drug: Refractory or relapsed acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL).
side_effects: Prolonged QTc interval, APL differentiation syndrome, tachycardia, hyperglycemia, hypomagnesemia, hypokalemia, weight gain, hypoxia.
dosage: Induction cycle: 0.15 mg/kg IV qDay until bone marrow remission (max 60 days) in combination with Oral Tretinoin 22.5 mg/m² twice daily. Consolidation cycle: 0.15 mg/kg IV daily on Days 1-5 of Weeks 1-4 of an 8-week cycle for 4 cycles.
precautions: Prolongs QTc interval; risk of APL differentiation syndrome and hyperleukocytosis. Monitor ECG, RFT, electrolytes, and weight regularly. Human carcinogen; monitor for second primary malignancies.
interactions: Maintain potassium > 4 mEq/L and magnesium > 1.8 mg/dL to avoid cardiac conduction abnormalities.

name: AZATHIOPRINE
uses: Cytotoxic drug: Refractory rheumatoid arthritis, renal transplants to prevent graft rejection.
side_effects: Dose-related myelosuppression, liver impairment, cholestatic jaundice, interstitial nephritis, hair loss, nausea, pancreatitis.
dosage: Rheumatoid arthritis: 1 mg/kg/day IV/PO initially; after 6-8 weeks, increase by 0.5 mg/kg/day every 4 weeks (max 2.5 mg/kg/day). Maintenance: Reduce daily dose by 0.5 mg/kg every 4 weeks until lowest effective dose reached.
precautions: Monitor CBC frequently; discontinue if leukocytes <3000/mm³ or platelets <100,000/mm³. Discontinue if signs of hepatotoxicity (dark urine, jaundice) occur. Avoid live vaccines.
interactions: Increased leukopenia with ACE inhibitors and sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim. Increased myelosuppression with cyclosporine and mercaptopurine.

name: CALCIUM FOLINATE (CALCIUM LEUCOVORIN)
uses: Cytotoxic support: Prevention of methotrexate-induced adverse effects, suspected methotrexate overdosage.
side_effects: Agitation, depression, pyrexia (after parenteral use).
dosage: Prevention: 15 mg IM/IV every 6 hours for 24 hours, usually starting 12–24 hours after start of methotrexate infusion. Overdosage: Initial dose equal to or exceeding dose of methotrexate at max rate of 160 mg/minute.
precautions: Use caution in pernicious anaemia or other B12 deficiency megaloblastic anemias.
interactions: Avoid concurrent use with methotrexate unless following specific rescue protocols.

name: CAPECITABINE
uses: Cytotoxic drug: Colorectal cancer, breast cancer.
side_effects: Diarrhea, hand-foot skin reaction, liver dysfunction, vomiting.
dosage: 1250 mg/m² twice daily for 2 weeks followed by a 1-week rest period (q21 days).
precautions: Stop drug in case of grade 2-4 hyperbilirubinemia. Monitor for hand-foot syndrome.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to capecitabine or 5-FU, DPD deficiency, severe renal impairment.
interactions: Increases bleeding risk with anticoagulants, NSAIDS, salicylates, and thrombolytics. Aluminium/Magnesium laxatives may affect absorption.

name: CARBOPLATIN
uses: Cytotoxic drug: Advanced ovarian cancer, germ cell tumours, small and non-small cell lung cancers, bladder cancer, endometrial cancer.
side_effects: Significant and dose-limiting myelosuppression (thrombocytopenia), renal toxicity, peripheral neuropathy, mild elevation of liver enzymes.
dosage: Single agent: 360 mg/m² IV every 4 weeks. Combination: 300 mg/m² IV (with cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m² IV) every 4 weeks.
precautions: Must be administered in a specialized care setting. Renal and hepatic studies required monthly. When using with paclitaxel, carboplatin should be given AFTER paclitaxel. Risk of hypersensitivity increases with number of cycles.
interactions: Increases nephrotoxicity or ototoxicity with aminoglycosides and amphotericin B. Bleeding risk with aspirin, NSAIDS, and anticoagulants.

name: CHLORAMBUCIL
uses: Cytotoxic drug: Waldenstrom macroglobulinaemia, chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL), non-Hodgkin lymphomas, Hodgkin disease.
side_effects: Bone marrow suppression, rashes, Steven-Johnson syndrome, hyperuricemia, GI upset.
dosage: CLL: 0.1 mg/kg/day for 3-6 weeks OR 0.4 mg/kg biweekly or monthly OR 0.03-0.1 mg/kg/day continuously.
precautions: Reduce initial dose if given within 4 weeks of radiation or if bone marrow is diseased. Not to exceed 0.1 mg/kg/day if bone marrow is infiltrated with lymphocytes.
contraindications: Pregnancy, gout, radiation or cytotoxic therapy within 1 month, severe renal/hepatic impairment.
interactions: Interaction with nalidixic acid. Avoid concomitant use with allopurinol or colchicines.

name: CISPLATIN
uses: Cytotoxic drug: Metastatic testicular tumor, ovarian carcinoma, advanced bladder cancer, cancer of cervix, endometrium, prostate, and oesophagus.
side_effects: Nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity, myelosuppression, nausea, vomiting, alopecia.
dosage: Usual dose: 20 mg/m²/day IV for 5 days per cycle.
precautions: Avoid aluminium needles or equipment (reacts with cisplatin). Maintain vigorous hydration (1-2 L fluid 8-12 hr before dose). Monitor for neuromuscular disease.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to platinum compounds, severe myelosuppression, renal impairment, hearing impairment, pregnancy, lactation.
interactions: Increased risk of nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity with aminoglycosides and loop diuretics.

name: CYCLOPHOSPHAMIDE
uses: Cytotoxic drug: Chronic lymphatic leukaemia, non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma, ovarian carcinoma, breast carcinoma, Hodgkin’s diseases, neuroblastoma, sarcomas.
side_effects: Myelosuppression, hemorrhagic cystitis, myocardial fibrosis, alopecia, sterility, SIADH.
dosage: Daily IV injection: 3-6 mg/kg twice weekly. Massive intermittent therapy: 20-40 mg/kg over 2-5 days with 10-20 day intervals OR 10-15 mg/kg with 7-10 day intervals. Oral dose: 1-5 mg/kg/day.
precautions: Fetal harm. Monitor temperature every 4 hr (infection sign). Chest x-ray every 2 weeks. Monitor CBC weekly. Ensure high fluid intake (2-3 L/day) to prevent hemorrhagic cystitis.
interactions: Decreases digoxin levels. Increases anticoagulant effects. Toxic effects increased by rifampicin, phenobarbitone, and allopurinol.

name: CYTARABINE
uses: Cytotoxic drug: Acute myelocytic leukemia (AML), acute non-lymphocytic leukemia, chronic myelocytic leukemia, lymphomatous meningitis.
side_effects: Myelosuppression (leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, anaemia), nausea, vomiting, alopecia.
dosage: AML: Continuous IV infusion 100 mg/m²/day for 7 days every 2 weeks. Meningeal leukemia: Intrathecal 5-70 mg/m² daily for 4 days every 2-7 days.
precautions: Monitor for tumor lysis syndrome. Administer allopurinol and alkalinise urine to maintain uric acid levels. Give antiemetic 30-60 min before treatment.
interactions: Do not use with live virus vaccines. Increased toxicity with methotrexate and radiation.

name: DAUNORUBICIN
uses: Cytotoxic drug: Combined treatment of acute leukemia.
side_effects: Cardiotoxicity, myelosuppression, red urine (harmless), alopecia, phlebitis, irreversible gonadal suppression.
dosage: Acute non-lymphocytic leukemia: (In combo with cytarabine) 30-45 mg/m² IVP on Days 1, 2, 3. Acute lymphocytic leukemia: 45 mg/m² IVP on Days 1, 2, 3.
precautions: VESICANT: Irritant to tissues; apply pressure to venipuncture sites for 10 minutes. Monitor for cardiotoxicity (CHF may occur 1-6 months after therapy). Periodic ECG and ejection fraction monitoring required.
interactions: Increased myelosuppression with other antineoplastics or radiation. Increased adverse effects with live vaccines.

name: DOCETAXEL
uses: Cytotoxic drug: Breast cancer, non-small cell lung cancer, metastatic prostate cancer, gastric cancer, bladder cancer.
side_effects: Myelosuppression, hepatotoxicity, seizures, sinus tachycardia, pulmonary fibrosis, SJS, hypersensitivity reactions (common in first two cycles).
dosage: Adult: IV 60-100 mg/m² given over 1 hr every 3 weeks. Reduce dose by 25% if neutrophil count <500/mm³ for >1 week.
precautions: Should receive steroid premedication. Monitor LFT, CBC, and daily I/O chart for peripheral edema (fluid retention syndrome).

name: DOXORUBICIN
uses: Cytotoxic drug: Acute leukemia, carcinoma of breast, bladder, stomach, ovary, thyroid, neuroblastoma, Hodgkin’s/non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma, soft tissue sarcoma.
side_effects: Cardiomyopathy, acute left ventricular failure, myelosuppression, alopecia, facial flushes, red discoloration of urine.
dosage: 60-75 mg/m² of body surface area.
precautions: VESICANT: Care must be taken during extravasation. Avoid sun exposure. Rapid injection causes facial flushing. Monitor CBC weekly. Monitor ECG for ST-T wave changes.
interactions: Precipitates with dexamethasone, 5-FU, and heparin. Increased cardiomyopathy with calcium channel blockers.

name: EPIRUBICIN
uses: Cytotoxic drug: Adjuvant therapy for breast cancer; bladder, gastric, lung, ovarian cancer.
side_effects: Bone marrow depression, heart failure, tumor lysis syndrome, amenorrhea, alopecia, red-orange urine.
dosage: Adjuvant breast cancer: Day 1: Epirubicin 100 mg/m² IV + 5-FU 500 mg/m² IV + cyclophosphamide 500 mg/m² IV. Repeat q21 days for 6 cycles.
precautions: VESICANT: Severe tissue necrosis if given IM/SC. Rapid injection (<3 min) causes facial flushing. Monitor CBC weekly (Nadir at 10-14 days). Monitor cardiac function at baseline.
contraindications: Pregnancy, breastfeeding, heart failure, recent MI, cardiomyopathy.
interactions: Increased toxicity with radiation/cimetidine. Risk of heart failure with Trastuzumab and calcium channel blockers.

name: ETOPOSIDE
uses: Cytotoxic drug: Germ cell tumors, small cell carcinoma of lungs, Non Hodgkin lymphoma, acute non-lymphocytic leukemia, Kaposi sarcoma.
side_effects: Myelosuppression, stomatitis, alopecia, anaphylaxis, secondary malignancies.
dosage: Testicular neoplasms: IV 50-100 mg/m² daily for 5 days OR 100 mg/m² on days 1, 3, 5; repeat q3-4 weeks. SCLC: Oral 70-100 mg/m² daily for 4-5 days; IV 35-50 mg/m² daily for 4-5 days.
precautions: Administer over 30-60 minutes to reduce hypotension risk. Caution in liver disease and renal/hepatic impairment.
interactions: Bone marrow depression increased by other antineoplastics and radiation. May alter immune response to live vaccines.

name: FLUDARABINE
uses: Cytotoxic drug: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia, non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
side_effects: CNS toxicity, myelosuppression, visual disturbance, gastrointestinal hemorrhage, edema.
dosage: Adult: IV 25 mg/m² over 30 min for 5 days.
precautions: Monitor CNS toxicity.
contraindications: Pregnancy, breastfeeding, hypersensitivity, decreased kidney functions.

name: FLUOROURACIL
uses: Cytotoxic drug: Colorectal cancer, GI neoplasms, breast, pancreatic, head and neck cancer.
side_effects: Hand-foot syndrome (erythema, desquamation, pain), mucosal ulcers, myelosuppression, alopecia, myelopathy.
dosage: Oral maintenance: 15 mg/kg weekly; maximum in one day 1 g.
precautions: Caution in infections and patients with oedema or ascites.
contraindications: Bone marrow suppression, active ischemic heart disease, pregnancy, lactation.
interactions: Additive myelosuppression with other depressants. Increased risk of toxicity with combination therapy (e.g., irinotecan).

name: HYDROXYUREA
uses: Cytotoxic drug: Melanoma, chronic myelogenous leukaemia, recurrent/metastatic ovarian cancer, head and neck cancer, sickle cell anaemia.
side_effects: Seizures, hepatotoxicity, increased BUN, uric acid, megaloblastic erythropoiesis, tumor lysis syndrome.
dosage: Ovarian cancer/Melanoma: Adult PO 80 mg/kg as single dose q3Days or 20-30 mg/kg daily. CML/AML: Adult PO 10-75 mg/kg/day adjusted to WBC count. Child: 10-20 mg/kg/day.
precautions: Monitor CBC weekly. Severe myelosuppression risk. Reduce dose in polycythemia vera. Monitor renal function.
interactions: Increased risk of pancreatitis/hepatotoxicity with didanosine or stavudine. Probenecid/sulfinpyrazone increase uric acid levels.

name: IRINOTECAN
uses: Cytotoxic drug: Metastatic colorectal carcinoma, epithelial lung cancers.
side_effects: Severe diarrhea, myelosuppression, colonic ulcerations, pancytopenia.
dosage: Adult IV: 125 mg/m² once weekly for 4 weeks followed by 2 weeks rest; OR 350 mg/m² every 3 weeks.
precautions: Risk of life-threatening diarrhea accompanied by dehydration. Use caution in patients >65 years or those with previous pelvic irradiation.
interactions: CYP3A4 inhibitors increase toxicity. Combination with 5-FU may cause serious sepsis/dehydration.

name: INTERFERON BETA
uses: Cytotoxic (Immunomodulator): Relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis.
side_effects: Flu-like symptoms, depression, suicide attempts, thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA), thyroid dysfunction, necrosis at injection site.
dosage: Subcutaneous: Initially 0.0625 mg every other day, gradually increasing over 6 weeks to 0.25 mg every other day.
precautions: Use caution in history of cardiac disorders or suicidal ideation. Monitor for hepatic injury, TMA, and new onset hypertension. Effective contraception required.
contraindications: Decompensated liver disease, severe depressive illness.

name: INTERFERON GAMMA-1B
uses: Cytotoxic (Immunomodulator): Reduce frequency of infection in chronic granulomatous disease, severe malignant osteoporosis.
side_effects: Myalgia, arthralgia, flu-like symptoms, systemic lupus erythematosus, proteinuria.
dosage: Subcutaneous: 50 mcg/m² 3 times a week.
precautions: Caution in cardiac disease, seizure disorders, or arrhythmias. Monitor CBC, renal, and liver function every 3 months. Use effective contraception.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to interferon gamma or E. coli-derived products.
interactions: Avoid simultaneous administration of foreign proteins (exaggerated immune response).

name: LOMUSTINE
uses: Cytotoxic drug: Brain tumors, lymphomas.
side_effects: Permanent bone marrow damage, vomiting.
dosage: Used alone: 120-130 mg/m² every 6-8 weeks.
precautions: Severe myelosuppression and hepatotoxicity. Avoid pregnancy.

name: MELPHALAN
uses: Cytotoxic drug: Multiple myeloma, advanced ovarian adenocarcinoma, advanced breast cancer.
side_effects: Marrow toxicity, hepatitis, pulmonary fibrosis, secondary malignancies.
dosage: Breast cancer: Oral 150 mcg/kg daily for 5-6 days, repeated every 6 weeks.
precautions: Monitor CBC for marrow toxicity.
interactions: Should be taken on an empty stomach.

name: MERCAPTOPURINE (6-MERCAPTOPURINE)
uses: Cytotoxic drug: Severe acute Crohn’s disease, maintenance of remission of Crohn’s/UC, acute leukaemias, CML.
side_effects: Pancreatitis, transient oligospermia, intestinal ulceration, bone-marrow suppression, hyperuricaemia.
dosage: Crohn’s/UC: Oral 1-1.5 mg/kg daily. Acute leukemia: Initially 2.5 mg/kg daily or 50-75 mg/m² daily.
precautions: Consider measuring TPMT activity before starting. Monitor liver function and CBC. Pregnancy Category X.

name: METHOTREXATE
uses: Cytotoxic drug: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia, gestational trophoblastic neoplasm, lymphomas, breast/lung cancer, RA, Crohn’s disease.
side_effects: Bone marrow suppression, mucositis, renal toxicity, dermatitis, interstitial pneumonitis, defective spermatogenesis, abortion.
dosage: Leukemia in children (maintenance): 15 mg/m² ONCE WEEKLY.
precautions: Monitor CBC, RFT, LFT. Consider titration in pleural effusion/ascites to prevent nephrotoxicity. Monitor for pneumonitis.
interactions: Toxicity increased by Sulfonamides, Salicylates, Tetracyclines, Chloramphenicol, Phenytoin, NSAIDs, Cisplatin, and PPIs.

name: MITOMYCIN
uses: Cytotoxic drug: Upper gastro-intestinal and breast cancers, superficial bladder cancer.
side_effects: Thrombocytopenia, leucopenia, mouth ulcers, thrombophlebitis, lung fibrosis.
dosage: IV infusion usually q6-weekly.
precautions: VESICANT: Causes delayed bone marrow toxicity; use with care at injection site.

name: MITOXANTRONE
uses: Cytotoxic drug: Acute myelogenous leukemia (adult), relapsed leukemia, advanced prostate cancer, multiple sclerosis.
side_effects: Myelosuppression, cardiotoxicity, alopecia, secondary AML.
dosage: MS: 12 mg/m² short IV infusion q3Months. AML: 12 mg/m²/day IV on Days 1-3. Prostate: 12-14 mg/m² q21Days in combination with corticosteroids.
precautions: Do not exceed lifetime cumulative dose of 140 mg/m².

name: OXALIPLATIN
uses: Cytotoxic drug: Colorectal carcinoma, gastro-oesophageal, lung, pancreatic cancers.
side_effects: Acute and chronic neurotoxicity, myelosuppression, hepatotoxicity.
dosage: Colon carcinoma: Day 1: 85 mg/m² IV + leucovorin 200 mg/m² IV; then 5-FU. Repeat q2weeks.
precautions: Administer under specialist supervision. Avoid cold exposure following administration (triggers neurotoxicity). Monitor for Grade 2/3 neuropathy.
interactions: Increased nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity with Bacitracin.

name: PACLITAXEL
uses: Cytotoxic drug: Ovarian, breast, NSCLC, SCLC, prostate, bladder cancer, AIDS related Kaposi sarcoma.
side_effects: Myelosuppression, neurotoxicity, myalgia, alopecia, mucositis.
dosage: Ovarian Ca: 175 mg/m² over 3 hours every 3 weeks.
precautions: Give premedication to prevent hypersensitivity. Monitor LFTs.
contraindications: Anaphylaxis, solid tumors with baseline neutrophil <1500/mm³.
interactions: Inhibitors of CYP3A4 affect metabolism. Quinidine and Amiodarone increase toxicity.

name: PEMETREXED
uses: Cytotoxic drug: Malignant pleural mesotheliomas, non-squamous NSCLC.
side_effects: Interstitial pneumonitis, severe myelosupression, fatigue, chest pain.
dosage: Mesothelioma: 500 mg/m² IV on Day 1 of each 21 day cycle with cisplatin. NSCLC: 500 mg/m² IV Day 1.
precautions: Premedication regimen mandatory: Folic acid, B12, and dexamethasone. Monitor CBC, RFT, LFT.
interactions: Renal toxicity increased with NSAIDs (Aspirin, Diclofenac). Increased nephron/oto toxicity with Bacitracin.

name: PROCARBAZINE
uses: Cytotoxic drug: Hodgkin’s disease, non-Hodgkin’s lymphomas, brain tumors.
side_effects: Myelosuppression, CNS toxicity, neuropathies, mental depression, ascites.
dosage: Initially 50 mg daily, increased to 250-300 mg daily in divided doses; cumulative total max 6 g.
precautions: Avoid alcohol. Monitor for CNS toxicity.
interactions: Disulfiram-like reaction with alcohol. Hypertensive crisis with tyramine foods. Potentiates hypoglycemic effects of insulin.

name: TACROLIMUS
uses: Cytotoxic (Immunosuppressant): Prophylaxis of graft rejection following kidney transplantation.
side_effects: Renal tubular necrosis, hyperglycemia, hypertension, tremor, visual disturbances, bile-duct abnormalities.
dosage: Initially 200–300 mcg/kg daily in 2 divided doses.
precautions: Use only with transplant specialist prescription. Increased risk of infection and lymphoma. Monitor serum drug concentration closely.
interactions: Avoid with amphotericin B, cidofovir. Caution with nephrotoxic drugs and calcium channel blockers. Dose adjustment required with CYP3A inducers/inhibitors.

name: TEMOZOLOMIDE
uses: Cytotoxic drug: Anaplastic astrocytoma with relapse, glioblastoma multiforme, malignant glioma, metastatic melanoma.
side_effects: Thrombocytopenia, leucopenia, seizures, anaphylaxis, secondary malignancy.
dosage: Initial: 150 mg/m² PO/IV qDay for 5 days of 28-day cycle. Maintenance: 200 mg/m² qDay if counts stable. Infuse IV over 90 minutes.
precautions: Assess CBC on day 22. PCP prophylaxis required when used with radiotherapy. Avoid sun exposure.
interactions: Avoid use within 24 hr of G-CSF or filgrastim. NSAIDS and anticoagulants increase bleeding risk.

name: TOPOTECAN
uses: Cytotoxic drug: Ovarian, small cell lung, and cervical cancer.
side_effects: Myelosuppression, hair loss, elevated liver transaminase, mouth sores.
dosage: Cervical: 0.75 mg/m² IV Days 1-3 q21days with cisplatin. Ovarian: 1.5 mg/m² IV qDay x 5 days q21days.
precautions: Avoid live vaccines. Reduce dose to 0.75 mg/m² in moderate renal dysfunction.
contraindications: Pregnancy, breastfeeding, severe bone marrow suppression.
interactions: Avoid use with P-glycoprotein inhibitors (amiodarone, clarithromycin).

name: TRETINOIN
uses: Cytotoxic (Retinoid): Acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL).
side_effects: Retinoic acid syndrome, cardiac arrhythmia, hemorrhage, dyspepsia.
dosage: 45 mg/m²/day PO divided q12h until 30 days after complete remission.
precautions: Monitor hepatic function and coagulation. Assess for retinoic acid syndrome.
contraindications: Pregnancy, hypersensitivity to retinoids or parabens.

name: VINCRISTINE
uses: Cytotoxic drug: Acute leukemia, combination therapy for various cancers.
side_effects: Peripheral neuropathy, loss of deep tendon reflexes, acute uric acid nephropathy, gait change, jaw pain, paralytic ileus.
dosage: IV Adult: 1.4 mg every week. Child: 2 mg/m² every week. (<10 kg: 0.05 mg/kg/week).
precautions: VESICANT: Caution during administration. FATAL IF GIVEN INTRATHECAL. Monitor for neuromuscular disease.
interactions: Use caution with neurotoxic or ototoxic agents.

name: VINBLASTINE
uses: Cytotoxic drug: Hodgkin’s lymphoma, testicular cancer, Kaposi’s sarcoma, bladder cancer.
side_effects: Myelosuppression, alopecia, bronchospasm, aspermia, cranial neuropathy (jaw pain).
dosage: Adult IV: Initially 3.7 mg/m² then increase weekly until WBC equals 3000/mm³ (max dose 18.5 mg/m²).
precautions: VESICANT: Avoid intrathecal administration. Caution in pulmonary disease and liver impairment.

name: VINORELBINE
uses: Cytotoxic drug: Non-small cell lung carcinoma, Hodgkin’s disease, breast/ovarian cancer.
side_effects: Myelosuppression, paresthesias, GI perforation, acute bronchospasm, ARDS.
dosage: Monotherapy: 30 mg/m² IV over 6-10 minutes weekly.
precautions: VESICANT: Irritant to veins. Assess BP during administration. Monitor AST, ALT, LDH.

name: BEVACIZUMAB
uses: Targeted drug: Metastatic colorectal cancer, non-small cell lung cancer, renal cell carcinoma, cervical cancer.
side_effects: Fatal hemorrhage, hemoptysis, CNS hemorrhage, proteinuria, thromboembolic events.
dosage: 5-10 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks.
precautions: Serious bleeding risk, GI perforation, wound dehiscence. Discontinue permanently if GI perforation occurs or for wound dehiscence requiring medical intervention.

name: BORTEZOMIB
uses: Targeted drug: Mantle cell lymphoma, multiple myeloma.
side_effects: Neuropathy, thrombocytopenia, pyrexia, anemia, dehydration.
dosage: 1.3 mg/m²/dose IV twice weekly for 2 weeks (Days 1, 4, 8, 11) followed by a 10-day rest period.
precautions: DO NOT ADMINISTER INTRATHECAL (fatal events reported). Use subcutaneous route to reduce neuropathy risk. Monitor for high tumor burden.
interactions: Green tea and supplements block efficacy and should be avoided.

name: CETUXIMAB
uses: Targeted drug: RAS-wild metastatic colorectal carcinoma, head and neck cancer.
side_effects: Infusion reactions, rashes, hypomagnesemia, interstitial lung disease.
dosage: Initial: 400 mg/m² IV. Subsequent: 250 mg/m² IV weekly. Not to exceed infusion rate of 10 mg/min.
precautions: RAS-testing is mandatory. Monitor for infusion reactions.
contraindications: Use only in metastatic setting. Don’t use if RAS mutations are present.

name: ERLOTINIB
uses: Targeted drug: EGFR mutant non-small cell lung cancer.
side_effects: Interstitial pneumonitis, increased serum transaminases, diarrhea, dry skin.
dosage: Adult: 150 mg/day oral.
precautions: EGFR mutation testing mandatory. Use only if EGFR positive.
interactions: Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice. Inhibitors of CYP3A4 increase toxicity.

name: GEFITINIB
uses: Targeted drug: EGFR mutant non-small cell lung cancer (same as erlotinib).
side_effects: Corneal erosion, conjunctivitis, skin rashes, hepatotoxicity.
dosage: Oral: 250 mg once a day.
precautions: Monitor LFTs and PT/INR if taking warfarin.
contraindications: Concurrent use of strong inhibitors of CYP3A4.
interactions: Rifampin and Phenytoin decrease blood levels. Itraconazole increases toxicity. Ranitidine decreases absorption.

name: IMATINIB
uses: Targeted drug: Ph+ CML, GIST, myelodysplastic/myeloproliferative disease.
side_effects: Fluid retention (edema), hepatotoxicity, muscle cramps, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia.
dosage: CML: Adult PO 400-600 mg daily. GIST: 400 mg daily. Oral Children: 340 mg/m²/day.
precautions: Monitor liver function monthly. Monitor for general fluid retention (common in blast crisis).
interactions: Toxicity increased by CYP3A4 inhibitors (clarithromycin, ritonavir). Efficacy decreased by CYP3A4 inducers (dexamethasone, rifampin).

name: NILOTINIB
uses: Targeted drug: Imatinib-resistant Ph+ CML, GIST.
side_effects: QT prolongation, pleural effusion, neutropenia.
dosage: New CML: 300 mg oral BD. Resistant/Intolerant: 400 mg BD.
precautions: Correct hypokalemia/hypomagnesemia before administration. Monitor Mg++ and K+ levels.
interactions: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase levels; decrease dose if must be used. Food interferes with absorption.

name: OSIMERTINIB
uses: Targeted drug: EGFR T790M mutation-positive NSCLC.
side_effects: Lymphopenia, cardiomyopathy, diarrhea.
dosage: 80 mg oral daily until disease progression.
precautions: Monitor for cardiomyopathy. Monitor patients with prior renal/hepatic disease closely.
interactions: Strong CYP3 inhibitors increase toxicity. Strong CYP3 inducers decrease concentration.

name: RITUXIMAB
uses: Targeted drug: B-cell lymphoma, mantle cell lymphoma, CML, rheumatoid arthritis, Wegener’s granulomatosis.
side_effects: Infusion reactions, late-onset neutropenia, transient hypotension, bleeding gum.
dosage: CLL/NHL: 237 mg/m² infusion weekly for 4 weeks. RA: 2 infusions of 1000 mg each separated by 2 weeks.
precautions: DO NOT ADMINISTER AS IV PUSH OR BOLUS. High risk of fatal infusion reactions. Reactivation of Hepatitis B. Caution if malignant cell count >10^9/L.

name: SUNITINIB
uses: Targeted drug: GIST, advanced renal carcinoma, pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor.
side_effects: Left ventricular dysfunction, hypertension, hypothyroidism, bleeding.
dosage: GIST: 50 mg PO qDay for 4 weeks, followed by 2 weeks drug-free.
precautions: Assess ANC and Platelets; stop if ANC <1x10^9/L or Platelets <50x10^9/L. Monitor LFTs monthly.
interactions: Toxicity increased by Bevacizumab. Erythromycin and haloperidol interactions.

name: TRASTUZUMAB
uses: Targeted drug: HER2-overexpressing breast cancer and gastric cancer.
side_effects: Cardiotoxicity, interstitial pneumonitis, ARDS, oligohydramnios (in pregnancy).
dosage: Metastatic breast cancer: 4 mg/kg IV over 90 min, then 2 mg/kg IV weekly.
precautions: Evaluate cardiac function (LVEF) every 3 months. Discontinue if LVEF decrease >16%. High risk of pulmonary toxicity.

name: ANASTROZOLE
uses: Hormonal drug: ER+ breast cancer, uterine leiomyoma, endometriosis.
side_effects: Hot flushes, osteoporosis, vaginal bleeding, thrombophlebitis, altered taste.
dosage: 1 mg daily.
precautions: Assess bone mineral density regularly. Avoid if CrCl < 20 ml/min.
interactions: Do not use with oral contraceptives or tamoxifen.

name: EXEMESTANE
uses: Hormonal drug: ER+ breast cancer in postmenopausal women.
side_effects: Hot flashes, diaphoresis, lymphopenia.
dosage: Adult: 25 mg/day after meals.
precautions: Use reliable contraception.

name: FULVESTRANT
uses: Hormonal drug: Advanced ER+ breast carcinoma.
side_effects: Hepatic failure, hyperbilirubinemia, angioedema.
dosage: IM 500 mg on Days 1, 15, 29 and monthly thereafter.
precautions: Caution in hepatic disease and coagulopathy.

name: TAMOXIFEN
uses: Hormonal drug: Breast cancer, endometrial cancer, anovulatory infertility.
side_effects: Endometrial polyps, vaginal bleeding, hot flushes, cataracts.
dosage: Breast cancer: 20 mg daily. Infertility: 20 mg daily on Days 2-5 of cycle.
precautions: Regularly assess CBC. Withdraw if WBC <3500 or Platelets <100,000. Periodic eye exams required.
interactions: Increased risk of bleeding with anticoagulants. Decreased level with rifampin.

name: TUBERCULIN, PURIFIED PROTEIN DERIVATIVE (PPD)
uses: Mantoux test; test for hypersensitivity to tuberculoprotein.
side_effects: Headache, nausea, malaise, rash, itch, vesicle formation, ulceration, necrosis, or pain at the administered site.
dosage: Intradermal injection: 10 units for 1 dose. (Note: 2 units is equivalent to 0.1 mL of 20 units/mL strength; 10 units is equivalent to 0.1 mL of 100 units/mL strength).
precautions: Avoid in patients with viral and bacterial infections (including HIV and severe tuberculosis), malignant disease, or those on corticosteroid/immunosuppressive therapy. Malnourished or elderly patients may show suppressed responses.
contraindications: Should not be used within 4 weeks of receiving live viral vaccination.
interactions: Effectiveness may be decreased by corticosteroids, immunosuppressives, or live vaccines (e.g., measles).

name: ANTI-D IMMUNOGLOBULIN (HUMAN)
uses: Prevention of formation of antibodies to rhesus positive blood cells in rhesus negative patients.
side_effects: Soreness at injection site, fever, anemia, intravascular hemolysis, renal insufficiency.
dosage: Post-abortion/birth of Rh+ infant: Deep IM injection 500 units within 72 hours; for transplacental bleed >4 ml, extra 100-125 units per ml fetal red cells. Sensitizing episodes (e.g., still birth): Up to 20 weeks gestation 250 units; after 20 weeks 500 units. Antenatal prophylaxis: Deep IM 500 units at weeks 28 and 34 of pregnancy.
precautions: Caution in Rh+ patients being treated for blood disorders and Rh- patients already possessing anti-D antibodies. Use only adequately screened preparations.

name: ANTIRABIES HYPERIMMUNE SERUM
uses: Passive immunization post-exposure or suspected exposure in unimmunized individuals (in conjunction with rabies vaccine).
side_effects: Soreness at injection site, mild temperature elevations, angioedema, skin rash, nephrotic syndrome, and rarely anaphylactic shock.
dosage: Pre-exposure: IM/Intradermal: 3 doses on days 0, 7, and 21 or 28. Post-exposure: IM: 5 doses on days 0, 3, 7, 14, and 28. Adult/Child: 20 units/kg by infiltration in and around the cleansed wound; remainder given IM into anterolateral thigh.
precautions: Safety in pregnancy not established (use only if benefits outweigh risks). Skin test should be performed before administration. Inquiry for history of allergy.
interactions: Antibodies may interfere with live vaccines (measles, mumps, polio, rubella); live vaccines should not be given within 3 months after serum administration.

name: POLYVENUM ANTISNAKE SERUM
uses: Venomous snake bite with clear indication of systemic or severe local involvement.
side_effects: Anaphylaxis with urticaria, hypotension, dyspnea, shock thermal sickness, and serum sickness.
dosage: Depends on the specific antivenom used. Refer to the specific product insert leaflet.
precautions: Resuscitation facilities must be available. NEVER inject into a finger or toe. Inject IM into a large muscle mass (gluteal region). Avoid nerve trunks. Notify physician if pregnant (venom may cause spontaneous abortion).

name: TETANUS IMMUNOGLOBULIN (HUMAN)
uses: Passive immunization against tetanus as part of management for tetanus-prone wounds.
side_effects: Soreness at injection site, temperature elevation, angioederma, nephrotic syndrome, and rare anaphylactic shock.
dosage: IM injection: 250 units. Increase to 500 units if the wound is older than 24 hours, heavily contaminated, or following burns.
precautions: Should NOT be given intravenously. Caution in patients with severe thrombocytopenia or coagulation disorders. Notify physician if pregnancy is planned/suspected.
interactions: May interfere with live viral vaccines (measles, mumps, polio, rubella); defer these vaccines for 3 months after injection.

name: PENTAVALENT VACCINE (DPT-HepB-Hib)
uses: Universal immunization for all newborns against Diphtheria, Tetanus, Pertussis, Hepatitis B, and Haemophilus influenzae type B.
side_effects: Mild local reactions, fever, malaise.
dosage: IM injection, child: 0.5 ml in 3 doses at 6, 10, and 14 weeks of birth.
precautions: Start for any child aged >6 weeks up to 1 year. Children initiated with DPT/HepB continue with those, not pentavalent.

name: MEASLES VACCINE
uses: Active immunization against measles.
side_effects: Local lymphadenopathy, rash, rarely thrombocytopenia purpura.
dosage: Infant: At 9 months: 0.5 ml. Prophylaxis (exposure): Over 9 months: 0.5 ml within 72 hours of contact.
precautions: Caution in febrile illness, seizure, or cerebral injury.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to antibiotics in vaccine, egg, or gelatin. Avoid in TB, AIDS, or respiratory infections.

name: MEASLES, MUMPS, RUBELLA (MMR) VACCINE
uses: Primary immunization against MMR; rubella immunization for seronegative women; pre-school booster.
side_effects: Parotid swelling (3rd week), sleep disturbances, arthropathy (2-3 weeks post-immunization), optic/peripheral neuritis.
dosage: First dose: IM/Deep SC, child 12-13 months: 0.5 ml. Second dose: IM/Deep SC, child 40 months - 5 years: 0.5 ml.
precautions: Leave an interval of 3 months after immunoglobulin or blood transfusion before vaccination.
interactions: Do not administer on the same day as Yellow Fever vaccine; maintain a minimum 4-week interval.

name: NORMAL IMMUNOGLOBULIN
uses: Hepatitis A, measles, mumps, rubella, varicella; ITP, Kawasaki disease, Guillain-Barre syndrome, allogenic bone marrow transplantation prophylaxis.
side_effects: Dizziness, light-headedness, nausea, vomiting, chills, fever, local pain at injection site.
dosage: ITP: Adult IV: 400 mg/kg/day for 2-5 days. Kawasaki: Adult IV: 1.6-2 g/kg divided over 2-5 days. Guillain-Barre: Adult IV: 400 mg/kg daily for 5 days. Hep A (Outbreak): Adult IM: 500 mg; Child <10yr: 250 mg.
precautions: Monitor for acute renal failure. Preparations containing maltose may falsely elevate blood glucose tests (GDH-PQQ methods).
contraindications: Patients with selective IgA deficiency who have known antibody against IgA.
interactions: May interfere with live vaccines (measles, mumps, rubella, varicella); give vaccines 3 weeks before or 3 months after immunoglobulin.

name: POLIOMYELITIS VACCINE (ORAL)/OPV (LIVE ATTENUATED)
uses: Active immunization against poliomyelitis.
side_effects: Rarely, vaccine-associated poliomyelitis in recipients or contacts.
dosage: Primary (Child): Oral: 3 drops at birth and at 6, 10, and 14 weeks. Reinforcing (Child): 3 drops at least 3 years after primary course and another 3 drops at 15-19 years. Unimmunized Adult: 3 doses of 3 drops with 4-week intervals.
precautions: Do not take with food containing preservatives; hypersensitivity to antibiotics in vaccine.

name: ROTAVIRUS VACCINE
uses: Immunization against gastro-enteritis caused by rotavirus.
side_effects: Abdominal cramps, abdominal pain, diarrhea, nausea, vomiting.
dosage: Oral, 6-24 weeks: 1.5 ml at least every 4 weeks for 2 doses. First dose must be given between 6-15 weeks of age; course must be completed before 24 weeks.
precautions: Postpone vaccination in cases of diarrhea or vomiting.
contraindications: History of intussusception, severe combined immunosuppression.

name: TETANUS TOXOID
uses: Active immunization against tetanus and neonatal tetanus; wound management prophylaxis.
side_effects: Rarely associated with peripheral neuropathy, seizures, fever, loss of appetite.
dosage: Primary (Adults/Adolescents): IM: 3 doses (0.5 ml) with 4 weeks between 1st/2nd dose and 6 months between 2nd/3rd dose. Reinforcing (Adult): 2 doses (0.5 ml) 10 years apart. Pregnant women (unimmunized): IM: 2 doses (0.5 ml) 4 weeks apart (2nd dose at least 2 weeks before delivery). Wounds: IM: 0.5 ml single dose.
precautions: Use separate syringes and sites if given with antitetanus immunoglobulin.

name: DIPHTHERIA ANTITOXINS
uses: Passive immunization in suspected cases of diphtheria.
side_effects: Anaphylaxis, urticaria, hypotension, dyspnea, shock thermal sickness, serum sickness (up to 12 days post-injection).
dosage: Therapeutic use (pharyngeal/laryngeal): IV infusion, adult: 20,000 to 40,000 units; child (<10 years): half of adult dose.
precautions: Initial test dose should be given; full dose must be under observation with resuscitation facilities available. Patients allergic to horse serum are at high risk.

name: HEPATITIS B IMMUNOGLOBULIN
uses: Post-exposure prophylaxis for healthcare workers, accidental inoculation, or babies of infected mothers.
side_effects: Hypertension, hypotension, malaise, agitation, amnesia, aphthous stomatitis, ecchymosis, splenomegaly.
dosage: IM injection (as soon as possible, ideally within 7 days): Adult/Child >10 yr: 500 units; Child <5 yr: 200 units; 5-9 yr: 300 units; Neonate: 200 units as soon as possible after birth.
precautions: Skin test must be done prior to giving the sera. Give at the same time as the vaccine if exposure is certain.
contraindications: Anaphylactic reaction to human globulin, thrombocytopenia, or coagulation disorders contraindicating IM injection.

name: HUMAN PAPILLOMA VIRUS VACCINE
uses: Prevention of premalignant genital (cervical, vulvar, vaginal) and anal lesions, cancers, and genital warts.
side_effects: N/A
dosage: Intramuscular, female >9 years: 0.5 ml for 1 dose, follow with 0.5 ml after 1 month, then 0.5 ml after 3 months (Total 3 doses within 12 months). Alternative (9-13 years): 0.5 ml for 1 dose, follow with 0.5 ml after 6 months.
precautions: If course is interrupted, resume but do not repeat. Vaccination should be postponed until completion of pregnancy.

name: INFLUENZA VACCINE
uses: Annual immunization against seasonal influenza.
side_effects: Epistaxis, febrile convulsions, transient thrombocytopenia, vasculitis (adults).
dosage: IM injection (Children 6 mo - 9 yr): 0.5 ml for 1 dose, followed by 0.5 ml after 4 weeks. Intranasal (Child 2-9 yr): 0.1 ml (total) into each nostril, followed by 0.1 ml after 4 weeks. General: IM: 0.5 ml for 1 dose.
precautions: Child under 5 years at increased risk of febrile convulsions. Egg-free vaccine required for those with egg allergy.

name: RABIES VACCINE
uses: Active immunization; pre-exposure prophylaxis and post-exposure treatment.
side_effects: Mild gastrointestinal disturbance, headache, dizziness.
dosage: Pre-exposure: IM: 3 doses (0, 7, 28 days) OR Intradermal: 3 doses (0.1 ml) on same days. Post-exposure (Unimmunized): IM: 1 dose on days 0, 3, 7, 14, 28 (Total 5 doses). Post-exposure (Fully Immunized): IM/Intradermal: 2 doses separated by 3 days.
precautions: Use separate syringes and sites if given with rabies immunoglobulin.

name: TYPHOID VACCINE
uses: Active immunization against typhoid.
side_effects: Anaphylactoid reaction, nausea, vomiting, fever, redness, itching, abdominal pain.
dosage: Oral (Capsules, >5 yrs): One dose on days 1, 3, 5, and 7. Oral (Suspension, >2 yrs): One dose on days 1, 3, and 5. Vi capsular polysaccharide vaccine: SC/IM: 0.5 ml (child >=2 yrs and adults), reinforce every 3 years.
precautions: Proguanil, mefloquine and antibiotics must be stopped 3 days before and after administration of Ty21a oral vaccine.
interactions: Antibiotics, Proguanil, and Mefloquine interfere with oral vaccine.

name: YELLOW FEVER VACCINE
uses: Active immunization against yellow fever.
side_effects: Headache, myalgia, weakness; rarely encephalitis (infants), viscerotropic disease, multiple organ failure (elderly).
dosage: Child (9-12 months): 0.5 ml single dose by deep SC/IM. Adult/Child (>9 months): 0.5 ml single dose by deep SC/IM.
precautions: N/A
contraindications: Infants under 9 months, pregnancy, severe immunodeficiency, egg allergy.

name: NEPAL EPI SCHEDULE (2017)
uses: Routine infant immunization protocol in Nepal.
side_effects: N/A
dosage: At Birth: BCG (Tuberculosis). 6 Weeks: Rota (1st), Polio (1st), FIPV (1st), PCV (1st), Pentavalent (1st). 10 Weeks: Rota (2nd), Polio (2nd), PCV (2nd), Pentavalent (2nd). 14 Weeks: Polio (3rd), FIPV (2nd), Pentavalent (3rd). 9 Months: PCV (3rd), Measles-Rubella (1st). 12 Months: Japanese Encephalitis. 15 Months: Measles-Rubella (2nd).
precautions: N/A

name: BENZOIC ACID AND SALICYLIC ACID
uses: Antibacterial/Antifungal: Superficial dermatophyte infections - Tinea corporis, Tinea cruris.
side_effects: Erythema, hypersensitivity reactions, itching, mild burning sensation, occasional local irritation.
dosage: Apply twice daily until the infected skin is shed (usually at least 4 weeks).
precautions: Salicylate toxicity may occur if applied on large areas of skin. Avoid broken or inflamed skin. Avoid contact with eyes and mucous membranes.

name: FUSIDIC ACID
uses: Antibacterial: Staphylococcal skin infection (impetigo, folliculitis), erythrasma, pitted keratolysis.
side_effects: Hypersensitivity reactions.
dosage: Apply 3–4 times a day to the skin.
precautions: Avoid contact with eyes. To avoid development of resistance, do not use for longer than 10 days.
contraindications: Allergy to fusidic acid or its salts.

name: METRONIDAZOLE
uses: Antibacterial: Rosacea, malodorous gravitational and decubitus ulcers.
side_effects: Dryness, itching, burning, stinging, metallic taste in mouth, paraesthesias.
dosage: Acute rosacea: Apply twice daily for 8 weeks. Malodorous ulcers: Apply 1-2 times a day to clean wound with non-adherent dressing.
precautions: Avoid exposure to strong sunlight or UV light. Use with caution in patients with blood dyscrasias or hepatic disease.

name: MUPIROCIN
uses: Antibacterial: Bacterial skin infections (Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus pyogenes), excluding pseudomonal infection.
side_effects: Burning sensation, local reactions, pruritus, rash, urticaria.
dosage: Apply up to 3 times a day for up to 10 days.
precautions: Renal impairment, burns, large open wounds. Discontinue if chemical irritation occurs.

name: SILVER SULFADIAZINE
uses: Antibacterial: Minor burns.
side_effects: Allergic reactions, argyria (after large area/prolonged use), leucopenia, burning.
dosage: Apply once daily or twice daily if exudative.
precautions: G-6PD deficiency. Stop treatment immediately if blood disorders or rashes develop.

name: AMOROLFINE
uses: Antifungal: Fungal nail infections, dermatophyte infections, yeast infections.
side_effects: Burning sensation, erythema, hypersensitivity reactions, itching.
dosage: Nails: Apply 1–2 times a week (6 months for fingers, 9–12 months for toes). Skin: Apply once daily for 4 weeks.
precautions: Hypersensitivity. Avoid contact with ears, eyes, and mucous membranes. Caution in children likely to suck digits.

name: CLOTRIMAZOLE
uses: Antifungal: Tinea pedis, T. cruris, T. corporis, T. versicolor, Cutaneous candidiasis.
side_effects: Local irritation, erythema, hypersensitivity reactions, mild burning sensation.
dosage: Apply 2-3 times daily for 4-6 weeks.
precautions: Avoid contact with eyes and mucous membranes.

name: GENTIAN VIOLET
uses: Antifungal: Cutaneous/mucocutaneous infections caused by Candida albicans.
side_effects: Irritation, mucous membrane ulcerations.
dosage: Local application: Apply locally 2-3 times daily.
precautions: N/A
contraindications: Avoid use in ulcerated lesions, broken skin, or mucous membranes.

name: MICONAZOLE NITRATE
uses: Antifungal: Fungal skin infections, nail infections, oral fungal infection, vaginal candidiasis.
side_effects: Local irritation and burning.
dosage: Skin: Apply twice daily for 10 days after lesions heal. Nails: Apply 1-2 times a day.
precautions: Avoid contact with eyes and mucous membranes.

name: NYSTATIN
uses: Antifungal: Mucocutaneous infection, vaginal infections.
side_effects: Contact dermatitis, SJS (rare).
dosage: Mucocutaneous: Apply q8-12h for 2 weeks. Vaginal: Insert 1 tab/day qHS for 2 weeks.
precautions: Cream is preferred over ointment for intertriginous areas. Moist lesions best treated with powder.

name: SERTACONAZOLE
uses: Antifungal: Tinea pedis.
side_effects: Contact dermatitis, dry skin, burning, hyperpigmentation.
dosage: Apply BID for 4 weeks.
precautions: Cross-reactivity with other imidazole antifungals may occur.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Not for ophthalmic, oral, or intravaginal use.

name: TERBINAFINE
uses: Antifungal: Tinea infections (pedis, corporis, cruris).
side_effects: Erythema, hypersensitivity reactions, itching, local irritation.
dosage: Apply 1–2 times a day for 1–2 weeks.
precautions: Maximum treatment duration: 4 weeks.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Not for oral, intravaginal, or ophthalmic use.

name: BENZYL BENZOATE
uses: Parasitic: Scabies.
side_effects: Burning sensation (especially on genitalia), rashes, skin irritation.
dosage: Apply over whole body; wash off after 24 hours. A third application may be required.
precautions: Dilute for use in children. Avoid contact with eyes and mucous membranes. Avoid broken or infected skin.

name: IVERMECTIN
uses: Parasitic/Anti-acne: Lice, inflammatory lesions of Rosacea.
side_effects: Conjunctivitis, ocular hyperemia, eye irritation, dry skin, burning.
dosage: Lice: Apply 0.5% lotion to dry hair for 10 minutes then rinse. Rosacea: Apply 1% cream to affected area once daily.
precautions: Administer to children only under direct adult supervision to prevent ingestion.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Not for oral, ophthalmic, or intravaginal use.

name: PERMETHRIN
uses: Parasitic: Scabies, body lice, head lice.
side_effects: Local irritation, rashes, itching, erythema.
dosage: Scabies/Lice: Apply over whole body and wash off after 8-12 hours; repeat after 7 days if necessary.
precautions: Avoid contact with eyes. Medical supervision required for infants 2 months – 2 years.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Do not use on broken or infected skin.

name: ACICLOVIR
uses: Viral: Herpes labialis, genital herpes, herpetic keratitis.
side_effects: Burning, stinging, pruritus, dry lips, angioedema.
dosage: Labialis: Apply 5 times daily for 4 days. Genital: Apply every 3 hours (6 times daily) for 7 days.
precautions: Not for use on eye or inside mouth. Caution in immunocompromised patients.

name: CLOBETASONE BUTYRATE
uses: Inflammatory: Eczemas and dermatitis of all types.
side_effects: Hyperglycemia, folliculitis, hypertrichosis, skin irritation.
dosage: Apply 1–2 times a day thinly. Limit treatment to 2 weeks.
precautions: Do not use with occlusive dressings. Maintenance between more potent steroid courses.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Monotherapy for primary bacterial infections. Use on face, axilla, or groin.

name: CLOBETASOL PROPIONATE
uses: Inflammatory: Corticosteroid responsive dermatoses, scalp psoriasis, plaque psoriasis.
side_effects: Hyperglycemia, burning, skin atrophy, acne.
dosage: Apply 1–2 times a day for up to 2 weeks; max 50g per week.
precautions: Do not use with occlusive dressings. Limit use to 2 weeks.

name: DITHRANOL (ANTHRALIN)
uses: Inflammatory: Psoriasis.
side_effects: Local burning, irritation, stains hair and skin.
dosage: 0.1–0.5% suitable for overnight treatment. 1–2% cream for maximum 1 hour.
precautions: Avoid sensitive areas of skin; avoid use near eyes.

name: FLUOCINOLONE ACETONIDE
uses: Inflammatory: Severe inflammatory skin disorders, Psoriasis.
side_effects: Hyperglycemia, burning, folliculitis.
dosage: Apply 1–2 times a day thinly.
precautions: Do not use with occlusive dressings.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity; use on face, axillae, or groin.

name: FLUTICASONE
uses: Inflammatory: Dermatitis and eczemas unresponsive to less potent steroids, Psoriasis.
side_effects: HPA axis suppression, Cushing syndrome, hypertrichosis.
dosage: Apply 1–2 times a day thinly.
precautions: Not to use with occlusive dressings.
contraindications: Children under 2 months, skin infections, skin atrophy.

name: HYDROCORTISONE
uses: Inflammatory: Mild inflammatory skin disorders, nappy rash.
side_effects: Burning, folliculitis, striae.
dosage: Apply 1–2 times a day for 2 weeks. Nappy rash: Max 1 week.
precautions: HPA suppression risk if used >2 weeks at high potency.
contraindications: Broken or infected skin (cold sores, athlete's foot). Use on face or ano-genital region.

name: MOMETASONE FUROATE
uses: Inflammatory: Severe inflammatory skin disorders, Psoriasis.
side_effects: Burning, tingling, pruritus, adrenal suppression (if overused).
dosage: Apply once daily thinly.
precautions: Avoid application over large areas or under occlusive dressings (systemic absorption risk).

name: TACROLIMUS
uses: Inflammatory: Atopic eczema, Seborrheic Dermatitis, Vitiligo, Lichen sclerosus.
side_effects: Application-site infections, Kaposi’s varicelliform eruption, rash.
dosage: Short-term: Apply twice daily until lesion clears. Prevention: Apply twice weekly.
precautions: Avoid UV light (sunlight, sunlamps). Avoid contact with eyes and mucous membranes.
contraindications: Lactation. Malignant skin lesions. Congenital epidermal barrier defect.
interactions: Risk of facial flushing and skin irritation with alcohol consumption.

name: ACITRETIN
uses: Retinoid: Psoriasis, severe congenital ichthyosis, Darier’s disease.
side_effects: Cheilitis, alopecia, hypertriglyceridemia, skin peeling, hyperostosis.
dosage: Initially 25–30 mg daily for 2–4 weeks; adjusted to 25–50 mg daily; max 75 mg.
precautions: Highly teratogenic. Avoid excessive sunlight. Monitor liver function and serum lipids.
interactions: Alcohol converts acitretin to etretinate (remains in body for years). Tetracyclines increase intracranial pressure.

name: ADAPALENE
uses: Retinoid/Anti-acne: Mild to moderate acne vulgaris.
side_effects: Skin irritation, erythema, scaling, stinging.
dosage: Apply once daily thinly in the evening.
precautions: Avoid accumulation in angles of nose, eyes, or mouth. Avoid UV light exposure.
contraindications: Pregnancy. Apply to cuts, abrasions, or sunburnt skin.

name: ISOTRETINOIN
uses: Retinoid/Anti-acne: Acne vulgaris, ichthyosiform disorders.
side_effects: Anaemia, epistaxis, skin scaling, epidermal fragility, raised triglycerides/LFTs.
dosage: Initially 500 micrograms/kg daily; increased if necessary to 1 mg/kg for 16–24 weeks.
precautions: Monitor for depression. Risk of dry eye/keratitis. Avoid use with abrasive cleaners.
interactions: Alcohol increases teratogenicity. Tetracyclines increase intracranial hypertension risk.

name: TAZAROTENE
uses: Retinoid: Psoriasis and acne.
side_effects: Burning, contact dermatitis, desquamation, worsening of psoriasis.
dosage: Apply once daily usually for 12 weeks, apply in the evening.
precautions: Avoid contact with eczematous skin, eyes, face, or hair-covered scalp. Effective contraception required.

name: COAL TAR
uses: Coal tar: Psoriasis, Chronic atopic eczema, Seborrhoeic dermatitis.
side_effects: Acne-like eruptions, photosensitivity, skin irritation.
dosage: Eczema (Paste): 1–3 times a day. Shampoo: 100 ml per bath. Seborrhoeic: Shampoo every 2–3 days.
precautions: Avoid application to face or skin flexures.
contraindications: Broken or inflamed skin; avoid eye area, genital area, or mucosal areas.

name: CALCIPOTRIOL
uses: Vitamin D analogue: Psoriasis.
side_effects: Local skin reactions, paraesthesia, aggravation of psoriasis.
dosage: Apply 1–2 times a day. Max 5 mg (100g ointment) per week.
precautions: Avoid exposure to sunlight/sun lamps. Avoid use on face. Risk of hypercalcaemia in erythrodermic psoriasis.

name: ALUMINIUM CHLORIDE HEXAHYDRATE
uses: Antiperspirant: Hyperhidrosis, bromidrosis, prevention of tinea pedis.
side_effects: Skin irritation.
dosage: Apply once daily at night to dry skin; wash off next morning.
precautions: Avoid contact with eyes/mucous membranes. Do not shave axillae within 12 hours of use.

name: GLYCOPYRRONIUM BROMIDE (GLYCOPYRROLATE)
uses: Antimuscarinic: Hyperhidrosis of axilla/face, Frey’s syndrome.
side_effects: Tingling at site, dryness.
