dosage: Treat only 1 site at a time; max 2 sites in 24 hours. Do not wash for 3-4 hours.
precautions: Avoid contact with nose, mouth, and eyes.

name: FLUOROURACIL
uses: Antimetabolite/Photodamage: Actinic keratoses, superficial malignant lesions.
side_effects: Burning, crusting, soreness at application site.
dosage: Apply 1–2 times a day for 3–4 weeks. Max skin area 500 cm².
precautions: Avoid contact with eyes and mucous membranes. Do not apply to bleeding lesions.

name: DOXEPIN
uses: Antipruritus: Pruritus (eczema).
side_effects: Dizziness, drowsiness.
dosage: Apply up to 3 g 3–4 times a day thinly. Max 12 g per day.
precautions: Risk of QT prolongation. Coverage should be <10% of body surface area.
contraindications: Urinary retention, closed-angle glaucoma, prostatic hypertrophy.
interactions: Potentiated by alcohol. Do not use with MAO inhibitors.

name: AZELAIC ACID
uses: Anticomedonal/Depigmenting: Facial acne vulgaris, rosacea, melasma.
side_effects: Local irritation, burning, stinging.
dosage: Apply twice daily.
precautions: Avoid contact with eyes, mouth, and mucous membranes. Monitor for hypopigmentation in dark complexions.

name: SELENIUM SULPHIDE
uses: Essential trace element: Seborrhoeic dermatitis, dandruff, Tinea versicolor.
side_effects: Local irritation, tremors, lower abdominal pain.
dosage: Seborrhoeic: Twice weekly for 2 weeks. Tinea versicolor: Daily for 7 days (leave on for 10 min).
precautions: Not for ophthalmic, oral, or anal use.

name: MINOXIDIL
uses: Alopecia: Androgenetic alopecia.
side_effects: Headache, local irritation.
dosage: Apply 1 ml twice daily to affected areas of scalp.
precautions: Avoid contact with broken or inflamed skin. Avoid inhalation of spray mist. Avoid occlusive dressings.
interactions: Avoid topical drugs which enhance absorption.

name: EFLORNITHINE
uses: Hirsutism: Adjunct to laser therapy for facial hirsutism in women.
side_effects: Stinging at site, rash, alopecia, anorexia.
dosage: Apply twice daily thinly.
precautions: Discontinue if no improvement after 4 months.

name: CHLORHEXIDINE
uses: Cleanser/Antiseptic: Skin disinfection, umbilical cord stump care.
side_effects: Chemical burns in preterm neonates.
dosage: Pre-op: Dilute 1 in 10 (0.5%). General disinfection: Dilute 1 in 100 (0.05%).
precautions: Avoid contact with brain, eyes, meninges, and middle ear.
contraindications: Do not use in body cavities (deep wound cleansing). Not for presurgery of face/head.

name: POTASSIUM PERMANGANATE
uses: Cleanser/Antiseptic: suppurating eczematous reactions and wounds.
side_effects: Corrosion, burns, pain.
dosage: Wet compress twice daily. For dressings, use 1 in 40,000 to 1:25,000 solution.
precautions: Irritant to mucous membranes. Concentrated solution causes erosion.

name: CAPSAICIN
uses: Depigmenting/Pain relief: Post-herpetic neuralgia, musculoskeletal pain, diabetic neuropathy, psoriasis.
side_effects: Transient increased pain, burning, erythema.
dosage: Apply to affected area TID or QID for 3-4 weeks.
precautions: Do not apply to face or scalp. Avoid eyes and mucous membranes.

name: HYDROQUINONE
uses: Depigmenting: Melasma, post inflammatory hyperpigmentation.
side_effects: Mild skin irritation, sensitization, inflammatory reaction.
dosage: Local application twice a day or at night.
precautions: Exogenous ochronosis risk in black skin. Do not apply near eyes or to abraded skin.

name: PSORALENS
uses: Depigmenting: Vitiligo, psoriasis, cutaneous T cell lymphoma.
side_effects: Irritation, blistering, nausea, cataract formation (if eyes unprotected).
dosage: Local application 30 min before UVA exposure. Oral: 0.5-0.7 mg/kg twice a week, 2 hours before exposure.
precautions: Ensure skin is clean and dry. Avoid other artificial UV treatments.

name: CHLORAMPHENICOL
uses: Superficial bacterial infection (broad spectrum antibiotics).
side_effects: Transient stinging.
dosage: Bacterial conjunctival infection: Eye drop: 1 drop 4-6 times a day for 5 to 7 days; Eye ointment: apply twice daily (at night if drops used during day).
precautions: Avoid unless essential; theoretical risk of bone marrow toxicity.

name: CIPROFLOXACIN
uses: Superficial bacterial infections, corneal ulcer.
side_effects: Corneal deposits (reversible), ocular discomfort, ocular hyperemia, taste disturbance, contact dermatitis.
dosage: Superficial infection: Eye drop: 1 drop 4-6 times daily (max 5-7 days). Eye ointment: 1.25 cm 3 times daily for 2 days then twice daily for 5 days. Corneal ulcer: 1 drop 2 hourly until ulcer heals (titrated to response).
precautions: Avoid wearing contact lens.
interactions: Not to be given with tizanidine (α2 agonist).

name: GENTAMICIN
uses: Bacterial eye infection, corneal ulcer.
side_effects: Transient irritation, burning, itching, overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms including fungi.
dosage: Bacterial conjunctival infection: 1 drop 4-6 times daily; reduce frequency as controlled and continue for 48 hrs after healing. Fortified gentamicin can be used for corneal ulcer.
precautions: Monitoring for overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms.

name: LEVOFLOXACIN
uses: Bacterial corneal ulcer.
side_effects: Dry eye, corneal deposits, contact dermatitis.
dosage: Bacterial corneal ulcer: apply every 2 hours for first 2 days (8 times a day), then 4 times a day for 3 days. Titrated according to response.
precautions: N/A

name: OFLOXACIN
uses: Bacterial conjunctivitis, corneal ulcer.
side_effects: Irritation and contact dermatitis.
dosage: Bacterial conjunctivitis/corneal ulcer: Apply every 2-4 hours for first 2 days then reduce to 4 times a day for maximum 10 days.
precautions: See under ciprofloxacin.

name: POLYMYXIN B
uses: Superficial infection of eye (effective for pseudomonas aeruginosa), prophylaxis of infection in ocular surgery.
side_effects: Irritation and contact dermatitis.
dosage: Same as ciprofloxacin.
precautions: Not given systemically.

name: TETRACYCLINE
uses: Superficial bacterial infection, chlamydial infection, trachoma, chemical injury, blepharitis.
side_effects: N/A
dosage: Given once or twice a day.
precautions: Topical use may result in overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms like fungi; SLE.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity; lactation; children less than 12 years.
interactions: With topical corticosteroid, may mask clinical signs of infection.

name: ACYCLOVIR
uses: Herpes simplex epithelial keratitis and herpes zoster ophthalmicus associated keratitis.
side_effects: Local burning and stinging, blepharitis, superficial punctate keratitis.
dosage: Ointment: apply 5 times a day for 2 weeks to 3 weeks.
precautions: Can be used in immunocompromised.

name: GANCICLOVIR
uses: Herpes simplex epithelial keratitis, Herpes zoster ophthalmicus, CMV retinitis.
side_effects: Local irritation and visual disturbance.
dosage: Herpes simplex: 5 times a day until complete re-epithelization, then 3 times daily for 7 days (total 21 days). CMV retinitis: IV 5 mg/kg infusion over 1 hour q12 hrly for 14-21 days; maintenance 1000 mg 3 times a day.
precautions: Use with caution in pregnancy and lactation.

name: IDOXURIDINE
uses: HSV keratitis, CMV, varicella zoster.
side_effects: Local irritation, edema of eyelids, photophobia, superficial punctate keratitis, corneal filaments.
dosage: 1 drop every hour during day and every 2 hrs at night until lesions do not stain with fluorescence (usual 21 days). Ointment: q4hrly during day and once before bedtime.
precautions: Do not give steroid with it locally. Caution in pregnancy and lactation.

name: FLUCONAZOLE
uses: Keratomycosis (fungal keratitis).
side_effects: Conjunctival hyperemia and irritation.
dosage: 1 drop instilled on affected eye every 2-4 hours according to severity.
precautions: Miconazole can be administered as subconjunctival and intra-vitreal injection for fungal endophthalmitis.

name: NATAMYCIN
uses: All keratitis especially fusarium solani keratitis, aspergillus.
side_effects: Conjunctival hyperemia and irritation.
dosage: Start with 1 drop every 1-2 hours on day 1, then reduce to 1 drop every 3-4 hourly for 2-3 weeks.
precautions: N/A

name: BETAMETHASONE
uses: Severe ocular inflammation, uveitis, endophthalmitis, post-operative inflammation.
side_effects: Glaucoma, posterior capsular cataract, adrenal suppression (prolonged use), corneal thinning, scleral thinning, blurred vision.
dosage: Eye drop: apply every 1-2 hour until controlled then decrease frequency. Eye ointment: apply 2-4 times a day (alternately apply at night in combination with drops).
precautions: Check intra-ocular pressure frequently in prolonged therapy. Protect from light.
contraindications: Acute untreated purulent bacterial, viral and fungal infections.

name: DICLOFENAC
uses: Inhibits intra-operative miosis, post-operative inflammation, seasonal allergic conjunctivitis, mild ocular surface inflammation.
side_effects: Ocular irritation, burning, tearing, conjunctival hyperemia, superficial punctate keratitis, retardation of re-epithelialization.
dosage: For post-op. inflammation: 1 drop 4 times a day for 1-2 weeks.
precautions: Caution in pregnancy, lactation, and children. Protect from light.

name: FLUOROMETHOLONE
uses: Local treatment of inflammation (short term).
side_effects: Adrenal suppression (prolonged use), glaucoma, corneal/scleral thinning.
dosage: Child/adult: apply 1 drop 2 to 6 hours according to severity.
precautions: N/A

name: FLURBIPROFEN
uses: Ocular surface inflammation, inhibition of intra-operative miosis.
side_effects: Ocular irritation, conjunctival hyperemia, superficial punctate keratitis.
dosage: Before surgery: 1 drop every 30 min for 4 times (max 4 drops). For inflammation: 1 drop 4 times a day for 2-4 weeks.
precautions: Caution in lactation.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to NSAIDS; HSV keratitis (dendritic); pregnancy.

name: INDOMETHACIN
uses: Cystoid macular degeneration, anterior uveitis, vernal conjunctivitis, prevention of intra-op miosis, episcleritis, scleritis, gastric ulcer.
side_effects: Corneal changes and deposits, ocular irritation, conjunctival hyperemia, superficial punctate keratitis.
dosage: 25 mg TDS or SR 75 mg OD for 7-10 days.
precautions: N/A

name: KETOROLAC
uses: Superficial ocular surface inflammation, pain, ocular itching (allergic conjunctivitis), postoperative inflammation, cystic macular edema.
side_effects: GI ulcer/bleeding, bronchospasm, psychosis, dry mouth, fever, bradycardia, transient stinging, local irritation.
dosage: Ophthalmic: 1 drop 4 times daily (7-10 days for inflammation; 3-4 weeks for edema). Oral: 10 mg every 4-6 hourly (max 40 mg/day, 7 days). Parenteral: 60 mg IM/30 mg IV (max 120 mg daily, 2 days).
precautions: Elderly, weight <50 kg, heart failure. Monitor renal function closely.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to aspirin/NSAIDS; asthma; coagulation disorders; labor; renal impairment; cerebrovascular bleeding.

name: PREDNISOLONE
uses: Anti-inflammatory agent (external/intra ocular), post-operative inflammation.
side_effects: Adrenal suppression (prolonged use), glaucoma, corneal/scleral thinning.
dosage: 1 drop every 1-2 hour until controlled then taper.
precautions: Lactation, old age, children. Long term therapy: check Potassium, blood/urine glucose, and H-P-A axis suppression.

name: KETOTIFEN
uses: Allergic conjunctivitis.
side_effects: Punctate corneal epithelial erosions, transient burning, headache, photophobia, dry eyes.
dosage: 2 times daily.
precautions: N/A

name: OLOPATADINE
uses: Allergic conjunctivitis, vernal keratoconjunctivitis.
side_effects: Ocular-local irritation, hyperemia, headache, rhinitis.
dosage: 2 times (0.1%) daily for max 4 months; 0.2% once daily only.
precautions: N/A

name: SODIUM CHROMOGLYCATE
uses: Allergic conjunctivitis, allergic keratoconjunctivitis.
side_effects: Transient burning.
dosage: 4 times daily (2%) and 2 times daily (4%).
precautions: Do not exceed frequency of administration.

name: ACETAZOLAMIDE
uses: Open-angle glaucoma, angle-closure glaucoma (preoperatively if surgery delayed).
side_effects: Seizures, confusion, cholestatic jaundice, metabolic acidosis.
dosage: Acute attack: Adult: PO/IV 500 mg stat followed by 250mg TID or QID.
precautions: Long-term use in non-congestive angle-closure glaucoma.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to sulfonamide; severe renal/hepatic disease; electrolyte imbalance; hypercalciuria; COPD.
interactions: Increases action of Amphetamines, Phenytoin, quinidine; toxicity of salicylate and cyclosporine; cardiac toxicity with arsenic trioxide.

name: BIMATOPROST
uses: Open angle glaucoma or ocular HTN, Hypotrichosis of eyelashes.
side_effects: Cataract, increased iris pigmentation, blepharitis, eyelid darkening, conjunctival edema, hypertrichosis, macular edema.
dosage: 1 drop in affected eye OD evening.
precautions: Risk factors for macular edema, active intraocular inflammation (uveitis).
contraindications: Hypersensitivity; children <16 years; aphakia/pseudoaphakia with torn posterior lens capsule.

name: BRIMONIDINE
uses: Glaucoma (IOP lowering) with increase in optic nerve head perfusion.
side_effects: Conjunctival blending, eyelid retraction, discomfort, ocular allergy (blepharoconjunctivitis), dry mouth, headache, lethargy.
dosage: 1 drop twice daily.
precautions: Coronary and cerebral insufficiency, hepatic and renal impairment; safety not established in children.

name: DORZOLAMIDE
uses: Elevated intraocular pressure, ocular hypertension, open-angle glaucoma.
side_effects: Headache, blurred vision, allergy, burning/stinging, corneal epithelial toxicity.
dosage: Instill 1 drop of a 2% solution into affected eye TDS.
precautions: Hepatic/renal disease; electrolyte disturbance. Notify if vision changes.
interactions: Increased effects of carbonic anhydrase inhibitors, salicylate.

name: LATANOPROST
uses: Open angle glaucoma, ocular hypertension.
side_effects: Conjunctival hyperemia, iris color change (brown pigmentation), ocular pruritis, xerophthalmia, blepharitis, cataract, rash.
dosage: Instill 1 drop in each affected eye every night.
precautions: Eye infection, renal/hepatic function impairment, intra ocular inflammation.

name: MANNITOL
uses: Reduce elevated IOP.
side_effects: Renal impairment, pulmonary edema, heart failure, hyponatremia, headache.
dosage: 1-2 g/kg or 5ml/kg IV infused over 30-60 minutes up to 4 times/day.
precautions: Use with caution in CCF and Hypertension.
contraindications: Anuria, severe renal disease, pulmonary edema, intracranial bleeding, heart failure, dehydration.

name: PILOCARPINE
uses: Acute-angle-closure glaucoma, open angle glaucoma.
side_effects: Accommodative spasm, miosis, follicular conjunctivitis, band keratopathy, retinal detachment, nausea, bronchial spasm.
dosage: 1 drop 4 times a day.
precautions: Use with caution in pregnancy and lactation.
contraindications: Avoid in nuclear/subcapsular cataract, neovascular/uveitis glaucoma, asthma, retinal detachment, iritis.

name: TIMOLOL
uses: Open angle glaucoma, angle closure glaucoma, lowering IOP after cataract surgery.
side_effects: Itching, conjunctivitis, keratitis, bradycardia, heart block.
dosage: 1 drop twice daily.
precautions: Caution in DM, thyroid disorders, and diminished myocardial contractility.

name: TRAVOPROST
uses: Reduction of elevated IOP in open angle glaucoma or ocular HTN.
side_effects: Ocular hyperemia, decreased visual acuity, cataract, keratitis, hypercholesterolemia, HTN, hypotension.
dosage: Eye drop 0.004%.
precautions: N/A

name: ATROPINE
uses: Cycloplegic refraction in children, cyclospasm, neovascular glaucoma.
side_effects: Local irritation, raised IOP, dermatitis, flushing, dryness of skin, blurred vision.
dosage: 1 drop up to 3 times daily.
precautions: N/A

name: CYCLOPENTOLATE
uses: Same as atropine.
side_effects: Same as atropine.
dosage: 1 drop every 5-10 minutes, not to exceed maximum 3 times for cycloplegic refraction.
precautions: Same as atropine.

name: HOMATROPINE
uses: Same as atropine.
side_effects: N/A
dosage: 1 drop twice to thrice daily.
precautions: Same as atropine.

name: PHENYLEPHRINE
uses: Uveitis to prevent posterior synechia, mydriatics.
side_effects: Burning eye pain, blurred vision, allergic conjunctivitis, systemic sympathomimetic effects.
dosage: Eye drops 2.5% - 10%.
precautions: Hypertension, cardiac disorders, diabetes mellitus.
contraindications: Angle closure glaucoma; children and elderly.

name: TROPICAMIDE
uses: Refraction procedure, mydriasis for fundus evaluation, corneal ulcer, uveitis.
side_effects: Increased IOP, burning, photophobia, systemic effects.
dosage: 1 drop every 5-10 minutes three times for fundus evaluation; 1 drop three times for therapeutic purpose.
precautions: Store at 8-15°C.

name: ACETYLCYSTEINE
uses: Dry eye.
side_effects: Temporary blurring of vision.
dosage: Instill 1 drop 3-4 times a day and as required.
precautions: Usually used together with hypromellose.

name: BEVACIZUMAB
uses: Choroidal neovascularization, macular edema (CRVO, diabetic).
side_effects: Transient rise in IOP, sterile/bacterial endophthalmitis, iridocyclitis, superficial punctate keratitis, cataract, retinal disorders.
dosage: 1.25 mg by intra-vitreal injection repeated after 4-6 weeks.
precautions: Ocular/peri-ocular infection, irreversible ischemic visual loss, diabetic patients with HbA1C>12%, history of strokes/TIA.

name: BUPIVACAINE
uses: Local anaesthesia.
side_effects: N/A
dosage: 0.5% infiltrated.
precautions: Hepatic impairment.

name: CARBOMER
uses: Dry eyes including keratoconjunctivitis, unstable tear film.
side_effects: N/A
dosage: Apply 3-4 times a day or when required.
precautions: Remove contact lens before use.

name: CYCLOSPORINE
uses: Corneal melting (autoimmune), graft rejection prevention, keratoconjunctivitis (Vernal/HSV), dry eye.
side_effects: Ocular burning, conjunctival hyperemia, discharge, eye pain, pruritus.
dosage: 1 drop two times a day approximately 12 hours apart in each eye.
precautions: May be used with artificial tears; allow 15 minutes interval between products.

name: FLUORESCEIN SODIUM
uses: Diagnostic staining, ophthalmic angiography.
side_effects: N/A
dosage: Eye drops 1%, 2% and 4%.
precautions: Protect from light.

name: HYPROMELLOSE
uses: Dry eye, moisten hardened contact lens.
side_effects: Eye irritation, blurred vision, stickiness of eyelashes.
dosage: Put 1 drop 3-4 times a day as required (may be used hourly).
precautions: Hypersensitivity. Contains Benzalkonium chloride (discolors soft contact lens).

name: LIQUID PARAFFIN
uses: Dry eyes (night use), recurrent epithelial erosion.
side_effects: Irritation, burning, stinging, temporary blurring of vision.
dosage: Usually applied at bedtime.
precautions: Apply other drops first then wait 5 mins before ointment.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Should not be used while wearing contact lens.

name: POLYVINYL ALCOHOL
uses: Tear deficiency (useful when ocular surface mucin decreased).
side_effects: See under hypromellose.
dosage: Child/adult: apply as required.
precautions: N/A
contraindications: Concomitant droxidopa, MAOI, or furazolidone in last 14 days.

name: SODIUM CHLORIDE
uses: Short term relief of corneal edema, comfort drops for lens removal, tear deficiency, bullous keratopathy.
side_effects: Eye discomfort, burning, redness, temporary blurred vision.
dosage: Apply as required.
precautions: Remove contact lens; do not touch the tip of the vial.

name: TRIAMCINOLONE
uses: Sympathetic ophthalmia, uveitis (unresponsive to steroids), hemangioma, chalazion, macular edema.
side_effects: Abnormal sensation, cataract, exophthalmos, glaucoma, increased IOP, vitreous detachment, secondary intraocular infection.
dosage: Injectable suspension 4 mg/0.05 ml or 4 mg/0.1 ml.
precautions: Prolonged use: subcapsular cataracts, glaucoma (optic nerve damage risk), secondary fungal/viral infections. Proper aseptic technique is mandatory.

name: CHLORAMPHENICOL
uses: Bacterial infection in otitis externa.
side_effects: Rash, headache.
dosage: Intra-aural: 2–3 drops in affected ear, 2–3 times a day. For maximum benefit, the patient should lie with the affected ear up for several minutes.
precautions: Avoid prolonged use.

name: CIPROFLOXACIN
uses: Bacterial infection in otitis externa.
side_effects: Local sensitivity.
dosage: Intra-aural: 2–3 drops in affected ear, 2 times a day for 7 days.
precautions: Concurrent tizanidine administration. Avoid prolonged use.

name: GENTAMICIN
uses: Chronic suppurative otitis media with perforated tympanic membranes.
side_effects: Local sensitivity.
dosage: Intra aural: 2–3 drops in the affected ear 4–5 times a day (including a dose at bedtime).
precautions: Avoid prolonged use to prevent aminoglycoside-induced ototoxicity.
contraindications: Patent grommet, perforated tympanic membrane (as a general rule for non-specialist use).

name: OFLOXACIN
uses: Chronic suppurative otitis media (CSOM) with perforated tympanic membranes, otitis externa.
side_effects: Local sensitivity, taste perversion, pruritus, dizziness, vertigo.
dosage: CSOM with perforated membranes: 10 drops 2 times a day in affected ear for 14 days. Otitis externa: 10 drops 2 times a day in the affected ear for 7 days.
precautions: Complete the full course of 14 days for CSOM even if symptoms resolve earlier.

name: CLOTRIMAZOLE
uses: Fungal infection in otitis externa.
side_effects: Local irritation, local sensitivity.
dosage: Intraaural: 2-3 drops in the affected ear 2–3 times a day; continue for at least 14 days after disappearance of infection.
precautions: Local irritation may occur.

name: CHLORAMPHENICOL WITH DEXAMETHASONE
uses: Chronic suppurative otitis media.
side_effects: Local irritation, steroid-related effects with prolonged use.
dosage: Intraaural: 2-3 drops in the affected ear 2-3 times a day for 7-10 days.
precautions: Limit duration to 10 days to avoid steroid side effects and resistance.
contraindications: Untreated viral, fungal, or tubercular infections.

name: ALMOND OIL
uses: Soften dry or hardened ear wax and for ear wax removal.
side_effects: N/A
dosage: Intraaural: Use 3-4 drops twice daily for 3-5 days. The patient should lie with the affected ear up for 5-10 minutes after the oil has been introduced.
precautions: Allow drops to warm to room temperature before use.

name: SODIUM BICARBONATE
uses: Soften dry or hardened ear wax and for ear wax removal.
side_effects: Dryness of the ear canal.
dosage: Intraaural: Use 3-4 drops twice daily for 3-5 days. Allow the solution to remain in the ear (patient lying with ear up) for 5-10 minutes.
precautions: N/A

name: ICHTHAMMOL IN GLYCERINE PACK
uses: Acute otitis externa, diffuse otitis externa.
side_effects: Local irritation.
dosage: Intraaural: Soaked thin ribbon gauge is to be placed in the ear canal for 24-48 hrs.
precautions: Use cautiously in pregnancy. Don’t use on broken skin.
contraindications: Allergic to glycerin or topical medicine.

name: AMOXICILLIN
uses: Systemic treatment for otitis media, sinusitis.
side_effects: Diarrhea, rash.
dosage: Oral, Child (1–11 months): 125 mg 3 times a day. Child (1–4 years): 250 mg 3 times a day. Child (5–11 years): 500 mg 3 times a day. 12 years and above: 500 mg 3 times a day. Dose can be increased up to 30 mg/kg or 1 g TID in severe infections.
precautions: Monitor for allergic reactions.

name: BETAHISTINE
uses: Ménière’s disease (Chronic stage vertigo).
side_effects: Gastrointestinal disturbances, headache, pruritus, rashes.
dosage: Oral, adult: Initially 16 mg 3 times daily, preferably with food; maintenance 24- 48 mg daily.
precautions: Use with caution in asthma or history of peptic ulcer. Not recommended in children.

name: CINNARIZINE
uses: Vestibular disorders (vertigo, tinnitus, nausea, vomiting) in Ménière’s disease, motion sickness.
side_effects: Drowsiness, paradoxical stimulation (children), angioedema, hypotension, lichen planus, lupus-like skin reactions.
dosage: Ménière’s: 12 years and above: 25 mg 3 times a day for 5-7 days. Motion sickness: child (5–11 yrs): 15 mg 2 hours before travel, then 7.5 mg every 8 hrs; 12 years and above: 30 mg 2 hours before travel, then 15 mg every 8 hrs.
precautions: Use with caution in renal impairment, epilepsy, glaucoma, Parkinson’s, and prostatic hypertrophy.
contraindications: Avoid in acute porphyria, neonates, and severe liver disease.

name: MUPIROCIN
uses: Eradication of nasal carriage of staphylococci, including MRSA.
side_effects: Local irritation.
dosage: Intranasal: 2–3 times a day for 5 days.
precautions: A sample should be taken 2 days after treatment to confirm eradication.

name: IPRATROPIUM BROMIDE
uses: Intrinsic rhinitis.
side_effects: Epistaxis, nasal dryness, pharyngitis (in children), headache, nausea.
dosage: Intranasal, >12yrs of age: 2 sprays, 2–3 times a day into each nostril.
precautions: Avoid spraying near eyes. Caution in bladder outflow obstruction, cystic fibrosis, and prostatic hyperplasia.

name: OXYMETAZOLINE
uses: Acute rhinitis.
side_effects: Local burning, sneezing; prolonged use: rebound congestion, tachycardia, arrhythmias, high BP.
dosage: Intranasal drop, adult (0.05%): 2-3 drops into each nostril 2-3 times daily (max 7 days). Child >3 months (0.025%): 1-2 drops into each nostril twice daily (max 7 days).
precautions: Hyperthyroidism, heart disease/hypertension, diabetes, children < 3 months, glaucoma, dysuria.

name: XYLOMETAZOLINE
uses: Nasal congestion.
side_effects: Local burning, rebound congestion, palpitations, arrhythmias.
dosage: Intranasal drop, adult (0.1%): 1-2 drops in each nostril, 1-2 times a day (max 7 days). Child >6 years (0.1%): 2–3 drops in each nostril, 2–3 times a day (max 7 days).
precautions: Use with caution in pregnancy, lactation, and elderly.

name: GLUCOSE IN GLYCERINE
uses: Atrophic rhinitis.
side_effects: N/A
dosage: Cotton swab dipped in glucose 25% in glycerine and apply in bilateral nasal cavity for 1 month twice daily; then continue once daily dosing for life or until underlying cause treated.
precautions: Ensure gentle application with cotton swabs.

name: CETIRIZINE
uses: Symptomatic treatment of allergic conditions related to ENT, urticaria, chronic idiopathic urticaria.
side_effects: Dry mouth, psychomotor impairment, urinary retention, blurred vision.
dosage: Oral, child (2-5 yrs): 2.5 mg twice daily. Child (6–11 yrs): 5 mg twice daily. 12 years and above: 10 mg once daily.
precautions: Use with caution in epilepsy. Renal impairment (GFR 30-50): use half dose. Renal impairment (GFR 10-30): use half dose every other day.

name: TRANEXAMIC ACID
uses: Epistaxis.
side_effects: See under Chapter 3 (Drugs Used in Blood).
dosage: Epistaxis: 1000-1500 mg every 8-12 hours for 10 days.
precautions: N/A

name: BENZALKONIUM CHLORIDE + CHOLINE SALICYLATE
uses: Aphthous ulcer, oral ulcers.
side_effects: Hypersensitivity reactions.
dosage: Local application, three times a day for 5 to 10 days.
precautions: N/A

name: CHLORHEXIDINE
uses: Aphthous ulcer, acute tonsillitis, oropharyngitis, tonsillar keratosis, gingivitis.
side_effects: Hypersensitivity reactions.
dosage: Gingivitis: oral rinse 15mL two times a day.
precautions: Do not use in patients who cannot gargle.

name: CHLORHEXIDINE + LIDOCAINE + METRONIDAZOLE
uses: Oral cavity laceration, aphthous ulcer, oral ulcers with high risk of infection (sutured wound).
side_effects: Hypersensitivity reaction.
dosage: Oral cavity lesion, local application, three times a day for 5-7 days.
precautions: N/A

name: HYDROGEN PEROXIDE
uses: Hemostasis in tonsillectomy, remove unhealthy slough from wounds.
side_effects: Erythema, stinging, edema, pruritus, vesiculation.
dosage: Oral gargle: diluted with water (10 mL in 1L of water), used 3-4 times a day. Unhealthy wound: diluted in povidone iodine (4-5 drops in 10mL 10% PI).
precautions: Should not be used in healthy tissue. Avoid exposure to eye.

name: NYSTATIN
uses: Oropharyngeal candidiasis.
side_effects: Irritation, sensitization (rash, urticaria, contact dermatitis).
dosage: Adult and child: swish and swallow, 4-6 mL, 5 times a day for minimum 7 days (or 2 days after symptoms improve). Infant: 1-2 mL local application 4 times daily.
precautions: Keep the suspension in the mouth for as long as possible before swallowing.

name: POVIDONE IODINE
uses: Oral ulcer, wound dressing.
side_effects: Hyperthyroidism, irritation, pruritus, rashes.
dosage: Oral ulcer: gargle, dilute with water and 3-4 times a day.
precautions: Cautious in children.
contraindications: Burn skin, renal impairment, thyroid disorders.

name: CEFDINIR
uses: Acute tonsillitis, acute oropharyngitis.
side_effects: Urticaria, skin rash.
dosage: Adult: 600 mg once a day or 300 mg twice a day for 10 days. Child: 14 mg/kg once daily for 10 days.
precautions: N/A

name: PENICILLIN V
uses: Tonsillitis and pharyngitis, quinsy (with metronidazole).
side_effects: Diarrhea, nausea, vomiting.
dosage: Adult (penicillin susceptible): 500 mg twice a day or 250 mg four times a day for 10 days. Child: 25-50 mg/kg/day divided q6h for 10 days.
precautions: Renal impairment.

name: VALACYCLOVIR
uses: Herpes labialis.
side_effects: Hypersensitivity reaction.
dosage: Oral: 2 grams twice a day for one day.
precautions: Ensure adequate hydration during treatment.

name: PANTOPRAZOLE
uses: Laryngopharyngeal reflux.
side_effects: N/A
dosage: Oral: 40 mg twice a day for 6 weeks with/without domperidone.
precautions: Take before meals.

name: ADRENALINE/EPINEPHRINE
uses: Anaphylaxis; As a vasoconstrictor for haemostasis.
side_effects: Vasoconstriction, tissue necrosis.
dosage: Adult: 0.3 mg IM up to 0.5 mg per dose as soon as anaphylactic shock occurs. May be repeated every 5-10 minutes (total 3 doses). Children: 0.01 mg/kg.
precautions: Do not administer repeated injections at the same site (risk of tissue necrosis). Inject IM or SC into the anterolateral aspect of the thigh.
contraindications: Do not use if the solution is colored, cloudy, or contains particulate matter.

name: SALBUTAMOL/ALBUTEROL
uses: Relief of bronchospasm during dental procedures in patients with reversible obstructive airway disease.
side_effects: Paradoxical bronchospasm (life-threatening).
dosage: 1-2 puffs per dose. For children 6 years of age and older.
precautions: Discontinue immediately if paradoxical bronchospasm occurs.

name: ASPIRIN
uses: Suspected myocardial infarction (MI) during dental treatment.
side_effects: N/A
dosage: Administer 1 to 4 tablets (chewed and swallowed) as soon as MI attack occurs.
precautions: Chew the tablet thoroughly before swallowing for faster absorption during an emergency.

name: GLUCAGON
uses: Treatment of hypoglycemic shock during dental procedures.
side_effects: N/A
dosage: Children (<20 kg): 0.5 mg IM, IV or SC. Adults and children (>20 kg): 1 mg IM, IV or SC. If weight unknown: children <6yrs: 0.5 mL; children 6yrs and older: 1 mL.
precautions: Use only if the person is unable to eat, is unconscious, or having a seizure. If conscious, oral glucose is preferred.
contraindications: Hypoglycemic patients experiencing starvation or adrenal insufficiency.

name: GLYCERYL TRINITRATE (GTN)
uses: Relief of chest pain associated with angina pectoris during dental treatment.
side_effects: Local burning or tingling sensation.
dosage: Place one sublingual tablet or 1-2 sprays under the tongue. May repeat at 5-minute intervals (total 3 doses).
precautions: If symptoms do not resolve after 3 doses, treat as acute MI.

name: MIDAZOLAM
uses: Status tonic-clonic seizures in patients undergoing dental treatment.
side_effects: Low blood pressure, respiratory depression.
dosage: Adults: 10 mg. Pediatric: 1-5 years: 5 mg; 5-10 years: 7.5 mg; >10 years: 10 mg.
precautions: Rapid IV injection in neonates can result in low blood pressure and seizures.

name: DIPHENHYDRAMINE
uses: Allergic reactions to materials or medications used during dental procedures; alternative anesthetic agent for 'caine' allergies.
side_effects: Greater perception of pain at injection site relative to 1% Lidocaine; risk of local tissue necrosis.
dosage: Oral: 25-50 mg q6-8h (max 300 mg/day). IV/IM: 10-50 mg (max 100 mg per dose) q4-6h (max 400 mg/day).
precautions: For local anesthesia, dilute 1 mL of 50 mg/mL with 4 mL of 0.9% NaCl to yield a 1% concentration.

name: AMOXICILLIN
uses: Standard general prophylaxis for endocarditis; Orodental infections; Actinomycosis; Maxillary sinusitis.
side_effects: GI disturbances.
dosage: General Prophylaxis: Adult 2 g; Child 50 mg/kg (single dose 30-60 min before procedure). Infection: Adult 250-500 mg TID; Child 20-40 mg/kg/day in 3 divided doses.
precautions: Caution in patients with chronic renal dysfunction.
contraindications: Allergy to β-lactam antibiotics (penicillins and cephalosporins).

name: CLINDAMYCIN
uses: Prophylaxis for patients allergic to penicillin; Systemic treatment of dental infections.
side_effects: Diarrhoea, colitis.
dosage: Oral Prophylaxis: Adult 600 mg; Child 20 mg/kg (30-60 min before procedure). Infection: Adult 150-300 mg 6 hourly; Child 3-6 mg/kg 6 hourly.
precautions: Inform doctor immediately if persistent diarrhea occurs.

name: TETRACYCLINE
uses: Aphthous ulcers; Periodontal diseases.
side_effects: Permanent tooth discoloration; diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, light-sensitive rashes, Benign Intracranial hypertension, Pancreatitis, Pseudomembranous colitis.
dosage: Adult: 1 g daily in 2-4 divided doses (max 2 g/day). Children: 20-40 mg/kg/day in 2-4 divided doses.
precautions: Deposits in teeth causing yellow discoloration; avoid in late pregnancy and young children.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to tetracycline; Renal failure; SLE; Pregnant women and nursing mothers; Children less than 8 years of age.

name: NYSTATIN
uses: Oral candidiasis (Oral thrush); Denture stomatitis; Candidal angular cheilitis.
side_effects: N/A
dosage: Thrush: Hold 5 ml (infant 2 ml) of suspension in oral cavity for several minutes 4 times daily before swallowing. Pastille: Dissolve slowly in mouth 5 times a day.
precautions: For denture stomatitis, may be used as a gel with 0.2% chlorhexidine.

name: ACYCLOVIR
uses: Cold sores (Herpes Simplex); oral lesions related to chicken pox and shingles.
side_effects: Stinging and burning sensation after application; mouth pain (buccal tablet).
dosage: 200 mg 5 times daily for 10 days. Recurrent prophylaxis: 400 mg twice daily for 10 days.
precautions: Should be administered within the first 72 hours of symptom onset.

name: POTASSIUM NITRATE
uses: Dentinal hypersensitivity.
side_effects: Vertigo, headache, hypotension, convulsions, cyanosis, methemoglobinemia.
dosage: Apply as directed by a dentist; do not use longer than 4 weeks without consultation.
precautions: Use cautiously in case of pregnancy or lactation. Pre-existing diseases should be ruled out.

name: GLUTARALDEHYDE
uses: Symptomatic relief from dentinal hypersensitivity; Disinfectant.
side_effects: Headache, nausea, rashes, brownish discolouration of skin, asthma, eye irritation.
dosage: Blot area dry; apply with cotton pellet or applicator tip by rubbing for 30 seconds and dry thoroughly.
precautions: Should not be given to neonates. Wearing respirators and protective clothing is mandatory when handling.

name: SILVER NITRATE
uses: Desensitizing agent; Caries control; Healing oral ulcers; Astringent/Hemostatic; Disinfectant.
side_effects: Dark purple or brown staining of skin; burns; argyria (blue-gray skin color) with long-term exposure.
dosage: Apply a cotton applicator dipped in solution to the affected area 2-3 times/week for 2-3 weeks.
precautions: Patients and staff must wear eye protection and masks. Reacts rapidly with chloride to precipitate silver chloride.

name: SODIUM FLUORIDE
uses: Caries prevention; Dentinal hypersensitivity.
side_effects: Rashes, itching, difficulty breathing, chest tightness, swelling of mouth/face.
dosage: In-office: Four-visit procedure at intervals of approximately one week. NaF recommended at ages 3, 7, 11, and 13.
precautions: Do not use if drinking water fluoride >0.6ppm. No more than 2g of gel per tray (40% capacity).
contraindications: Children unable to expectorate; Infants younger than 6 months.

name: CHLORHEXIDINE
uses: Anti-plaque; Initial periodontal therapy; Postsurgical oral hygiene; Gingival enlargements; Post-extraction bacteremia prevention.
side_effects: Extrinsic brown staining of teeth and restorations; impaired taste sensation; dryness and soreness of mucosa; painful desquamative lesions.
dosage: Rinse with 10ml of 0.2% mouthwash twice daily for 2 weeks.
precautions: Do not add water to the rinse. Do not swallow. Categorised under Category B and C for pregnancy.
contraindications: Not usually indicated for patients under 18 years; Allergic to Chlorhexidine.

name: DOXYCYCLINE HYCLATE (SDD)
uses: Adjunct to scaling and root planing (SRP) for chronic or aggressive periodontitis.
side_effects: Generally well tolerated.
dosage: 20 mg taken twice a day for 3 months (maximum 9 months).
precautions: Should not be used as a stand-alone therapy. Prescribe to coincide with first episode of SRP.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to tetracyclines; Pregnancy and lactation; Children < 12 years.
interactions: Reduces efficacy of oral contraceptive pills.

name: GELFOAM
uses: Control of minor bleeding in oral and dental surgery.
side_effects: Giant cell granuloma, hematoma formation, toxic shock syndrome, failure of absorption.
dosage: Place dry or moistened rolled pack into the cavity/socket. Apply light finger pressure for 1-2 minutes.
precautions: Not recommended in presence of frank infection. Avoid over-packing as it expands when fluid is absorbed.
contraindications: Closure of skin incisions (interferes with healing); Allergy to porcine collagen.

name: BONE WAX
uses: Local hemostasis of bone (tamponade) in visualized vascular channels ('bone bleeders').
side_effects: Mild inflammatory reactions; may enhance existing infection; inhibits osteogenesis.
dosage: Warm to desired consistency and apply to bone edges.
precautions: Use sparingly. Do not manipulate with latex gloves (latex proteins may cause allergic reaction). Do not resterilize.
contraindications: Procedures where rapid osseous regeneration and fusion are desired.

name: TRANEXAMIC ACID
uses: Dental extractions in patients with hemophilia to reduce hemorrhage.
side_effects: Nausea, diarrhoea, headache, giddiness, thrombophlebitis of injected veins, convulsions.
dosage: 10 mg/kg IV repeated every 4-6 hourly for 2-8 days.
precautions: Reduce dose in renal insufficiency. Caution in upper urinary tract bleeding.
contraindications: Active intravascular clotting; acquired defective colour vision; hypersensitivity.

name: PILOCARPINE
uses: Treatment of dry mouth (xerostomia) secondary to drug/radiation induction or Sjogren’s syndrome.
side_effects: Sweating, nausea, flushing, rhinitis, increased salivation, tachycardia, taste perversion.
dosage: Adult: Initially 2.5 mg to 5 mg TID. Titration up to 30 mg per day at variable intervals.
precautions: Caution in cholelithiasis or biliary tract disease. Monitor in renal/liver impairment.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity; uncontrolled asthma; cardiovascular diseases; narrow angle glaucoma.

name: TACROLIMUS
uses: Autoimmune mucosal lesions; vesiculobullous lesions; second-line therapy for moderate to severe atopic dermatitis.
side_effects: Application-site infections, burning, stinging, rash.
dosage: Apply topically morning and evening twice daily as a thin layer to affected areas.
precautions: Avoid UV light/sunlight. Avoid contact with eyes and mucous membranes.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity; long-term use (risk of lymphoma/skin malignancy).
